description: Another song inspired by my favorite dead daddy, Bertrand Russel, asking a fair, timeless question:  “Has Religion Contributed Anything Useful to Civilization?”  This EPx24 is volume 2 of this song & flows BLUES (1), FOLK (2-7), DUB (8-12), LOFI (13-15), INDIE (16-24)  — @bananasutra #songlyrics  [Verse 1] I walked down the path of righteous men, But I never found the proof they promised then, Said faith is the answer, you gotta believe, But what kind of truth is a web that deceives?  [Chorus] I ain’t no Christian, ain’t no holy fool, I keep my questions sharp, keep my thinking cool, No man in the clouds gonna govern my mind, In the light of reason, real freedom I find.  [Verse 2] They say without a book, there’s no morality, But my heart’s been kind without theology. I don’t need a heaven, I don’t fear no hell, For the love of humanity, my spirit will swell.  [Chorus] I ain’t no Christian, ain’t no savior’s pawn, Ain’t no miracles needed, I’ll keep pressing on. A life of free thought is where I belong, The blues of the soul keep my mind strong.  [Bridge] Why follow blind faith when we can see, The logic, the science, the philosophy? Oh, the universe ain’t got no plan, Just a cosmic dance, that’s where I stand.  [Outro] I ain’t no Christian, I ain’t shackled down, In a world of wonder, I ain’t bound to a crown. Let the truth roll in like a morning breeze, In reason’s embrace, I live with ease.  — For the curious: here's I Ain't No Christian (No Holy Fool) Volume 1: https://soundcloud.com/bananasutra/sets/i-aint-no-christian-no-holy-fool-epx4-vol02

description: Another song inspired by my favorite dead daddy, Bertrand Russel, asking a fair, timeless question:  “Has Religion Contributed Anything Useful to Civilization?”  This EPx24 is volume 2 of this song & flows BLUES (1), FOLK (2-7), DUB (8-12), LOFI (13-15), INDIE (16-24)  — @bananasutra #songlyrics  [Verse 1] I walked down the path of righteous men, But I never found the proof they promised then, Said faith is the answer, you gotta believe, But what kind of truth is a web that deceives?  [Chorus] I ain’t no Christian, ain’t no holy fool, I keep my questions sharp, keep my thinking cool, No man in the clouds gonna govern my mind, In the light of reason, real freedom I find.  [Verse 2] They say without a book, there’s no morality, But my heart’s been kind without theology. I don’t need a heaven, I don’t fear no hell, For the love of humanity, my spirit will swell.  [Chorus] I ain’t no Christian, ain’t no savior’s pawn, Ain’t no miracles needed, I’ll keep pressing on. A life of free thought is where I belong, The blues of the soul keep my mind strong.  [Bridge] Why follow blind faith when we can see, The logic, the science, the philosophy? Oh, the universe ain’t got no plan, Just a cosmic dance, that’s where I stand.  [Outro] I ain’t no Christian, I ain’t shackled down, In a world of wonder, I ain’t bound to a crown. Let the truth roll in like a morning breeze, In reason’s embrace, I live with ease.  — For the curious: here's I Ain't No Christian (No Holy Fool) Volume 1: https://soundcloud.com/bananasutra/sets/i-aint-no-christian-no-holy-fool-epx4-vol02

description: This is volume 2 of that song, which is a bit of a bananasutra anthem—except it's not patriotic, nor euphoric, not even psychedelic... it's just a slow, humble, heartfelt FLOWsutra breathing meditation lullaby, to help me (and maybe you) find #peace beyond the loud ambient #whitenoise of all the nonsense surrounding us.   ❥  ❥  ❥  @bananasutra #songlyrics:  [Intro] Just breathe, in sync, in flow…  [Verse 1] Making songs like others meditate, flex, or pray, I’m not chasing a corporate crown today, Don’t need algorithms to write my verse, My ego ain’t rehearsing for a popularity curse.  [Chorus] Only here to wonder, to learn, and share. Each song’s a little atheist prayer. In a world gone bananas, I hum for peace, Singing truths that refuse to cease.  [Verse 2] Raised atheist, humble but bold, Turning fears and hopes into stories told. Humming for justice, connecting the dots, Silly as it sounds, it’s all I’ve got.  [Chorus] Only here to wonder, to learn, and share, Each song’s a little atheist prayer. In a world gone bananas, I hum for peace Singing truths that refuse to cease.  [Outro] Music therapy, poetic play... Just a fool on a path, finding my way.   ❥  ❥  ❥   See also: Vol. 01, a dubby trippy hop hop dub gem @  https://soundcloud.com/bananasutra/making-songs-like-others  Learn more on bananasutra.com

description: Wrote this one in what felt like just one long holding of my breath, pondering how we got there—bullshitting, blames holding, trust failing. Culture wars, consuming, exonyms. Hopes sunken. Sweet heavens. So broken. Blessed be Björk, not fearing, not fading, still singing....  EPx26 is like a longer deeper breath... it flows JAZZ (1-9), INDIE (10-13), DUB (14-19), BLUES (20-26).  ⭐︎ ⭐︎ ⭐︎ @bananasutra #songlyrics  [Verse] So woken, It’s burning, Keeps turning, Gone rotten…  Here I go, So hoping We see them Fading flames With no names  So woken. Still breathing. So woken. Still singing.  Oh-see… Hmm… ooh, no…  [Verse] Here we are, Trust failing  Culture wars Consuming  Forgetting The future Lost laughter Woes wander  So woken. Still breathing. So woken. Still hoping.  Oh-see… Hmm… ooh, no.  [Bridge] Please tell me… Can peace Forget Justice?  Can love Grow Without Truth?  Oh no… But(t) still, I sing.  [Verse] Infinite Colors. Fuck finite Players   Broken soul Holy fool Fear blows cold. Love flows bold.  So woken. Still caring. So woken. Still praying.  Oh-see… Oh oui…  [Outro] In truth We grow. In justice We flow. For children To glow…  Peace On Earth Sweet home.  So broken. So woken.  We sing.

description: This is a KNOWsutra (Peace Not War) song I wrote upon one sleepless night, with a profoundly befuddled heart. It's a letter to a dead man I thought I knew well, but(t) I did not—one wickedly coercive soul, who chose to BLOW blow blow, rather than GROW, FLOW, GLOW, and BOW... A covertly sly, insane finite player who somehow thought it best to choose ego over letting go, fear over humility, violence over honesty, vengeance over empathy, darkness over transparency, lies over trust, war over peace, and ultimately, literally, death over life.  EPx17 is really just one whale wailing questions in the void of love gone hate, a peace mantra prayer of sorts, a piano-cello-accordion trance indie soul track musically inspired by Alicia Keys' song “Fallin'”; and, it is dedicated to the 3 daughters his bloody mad stupid choices left orphans 💔  ⭐︎ ⭐︎ ⭐︎ @bananasutra #songlyrics  [Verse 1] Can we talk of what we know, Maybe don’t know, I wanna know. Like everything, like all the time, The reasons, the rhythms, the riddles, the rhymes.  Because I care to understand, Who we are and where we stand. What shadows show, how humans grow, What seeds we blow, where kids’ dreams flow.  [Chorus] I wanna know. Can we talk? I gotta ask. What is the task?  Do you know? Do you care? Why the despair? Why go so low? I wanna know.  [Verse 2] I wanna know about predators, Why greed galore, why no candor. I have questions, and marks that rhyme, To tale the tale, to trace the crime.  Shared history. Shared memory. Truth and peace, I pray each day. For pride to drop, for hearts to soften, For fear to finally fade away.  Imagine grace. Imagine glow. Beyond glory, higher than low Integrity that wears no crown, A human heart completely known.  [Chorus] I wanna know. Can we talk? I gotta ask. What is the task?  Do you know? Do you care? Why the despair? Why go so low? I wanna know.  [Verse 3] How can we know all of the facts, Made of bullshit, shit magic acts. Say no to blow. And let us grow. So we all know when to say no.  Oh, I wanna know why truth still hides. Why fear still feeds on wounded sides. Why war? Why woes? Why pain? Why lies? Why do children pay the price?  Bananasutra asks: Has the world’s gone bananas? When do we split? When do we stand? Why not reach with open hands?  [Final Chorus] Oh God, oh nos... Who knows? Why? Why? Who cares?  Can we talk? I wanna know. How do we grow? I wanna know.  [Outro] To know. To blow. To show. To grow. To flow. To glow. To bow.  To know what is humane. To show what is hidden. To grow beyond grievance. To bow ’till we all dance.  ∞

Because I care to dare wonder how we ALL can help create a more inclusive, peaceful future, for everyone, together—beyond chains of fools, beyond colors, genders, grifters, and the relative morality of all righteous fauXist bullshitters out there. Because daring to listen to each other is the very least we can do, in the name of justice and peace. Because like Bertrand Russel almost said, we all ought to get the facts right, and keep love in sight.  ⭐︎ ⭐︎ ⭐︎ @bananasutra #songlyrics Blessed be your voice, let it rise, Ain’t no chains to hold what’s wise, The power’s in the truth you sing, Let your words fly on free wings.  Blessed be your voice, let it break the silence, In a world that’s hard, we need no compliance. Raise it high, let the truth unfold, Respect your voice, it’s purest gold.  Don’t you know, silence is their tool, They’ll try to keep you quiet, play the fool. But in every breath you take, you’ll find, Power in the words that speak your mind.  Blessed be your voice, let it break the silence, In a world that’s hard, we need no compliance. Raise it high, let the truth unfold, Respect your voice, it’s purest gold.  In the silence, war will grow, When words fail us, don’t you know, It’s the battle for your soul, So, speak up loud, make yourself whole.  Blessed be your voice, let it break the silence, In a world that’s hard, we need no compliance. Raise it high, let the truth unfold, Respect your voice, it’s purest gold.  ⭐︎ ⭐︎ ⭐︎ (*) In French, Fraternity does not refer to a drunken male society... it simply means the people must unite in the name of democracy.  Original ROCKsutra single, released on Jan 26, 2025:  https://soundcloud.com/bananasutra/blessed-be-your-voice-rocksutra  Learn more on https://bananasutra.com/ 🍌💦

description: Drop the weight. Lightly, lightly, my darling... This one's a psychedelic ambient reggae-dub mantra lullaby, for when the soul grips too tight.  ✦ ✦ ✦ “Drop Di Baggage” is the sister song of “Lightly, My Darling”(*) and a quintessential FLOWsutra song, inspired by Sir Aldous Huxley, and meant to help me (and maybe you) balance out all that freaking BLOWs out there, with the magic of music—psychedelick ragga mama vibrations style.  Here’s the quote (because quotes matter, and this one’s yummy, darling): "It's dark because you are trying too hard. Lightly child, lightly. Learn to do everything lightly. Yes, feel lightly even though you're feeling deeply. Just lightly let things happen and lightly cope with them. I was so preposterously serious in those days...Lightly, lightly - it's the best advice ever given me...to throw away your baggage and go forward. There are quicksands all about you, sucking at your feet, trying to suck you down into fear and self-pity and despair. That's why you must walk so lightly. Lightly, my darling..." —Aldous Huxley  ✦ ✦ ✦ [Intro] Lightly… lightly… (…lightly… lightly…) Too much weight pon di soul, yeah… Bananasutra vibration… drift now…  [Verse 1] Step weh yuh take, yeah it sink inna sand Quicksand mind, try fi pull yuh down man Grip too tight, now yuh lose command Life get cold when yuh overstand  Ease up now, no fight di breeze Universe move inna slow degrees Yuh nah alone inna dem unease Just let go… exhale… release…  [Pre-Chorus] Why yuh hold so hard, my friend? When di river just a twist and bend… Feel it deep but don’t pretend— Every weight got time fi end…  [Chorus] It’s dark ‘cause yuh try too much (too much… too much…) Loosen up, don’t grip so clutch Lightly now, no rush, no rush Drop di baggage, float and touch  Sky open when yuh step so light Echo fade inna velvet night Darling breathe, it all alright Drift… drift… into di light…  [Verse 2] Feel it deep but glide pon top Heartbeat sync wid di dub bass drop World spin wild but yuh don’t stop Float like smoke from a rooftop  Inna di moment, no control Let it pass through body and soul Wind nah show but it play its role Invisible hands make broken whole  [Bridge] Dem fears? Yeah, dem whisper low… (whisper low… whisper low…) Try fi drag yuh down below…  But walk like air beneath yuh feet No resistance, just retreat From di noise to something sweet, Where surrender and rhythm meet…  [Chorus] It’s dark ‘cause yuh try too much (try too much… try too much…) Ease yuh grip, don’t hold so clutch Lightly now, no rush, no rush Let it fall with a gentle touch  Sky open when yuh step so light Echo fade inna velvet night Darling breathe, it all alright Drift… drift… into di light…  [Outro] Lightly… my darling… lightly… (…lightly… lightly…) Throw it down… no carry… No fear… no worry…  Walk so light… you barely there… Just a whisper inna di air… Bananasutra… everywhere… Float… float… disappear…  ✦ ✦ ✦ * "Lightly, My Darling" FOLK dream: https://soundcloud.com/bananasutra/sets/lightly-my-darling-banjo-flowsutra-epx5

This one's a psychedelic ambient reggae-dub mantra lullaby, for when the soul grips too tight.  ✦ ✦ ✦ “Drop Di Baggage” is the sister song of “Lightly, My Darling”(*) and a quintessential FLOWsutra song, inspired by Sir Aldous Huxley, and meant to help me (and maybe you) balance out all that freaking BLOWs out there, with the magic of music—psychedelick ragga mama vibrations style.  Here’s the quote (because quotes matter, and this one’s yummy, darling): "It's dark because you are trying too hard. Lightly child, lightly. Learn to do everything lightly. Yes, feel lightly even though you're feeling deeply. Just lightly let things happen and lightly cope with them. I was so preposterously serious in those days...Lightly, lightly - it's the best advice ever given me...to throw away your baggage and go forward. There are quicksands all about you, sucking at your feet, trying to suck you down into fear and self-pity and despair. That's why you must walk so lightly. Lightly, my darling..." —Aldous Huxley  ✦ ✦ ✦ [Intro] Lightly… lightly… (…lightly… lightly…) Too much weight pon di soul, yeah… Bananasutra vibration… drift now…  [Verse 1] Step weh yuh take, yeah it sink inna sand Quicksand mind, try fi pull yuh down man Grip too tight, now yuh lose command Life get cold when yuh overstand  Ease up now, no fight di breeze Universe move inna slow degrees Yuh nah alone inna dem unease Just let go… exhale… release…  [Pre-Chorus] Why yuh hold so hard, my friend? Yeah, dem whisper low… (whisper low… whisper low…) Try fi drag yuh down below…  But walk like air beneath yuh feet No resistance, just retreat From di noise to something sweet, Where surrender and rhythm meet…  [Chorus] It’s dark ‘cause yuh try too much (try too much… try too much…) Ease yuh grip, don’t hold so clutch Lightly now, no rush, no rush Let it fall with a gentle touch  Sky open when yuh step so light Echo fade inna velvet night Darling breathe, it all alright Drift… drift… into di light…  [Outro] Lightly… my darling… lightly… (…lightly… lightly…) Throw it down… no carry… No fear… no worry…  Walk so light… you barely there… Just a whisper inna di air… Bananasutra… everywhere… Float… float… disappear…  ✦ ✦ ✦ * "Lightly, My Darling" FOLK dream: https://soundcloud.com/bananasutra/sets/lightly-my-darling-banjo-flowsutra-epx5

description: How, bro?  @bananasutra #songlyrics How is power still an issue of genders? Why is color still a matter of favors? Who knows where sorrow lingered longer? (Harder, darker) Are egos bros drunk on power, ever sober, do they ever grow kinder?  Yeah, no need to answer, to be fair… Everybody knows trust matters like psychological safety is air Everybody knows trump’s a mad joker, a serial killer of what is fair Equality knows bully winners couldn’t care less what it means to be fair Equality gone, bipartisanship spreading bias like they’re not even aware Like no one even cares, about double standards, felons, jerks, now it’s blessed be the pathological liars!  Like, wow. I mean, How is that safe or fair? I mean quack, look at that evil freaks faire ?! Are they just too busy to care Maybe too selfish to share Too cowardly to dare To fight for what is fair To tell the truth, to take the pis, To Remember what matter, like huh peace? (Peeeeace, oh brother!)  Don’t wanna be too simplistic, Game theory’s no vain dialectic, Playing fair is a matter of logic, That is why liars relish rhetoric.  They’ll Murky the waters to make it seem deep, Twats wannabe winners no matter what the bleep  I know, tho… so I’ll share right now Everybody knows kind loving humans glow, And coucous birds Blow, always breaking the flow, stealing the show, in a weird orange glow, Everybody knows Envy-driven “winners” are scary egos monsters who just gonna BLOW (blow, blow, blow) (low, low, and low-errrr)  So huh, excuse me sir, but(t) now what? Finding some true win wins or what? Your dozen kids, they hope for what?  Dolon Trusk, the new Shining twin plight Egos Gone Quack, no win-win in sight None, Billions hoarding turds acting like truth and hope are for losers and they dunno the difference between savior and monster —- as if biased bull babbles didn’t end up in sum’s zero  Well Shit… bravo <3  Reckless heartless greedy monsters Needy losers toddlers never learned to share  (Mwahahahahahaha)  Just kidding… I’m not laughing the truth is, I’ve been crying Just trying to make sense of this strange reality Can’t trust the Trusk, and why you gods let it be, all that cruelty Can’t you see the danger looming is sheer stupidity Sick Morons decrees, bye bye equality, hello poverty, it’s like a new pandemic, with higher rates of mortality—BECAUSE, jerks wanking in the glory of shameless STUPIDITY

[Verse 1] A soul with quirky charm, No need to raise alarm, Her words just slip and fall, A circus for you all, Please pardon my French.  [Chorus] She’s weird, she knows, But the language flows, Her phrases whirl and spin, Like croissants made of sin, Please pardon my French.  [Verse 2] She mimes with wild delight, Gestures through the night, Words like "crouton", “baguette,” Leave her audience perplexed, Please pardon my French.  [Chorus] She’s odd, she’s proud, Her quirks speak loud, In every twist and lunge, She’s a rogue with a hunch, Please pardon my French.  [Bridge] C’est la vie, mon ami, She’ll say it with glee, In a trance, her tongue just spins, Bienvenue, the silliness begins!  [Verse 3] So next time she says “bonjour,” And you’re unsure what’s in store, Just smile and let it go, It’s a goofy little show, Please pardon her French.  [Outro] Please pardon my French, It’s an odd but grand descent, With baguettes in her hand, Like it's a magic wand, Please pardon my French.  😘🥖

description: This one started like this:  In our dystopian world, where corporate media feeds control people’s attention spans and serial predators seized post-constitutional power, people are so proud, so loud, so shroud, everywhere, comme une guerre... Humans buzzing around, all increasingly poor or rich and unemployed, fending for fame, naming ‘em names, shaming with blames, playing lame lose-lose games, while feeling less and less humane.  So much radio static… Extroverts gone manic. Meek heroes turned tragic. The Sad, the Mad, and the Bad! It all rhymes, aren’t you just glad?!  Bananasutra Radio Philosophy à Gogo 💨  ⭐︎⭐︎⭐︎  @bananasutra #songlyrics   [Intro] Shhh… tune in. Frequency of the free and the flawed. Where logic sings lunacy, And truth gets the last laugh.  [Verse 1] In our dystopian cabaret, The clowns wear crowns, the saints get down. Sinners confess, big hearts decay… It’s real surrealité.  The rich feel poor in peace of mind, The poor feel rich in borrowed time, We trade our trust for stolen lines, And laugh it’s all gonna be fine,  [Pre-Chorus] Attention spans in flames, Empathy’s the rarest game, So we joke, we woke, name names, Then feel a little less humane.  [Chorus] So much radio static! Extroverts gone manic, Meek heroes turned tragic, The Sad, the Mad, the Bad! It all rhymes—aren’t you just glad?  Bananasutra Radio! Philosophy à Gogo, Not for profit, not for show, Just the joy of knowing what we know.  [Bridge] Between the buzz and the bling, You might hear something true sing. Frequency clear through the noise, Like conscience finding its voice.  The tired, wired, half-awake, Still dream, still dance, still make... Through static, chaos, clickbait rain, Let’s hum our way back to sane.  [Final Chorus] So much radio static! Extroverts gone manic! The meek and the magic, Still laughing through the tragic!  Bananasutra Radio Where wonder breaks the algorithm’s hold, And every soul, young or old, Tells truth like it’s made of gold.  [Outro] Signal fading, Spirit staying. Tune in again… Blessed be mayhem   #ahem 🤡

tags: growsutra, idiot, compassion, empathy, gipsy, peace, fusion music, prayer
description: This is a GROWsutra (Kindness) song that started as a comment on a meme about “Idiot Compassion”. It is dedicated to people who believe empathy is essentially a “performative” thing… simply because they can’t feel any, but(t) for themselves.   🌼 🌼 🌼 My original comment:  But who are the idiots lacking mindfulness really? The ones who care to ask, imagine, and relate, in an attempt to understand? Or, the ones who mock or shame them?  What I've observed is that those who frame compassion as manipulative also seem unable to imagine a version of compassion that isn’t about dominance... And that, to me, very much feels like cynical projection. Arguing that putting yourself in someone else’s shoes is essentially self-serving and deluded is very much a narcissistic worldview, a dark, flawed projection, by someone who simply, sadly cannot empathize.  In my divine book of joyful wisdom, what’s idiotic (and weak, and dangerous even) is interpreting curiosity, humility, openness, and tenderness as an hypocritical / tactical power exchange move motivated by a need for control, rather than a desire to connect and understand. Healthy empathy requires both mindfulness and imagination. And, I feel strongly that compassion is (by far) humanity's best line of defense against the global rise of fascism.  Real compassion ain’t dumb, it is brave. And it’s the best goddamn weapon the people got, to lead a peace rebellion.   🌼 🌼 🌼 And, the @bananasutra #songlyrics it became:  [Verse 1] Please tell me, my dear, who’s the fool in this affair? The one leaning in closer just to truly hear?  The one taking time to decode someone’s pain? Or the one throwing shade ’cause the truth bends their frame?  Who hides from the mirror, dodging their own glare? Who calls love “a weakness” ’cause they’re naked under there?  [Pre-Chorus] There’s a chant on the timeline: “Empathy is weak,” they speak, like compassion’s some disaster that’ll crack them in a week.  But if your own reflection cuts too sharp to stare, you call honesty a trap and torch what you can’t repair.  [Chorus] Real compassion isn’t frail, it illuminates the night. Not a failure, not a fairytale, just the discipline of light.  It’s the strength to stay steady when a story starts to tear; no pretending, no performance, just the quiet will to care.  [Verse 2] Funny how the cynics swear that tenderness is “bait,” a ploy, a polished tactic, some seductive sugar-gate.  But hearts afraid of contact fear the feelings they can’t feel, so they label trust “delusion” ’cause they doubt that love is real.  Ask them softly, Bananasutra: “Is it truth you fear… or proof?” Watch the armor split and shimmer like an old forgotten youth.  [Pre-Chorus] They say open hearts will “break you,” curiosity will “fail,” mindful listening is “naïve,” warmth is “cheap and just for sale.”  But a lie screamed repeatedly starts dressing up as “true,” ’til the echo chambers tremble ’cause they’ve drowned out something new.  [Chorus] Real compassion has a spine soft enough for fears to land; it can bend, it can align, it can gently guide a hand.  It’s a practice of attention that rejects the slow despair, the foundation of connection in a world too numb to care.  [Bridge] Step into another’s sky, not to fix, not to sway, just to widen your horizon in a humble human way.  Peace grows out of trust, and trust grows out of care; and the bravest kind of mercy is the mercy that stays there.  [Final Chorus] Real compassion isn’t soft, it’s an odyssey of heart. It’s the bravery to feel what could pull a world apart.  Call it foolish, call it foreign, still the strongest force we share; nothing’s more rebellious than the courage to care.  [Outro] Let them chant their tired slogans, we don’t borrow secondhand fear. Compassion isn’t weakness; it’s the brightest way to hear.  It’s the method, it’s the mirror, it’s the long, unbroken stare of a world that heals itself through the courage to care.  🕊️

[Bridge (KNOW + GROW + FLOW + GLOWsutra)] Entre nihilisme et illusion, J’choisis l’absurde en révolution. Le nihilisme abandonne, L’absurde, lui, me façonne. description: "No, I'm Not Being Political" is a true KNOW/QUACK/BLOWsutra story of apes gone wrong. It's inspired by an IRL chat I had with an older African American man walking his adorable dog, on a beautiful foggy summer day at Fort Funston, California... and whose only response to my humanist spill about the dangers of neofasc!sm in Murica was to smirk, and say "Oh, so you're political?" 😏  And, it just broke my heart... Because, if a human who directly lived and endured lawfool racism for over 60 years won't care enough to feel outraged by the normalization of evil, well, no wonder most people I know seem to prefer playing dead possum scrotum (*) in the face of cruelty heh 💔  This is Volume 2 of that song, a 2026 remake of the original, updated for current events.... now that the Big Beautiful Bill made Orwell's dystopian propaganda tales truer than ever, and now that daring to be #antifa or a woman suffering a miscarriage can get you condemned for being a "domestic terrorists" and "murderer" (sic), respectively, and now that congress clearly lost their balls, and is completely useless, even to stop illegal wars killing real people, for example 💣  Because, guess what (history taught us)? When fasc!sts rule , it never "gets better"... until someone freaking dares to care #goddamnit #revoltnow 🕊️ so, no, I'm not being political, I just care when power’s lethal  🏴‍☠️  ⚉ ⚉ ⚉  @bananasutra #songlyrics Edit, CIRCA 2026  [Intro] You may think I’m emotional, But I’m just awake, and real. This ain’t business as usual, It’s history gone surreal.  [Verse 1] This ain’t sliding, this is exploding, White men wanking, power brokering, Acting like cruelty brings them glory, Like democracy’s just a dumb story.  They renamed defense to war, oh yeah, No Congress vote, just bomb the way, Two funded wars we never chose, While they demand we never oppose.  [Verse 2] The “Beautiful Bill” is finally here, Millions lose health, live in fear, While “SAVE” acts strip the right to vote, Women are silenced at the throat.  Say “Antifa,” now it’s a crime, Free speech buried on our dime, If you think this is debate or fate, You’re sleeping at the gallows gate.  [Chorus] No, I’m not being political, Just a conscious, caring gal. No one needs to be spiritual To know this isn’t right at all.  Fascism ain’t some abstract inanity, It’s violence dressed up as banality, Human rights aren’t culture war decor, Wake up, people, this is so much more.  [Verse 3] You shrug as doctors haul away Bleeding mothers, grief judged foul play, They call it “murder” when bellies fail, Then lock up women inside a jail.  You say “I don’t do politics” with a grin, Like indifference isn’t a sin, But tolerance of evil helps it thrive, Just ask the ghosts who stayed alive…  [Bridge] I’m not especially radical, Hell, I’m barely social, I’m just partial to what’s ethical,  I’m just aware of what’s brutal.   Evil isn’t just conceptual, It’s become normal, habitual, I don’t march like it’s ritual, I just care when power’s lethal.  [Chorus] No, I’m not being political, Just a conscious, caring gal. No one needs to be spiritual To know this isn’t right at all.  Are you under some kind of spell? But(t) how can you not cry or yell? I’d rather feel it, heed the sting, Than hide behind not noticing.  [Outro] I don’t sing to play a role, I just can’t ignore the toll, Silence isn’t self-control, It’s surrender of the soul.  “I’m not political” you say, Like that keeps the dark away, But let’s not forget “never again”… Or it won’t get better in the end.  ⚉ ⚉ ⚉   Still here? Yay :) If you're curious, thank you for caring... here's the original (circa 2025) version of that song--same fasc!st regime, slightly less hardcore, because (you know?) that's how normalization of evil 101 works... It creeps on ya #boo https://soundcloud.com/bananasutra/sets/no-im-not-being-political-knowsutra-indie-dub-epx15  (*) "Possum Scrotum" song coming soon ;)

They renamed defense to war, oh yeah, No Congress vote, just bomb the way, Two funded wars we never chose, While they demand we never oppose.  [Verse 2] The “Beautiful Bill” is finally here, Millions lose health, live in fear, While “SAVE” acts strip the right to vote, Women are silenced at the throat.  Say “Antifa,” now it’s a crime, Free speech buried on our dime, If you think this is debate or fate, You’re sleeping at the gallows gate.  [Chorus] No, I’m not being political, Just a conscious, caring gal. No one needs to be spiritual To know this isn’t right at all.  Fascism ain’t some abstract inanity, It’s violence dressed up as banality, Human rights aren’t culture war decor, Wake up, people, this is so much more.  [Verse 3] You shrug as doctors haul away Bleeding mothers, grief judged foul play, They call it “murder” when bellies fail, Then lock up women inside a jail.  You say “I don’t do politics” with a grin, Like indifference isn’t a sin, But tolerance of evil helps it thrive, Just ask the ghosts who stayed alive…  [Bridge] I’m not especially radical, Hell, I’m barely social, I’m just partial to what’s ethical,  I’m just aware of what’s brutal.   Evil isn’t just conceptual, It’s become normal, habitual, I don’t march like it’s ritual, I just care when power’s lethal.  [Chorus] No, I’m not being political, Just a conscious, caring gal. No one needs to be spiritual To know this isn’t right at all.  Are you under some kind of spell? But(t) how can you not cry or yell? I’d rather feel it, heed the sting, Than hide behind not noticing.  [Outro] I don’t sing to play a role, I just can’t ignore the toll, Silence isn’t self-control, It’s surrender of the soul.  “I’m not political” you say, Like that keeps the dark away, But let’s not forget “never again”… Or it won’t get better in the end.  ⚉ ⚉ ⚉   Still here? description: “Lightly, My Darling” is the sister song of “Too Hard, (My Friend)”(*) and a quintessential intimate late night FLOWsutra song, inspired by Sir Aldous Huxley. It's meant to help me (and maybe you?) trust the love and light in my heart can balance out all the freaking violence and ignorance out there (you know?), all the maddening but(t) happening dark shite that BLOWs IRL, with the magic of music—psychedelic bluesy banjo folk french vocal jazz rêverie dream style...  Here’s the quote (because quotes matter, darling, and this one’s truly yummy): "It's dark because you are trying too hard. Lightly child, lightly. Learn to do everything lightly. Yes, feel lightly even though you're feeling deeply. Just lightly let things happen and lightly cope with them. I was so preposterously serious in those days...Lightly, lightly - it's the best advice ever given me...to throw away your baggage and go forward. There are quicksands all about you, sucking at your feet, trying to suck you down into fear and self-pity and despair. That's why you must walk so lightly. Lightly, my darling..." —Aldous Huxley  ☉☉☉  @bananasutra #lyrics    [Intro] Here it is, the weight we hold Grasping too tight, the world grows cold Oh, too hard, my dear, too hard  [Verse 1] The steps you take, they sink like stone Through quicksand fears, you're not alone But lightly, child, the path unfolds Lightly now, let go, let go  [Chorus] It’s dark because you try, you try Release the chains, and learn to fly Oh, lightly now, my darling, sigh Let baggage fall, and kiss the sky  [Verse 2] Feel deeply still, but take it soft The world spins fast, you drift aloft Yes, let it come, and let it go A fleeting wind, it doesn’t show  [Bridge] The fears that grip, they pull you down To pity’s depths, where sorrows drown But darling, walk as though the air Carries you lightly everywhere  [Chorus] It’s dark because you try, you try Release the chains, and learn to fly Oh, lightly now, my darling, sigh Let baggage fall, and kiss the sky  [Outro] Here it is, the truth you hold Let it be light, let it unfold Oh, too hard, my dear, too hard Walk lightly now, you’ve played your card  — * “Too Hard, (My Friend)” sister song(s) here: https://soundcloud.com/bananasutra/sets/too-hard-flowsutra-epx2  🍄✨

description: I confess, I’ve been spending too much time in BLOWsutra mode—mourning empathy and democracy, speaking up in the name of liberty, equality, fraternity, and it gets better (goddamn not)… but(t) after a while, it's true that kind of heavy cringe just get so heavy, it starts feeling like it's "too hard", you know? Plus, it’s Friday. So I figured, perfect time for a sonic FLOWsutra kiss, or two (you can download this one for free too :)   Lyrics inspired by monsieur Huxley: "It's dark because you are trying too hard. Lightly child, lightly. Learn to do everything lightly. Yes, feel lightly even though you're feeling deeply. Just lightly let things happen and lightly cope with them. I was so preposterously serious in those days...Lightly, lightly - it's the best advice ever given me...to throw away your baggage and go forward. There are quicksands all about you, sucking at your feet, trying to suck you down into fear and self-pity and despair. That's why you must walk so lightly. Lightly, my darling.”—Aldous Huxley, Island  🍄✨  — Track 1 lyrics: [Verse 1] Too hard, you push, you strive, you fight, It’s dark because you clutch too tight. The weight of worry, like quicksand deep, Pulls at your feet, won’t let you leap.  [Refrain] Lightly, my darling, let it all flow, Let the breeze take you where you need to go. Feel it all deeply, but wear it so thin, Let it go lightly and let life begin.  [Verse 2] Too hard, you build these walls of stone, Fighting the storms all on your own. But the wind it whispers, “Throw it away, Your heavy baggage keeps lightness at bay.”  [Refrain] Lightly, my darling, let it all flow, Let the breeze take you where you need to go. Feel it all deeply, but wear it so thin, Let it go lightly and let life begin.  [Bridge] I was serious once, so preposterously grim, Each step weighed down, the world so dim. But I’ve learned now to tread with a lighter air, To laugh at despair, to unburden the care.  [Verse 3] Too hard, you fight the shadows near, It’s fear that whispers despair in your ear. Throw it away, those whispers of doom, Let in the light, it’s the end of the gloom.  [Final Refrain] Lightly, my darling, let it all flow, Let the breeze take you where you need to go. Feel it all deeply, but wear it so thin, Let it go lightly and let life begin.  Lightly, lightly, let life begin…  — Track 2 lyrics:  [Verse 1] Too hard, you’re trying too hard, my friend, The weight you bear, it doesn’t end. Each step sinks deeper in the sand, So softly, child, take my hand.  Too hard, you push and pull and fight, But life’s not won by grasping tight. There’s quicksand, pulling at your shoes, Let go of fear, there’s none to lose.  [Chorus] Oh, lightly, oh, lightly, just let it all go, Feel deeply, but gently, there’s no need to show. The baggage you carry, it’s dragging you down, Throw it away and dance ‘round.  [Verse 2] Too dark, because you strain for light, But all you need is softer sight. The day won’t come with force or shove, It waits for ease, it waits for love.  Too much, your seriousness, so grave, You were not made to toil as slave. The weight of life is only air, So walk, my love, with tender care.  [Chorus] Oh, lightly, oh, lightly, just let it all go, Feel deeply, but gently, there’s no need to show. The baggage you carry, it’s dragging you down, Throw it away and dance ‘round.  [Outro] Too hard, you’re trying too hard, my dear, The way is clear, if you draw near. Just lightly walk, don’t press the ground, And joy will follow all around.

description: Are you a grifter or a gifter?  “Grifters” tears through 14 psychedelic flows, interrogating the anatomy of coercion: the hands that grab without asking, the fear sold as fate, the silence mistaken for consent... it’s not a left/right polemic. It’s just one question that matters, and won’t let go... It’s a song of reckoning. Can you hear no? Or do you believe silence means go?  Fool psychedelick EPx14 asks the same thing in every genre… like this: ❯ Psychedelic Punk Rock BURLESQUE (1-3) ❯ Psychedelic Post-Punk Country Burlesque Banjo BLUES (4-6) ❯ Queen of Authentic Country Banjo Folk Dub BLUES (7) ❯ Psychedelic Poetry Folk the Bridge DUB (8-9) ❯ Psychedelic F-Bomb Hip Hop LOFI (10-11) ❯ Psychedelic Gipsy Flamenco Fado Techno World INDIE (12-14)  — @bananasutra #lyrics   [intro] Grifters… (Grifters)  [Verse 1] Why do they take what’s not their due? Why do they cross all the lines of truth? Why do they claim their needs are holy, Dress up coercion as “destiny”?  [Pre-Chorus] They say it’s leadership, but see… Hands that grab like they’re entitled to me, They kill candor, forget trust’s earned, Consent ignored, no lesson learned…  [Chorus] (Grifters) Are you a grifter or a gifter? (Grifters) Do you take or ever consider? (Grifters) Can you hear me when I say no? (Grifters) Or believe silence means go?  [Verse 2] Who knows why they fake concern or care, Who knows why they weaponize despair, Why they like to sell fear dressed as fate, Then blame the crowd they agitate…  [Pre-Chorus 2] They speak of order, law, control, But do not know the human soul… They push, they pull, without a pause, Then call the fallout “natural laws”…  [Chorus] (Grifters) Are you a grifter or a gifter (Grifters) Truth-tearer or true listener? (Grifters) Can you dance, or just break? (Grifters) Dare to ask, or just take?  [Bridge] Not left or right, not votes that swing, Just how we touch another being… Can you meet me eye to eye, Or just share lies that justify?  [Final Chorus] (Grifters) Politics without consent’s a mask, (Grifters) Monsters that never bother to ask. (Grifters) Empathy always knows where it stands, (Grifters) With wide open hearts and open hands.  [Outro] Grifters… Differ…

description: "The Great Naked King" is a SHOWsutra song about the oldest trick in the book: convince the crowd that what they cannot see is proof of their own unworthiness. Add a golden throne, a Twitter account, and a loyal chorus of moronic applauders, et voilà, you have yourself an idiocracy. Oh, if only I was joking...  Hans Christian Andersen wrote "The Emperor's New Clothes" parable in 1837. And I bet he would not be surprised it is still so relevant. And then, there's Charlie, mon chéri. The song borrows its title from Chaplin's 1940 masterpiece "The Great Dictator"—the most tender act of political foolishness in cinema history. They both understood that laughter is not the opposite of seriousness. It is what seriousness becomes when it has nothing left to lose.  So here we are. Laughing. On purpose. At the pageantry, the bling-bling, the paper crowns, the hollow halls, the crooked applause, the vast collective hallucination stitched together in pompous complicity and called a nation... Until, somewhere in the crowd, a brave small voice (who knows better) speaks up. Simple truth with humble poise. They whispered low, “the wise ones see,” “What’s hidden here in mystery,” As white hillbillies praised the air, Swore up and down they saw it there. description: "The Great Naked King" is a SHOWsutra song about the oldest trick in the book: convince the crowd that what they cannot see is proof of their own unworthiness. Add a golden throne, a Twitter account, and a loyal chorus of moronic applauders, et voilà, you have yourself an idiocracy. Oh, if only I was joking... Until, somewhere in the crowd, a brave small voice (who knows better) speaks up. Simple truth with humble poise. description: Fair question-gone-banana-peel of the day: can you believe some people dare deny racism STILL is a core root cause of bias and injustice?! Yup, true crime story.  So here I trip hop again, with some of the logical and ethical yet somehow absurd KNOWsutra questions fuming in my soul... praying for a come back of critical thinking, empathy, equality, fraternity, and goddamn #shame in Murica. Vive la #musictherapy gone bananas!   This EPx9 is Volume 2 of this song, and flows  ❯ Gipsy Jazz (1-3)  ❯ Fusion LoFi (4-9)  🙈 🙉 🙊 "So, What Is Racism?" @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro/Chorus] Tell me, tell me, is it in the mirror? Or hiding in the jokes when the room gets clearer? If love’s universal, why you drawing them lines? Bananasutra asking questions, messing with your mind.  [Verse 1] Is it when you clutch your purse on the late-night train? Or when the résumé gets tossed for the “wrong” last name? Is it system-made, or just “a couple bad dudes”? Or is it brunch talk, served with fair-trade food?  What if you laugh at a meme, but it cuts like a blade, Would you still call it harmless, or truth in the shade? If color’s just skin, why’s the history so loud? Why the silence when the wrong ones speak too proud?  [Chorus] Tell me, tell me, is it in the mirror? Or hiding in the jokes when the room gets clearer? If love’s universal, why you drawing them lines? Bananasutra asking questions, messing with your mind.  [Verse 2] Is it subtle like perfume in a Sunday crowd, Or heavy like a cop’s knee pressing too loud? Is it “I don’t see race”, but you kinda still do? Or is it blaming all the problems on “a chosen few”?  Would you trade your skin just to borrow their shoes? Walk the block, pay the rent, get stopped with no clues? If fairness was real, would you lose your place? Or would equality feel like you’re in second place?  [Bridge] What’s the weight of a word when it’s not meant for you? What’s the cost of the dream when it don’t come true? If justice is blind, why she peeking through her mask? Here’s a question, baby, don’t be scared to ask.  [Chorus] Tell me, tell me, is it in the mirror? Or hiding in the jokes when the room gets clearer? If love’s universal, why you drawing them lines? Bananasutra asking questions, messing with your mind.  [Outro] So what is racism, honey, is it yours, is it mine? Or just a ghost in the closet we pretend’s benign? Keep on asking, keep peeling the skin, ’Cause the fruit gets sweeter when the truth kicks in…  🍌💨

description: This is an old (circa 2025) EPx6 I never released, and Vol. 2 of my remakes of "La quête" and flows crescendo-ish:  Lullaby INDIE (1-2) ❯ Cello JAZZ (3) ❯ Muse DUB (4) ❯  Burlesque ROCK (5) ❯ Banjo BLUES (6)   It's rare I have favorites, because you know, rainbows don't choose a favorite color... But(t), "La Quête" (The Quest) by Jacques Brel gets my heart beating like a wagging puppy with stars in the eyes! I love it because, to me, it embodies all of the sutras (i.e. the mantras of a holy life in a world gone bananas), as clear as Brel is true—to explore and share what matters with curiosity and courage, to play and learn with unyielding joy and empathy,  to trust and appreciate the humility and grace of GLOWsutra, we must first learn to love, lose, laugh, and loop around. Namely, we must live through KNOWsutra, BLOWsutra, SHOWsutra, GROWsutra and FLOWsutra... until the ultimate, glorious #blessedbe daze of BOWsutra <3  VOL1, released in November 2024 : To Dream EP X8 | Jacques Brel Chanson Reimagined : Psychedelic Psychedelic French Poetry  (The Quest of an Unyielding Star  • Jacques Brel Remake) https://soundcloud.com/bananasutra/sets/the-quest-brel-poetry-jazz-remakes-x8  -- Et pour une fois, pas de lyrics. Instead, here are Jacques' lyrics  La Quête Lyrics:  [Paroles de "La quête"]  [Couplet unique] Rêver un impossible rêve Porter le chagrin des départs Brûler d'une possible fièvre Partir où personne ne part  Aimer jusqu'à la déchirure Aimer, même trop, même mal Tenter, sans force et sans armure D'atteindre l'inaccessible étoile  Telle est ma quête Suivre l'étoile Peu m'importent mes chances Peu m'importe le temps Ou ma désespérance Et puis lutter toujours Sans questions ni repos Se damner Pour l'or d'un mot d'amour Je ne sais si je serai ce héros Mais mon cœur serait tranquille Et les villes s'éclabousseraient de bleu Parce qu'un malheureux Brûle encore, bien qu'ayant tout brûlé Brûle encore, même trop, même mal Pour atteindre à s'en écarteler Pour atteindre l'inaccessible étoile 💫

description: “But(t) How Can You?” is a silly quirky GROWsutra (i.e. where we be brave) detective story chasing conscience. Think Velma and Scooby-Doo gone "Where Are You!", but(t) asking philosophical questions that matter, instead of hunting ghosts with banter (same same, lol).  Blessed with goofy curiosity, a raised eyebrow, and magick howling glasses, they wonder how people manage to ignore the monsters—when science, education, and justice are getting booed by stinky fascist poo... How can one witness obvious, nefarious, scary dystopian  authoritarian nonsense, and just shrug?!  Across ragga DUB (1-4), gypsy LOFI (5-8), and INDIE cello sighs (8-9), this EPx10 pokes at cowardice and denial, and sings the clues of a simple mystery: what happens when good conscience meets convenient silence? Well, have you heard of what’s science, Or you deny it in essence? I’m just saying ‘cause I’m curious, And education is glorious.  But(t) how can you, Scoo-bi-doo woo?! Who goes poo poo, When fascists boo?!  Well now, who’s gonna take a chance, At true leadership, present tense? I’m just singing ‘cause I’m nervous, And I wish we’d be more cautious…  But(t) how can you, Scoo-bi-doo woo?! Who goes poo poo, When fascists boo?!

Think Velma and Scooby-Doo gone "Where Are You!", but(t) asking philosophical questions that matter, instead of hunting ghosts with banter (same same, lol).  Blessed with goofy curiosity, a raised eyebrow, and magick howling glasses, they wonder how people manage to ignore the monsters—when science, education, and justice are getting booed by stinky fascist poo... How can one witness obvious, nefarious, scary dystopian  authoritarian nonsense, and just shrug?!  Across ragga DUB (1-4), gypsy LOFI (5-8), and INDIE cello sighs (8-9), this EPx10 pokes at cowardice and denial, and sings the clues of a simple mystery: what happens when good conscience meets convenient silence? Spoiler: Scooby knows something smells funny, woo, but(t) also boo 👻  — @bananasutra #lyrics   Well, have you met your good conscience, Or you buried it in silence? I’m just asking ‘cause I’m curious, How one ignores what’s so obvious!  But(t) how can you, Scoo-bi-doo woo?! Who goes poo poo, When fascists boo?!  Well, have you heard of what’s science, Or you deny it in essence? I’m just saying ‘cause I’m curious, And education is glorious.  But(t) how can you, Scoo-bi-doo woo?! Who goes poo poo, When fascists boo?!  Well now, who’s gonna take a chance, At true leadership, present tense? I’m just singing ‘cause I’m nervous, And I wish we’d be more cautious…  But(t) how can you, Scoo-bi-doo woo?! Who goes poo poo, When fascists boo?!

description: “The line separating good and evil passes not through states, nor between classes, nor between political parties—but right through every human heart.” The Gulag Archipelago, by Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn  This song is inspired by and dedicated to Sasha (i.e. Sasha Solzhenitsyn, 1918–2008), a Russian writer, soldier, and historian, and (imho) one of the bravest truth-tellers of the 20th century. He survived the Soviet Gulag (forced labor camps), and then, literally risked his life to tell the world what happens when the truth collapses under totalitarianism—when we let lies, cruelty, and oppression run the show (like now, you know?...). He refused to play along with authoritarian narratives gone lethal bananas, even when everyone else pretended, and wrote “The Gulag Archipelago”, a massive, brutal, heartbreaking work that exposed how millions were imprisoned, tortured, or killed in the name of “progress” and “justice.” ❤️‍🔥 #grateful #revoltnow  “Spit Back the Lies” EPx20 peels deep and wide and crescendo, like a brave free whale gone wild banana :) ❯ Cello INDIE (1-3) ❯ Flamenco DUB (4-5) ❯ Dreamy DUB (5-10) ❯ Gipsy LOFI (11-12) ❯ Hip Dub LOFI (13-15) ❯ Psychedelic ROCK (16-18) ❯ Banjo BLUES (19-20)  — @bananasutra #lyrics   [Verse 1] They paved the streets with broken oaths,  Stacked their sins up stone by stone.  Built a house of hollow prayers,  And called it home.  [Chorus]  Spit back the lies,  Spit back the lies.  Burn down the thrones,  Bury the crowns.  We live,  We live not by lies.  [Verse 2] They crowned the rats, they blessed the thieves,  Fed the poets to the machine.  But Sasha carved it on the bones,  No lie will reign.  [Chorus]  Spit back the lies,  Spit back the lies.  Tear down the walls,  Sing through the scars.  We live,  We live not by lies.  [Bridge]  Truth don't wear a pretty dress,  Truth don't sell her soul for less.  Truth walks out, battered and bare,  Still standing there.  [Final Chorus]  Spit back the lies,  Spit back the lies.  Raise up the wreckage,  Let it rise.   [Outro] We live,  We live not by lies.  We live,  We live not by lies.

description: “Kiss a Pulse” is a GLOWsutra (Poetry) song inspired by a luminous Lucille Clifton’s quote I simply adore:  “Many people wish to be poets because they wish to wear the title, but one should wish to celebrate more than one wishes to be celebrated.”   It’s like a tender, psychedelic cabaret dream wrapped in sultry smoke drifting through indie bluesy Gipsy LoFi Dub Jazz, anchored in a hypnotic upright bass that beats like a second heart. The lyrics use playfool alliterations (like I like) and quirky iambic turns, inviting you to taste the song, blush at the mystery (the deeper the butter:), and let the music move through your marrow instead of your ego—not wearing crowned titles, but breathing the rhythm, not chasing vain applause, but savoring plain awe... description: “Hello, Oh No?” is a silly, cheeky GROWsutra true story that sings like psychedelic poetry, a hope-fool tune asking simple questions that actually matter, in a world gone mad bananas, a world that forgot how cute it is to blush... Think of it as a friendly wink in the dark, a small song with big questions—playful on the surface, philosophical underneath.  It’s about the magic healing power of free will, the importance of critical thinking with a pulse. It’s about courage, honesty, humility, and unity, i.e. the superpowers we misplaced somewhere on the cha-ching media conveyor belt, where noise dressed up as wisdom, and ego bought a throne and called it strength—because really, who(tf) sold us the myth that success means crushing others, and fear beats love? And why(tf) did we applaud?!  I wrote this for the brave dreamers and future-makers, to dare you to care for the kids and the grown-ups who got bamboozled along the way; the ones who were told empathy was weak and win-win was naïve, while hollow peacocks in blinged-out power suits paraded around calling hoarding “leadership.” Even though history keeps whispering the same truth: it is kindness that defines real winners.  This song hums a gentle but stubborn reminder: real winners don’t blindfold themselves for comfort. They choose spark over dark. Win-win over win-lose that end up being lose-lose. Empathy over hypocrisy. Unity over vanity. Because, see... kindness isn’t weakness, it’s clarity. Win-win isn’t cute or “woke”, it’s pragamatic, it's empiric, it's strategic. And humility? Oh darling, that’s DIVINE!  And maybe, just maybe, if we stop mistaking leadership for expensive cosplay, and start choosing clearer hearts over louder heroes, maybe we’ll see through the toxic smoke of shiny mirrors? Maybe we’ll recognize ego-madness when it struts by, cocky dressed as fancy progress. Maybe we’ll even learn (or remember) to laugh at (not with) the pompous Prometheus and snake oil fraudsters,  selling cha-ching over win-win sharing… Maybe. Can we?  So now, hello, oh no?!… What will you choose, bro? The choice is (y)ours. What’s the deal? Do we fight, or do we heal? To shine, or whine, it’s your choice, Kindness always lifts your voice.  Loving, not just winning, true, Don’t play the game to make others blue. description: Ok, y'all... sooo, who's ready to RISE (tf) UP, in the glorious name of liberty, equality, and fraternity—against the deadly absurdity of  tyrannic deceit and cruelty?? Victor Hugo would approve 🗽  ☆☆☆ Original (1821) French poem by Victor Hugo, i.e. the inspiration for this song:   Liberté  Gloire à toi, Liberté!  Toi dont le temple immense Est bâti dans les cieux sur l'éternelle loi! L'homme est fait pour ton culte, et dans son cœur immense Tu dois régner comme un dieu-roi. Gloire à toi!  Déjà l'ombre a fui devant l'aurore, Déjà sous d'autres cieux l'éclair luit, Et l'avenir, couvert de lumière sonore, Sort du tombeau de cette nuit. Levez-vous! peuples nus, esclaves des despotes! Brisez vos fers! Le jour est pur! Peuples! à vos bourreaux, à leurs lois scélérates Opposez la justice et l'azur! Que votre front s'éclaire aux feux de la tempête! Que l’orage ouvre enfin vos yeux! Que dans le grand combat, sous la foudre honnête, Votre cri soit juste et glorieux! Ah! que vois-je? Ils se lèvent! ô sublime armée! Debout sous l'étendard vivant! Et moi, debout aussi, mon âme enflammée Dira: aux tyrans de la terre… adieu!  ☆☆☆ @bananasutra English lyrics:  [Verse 1] You’ve been bound, you’ve been broken, Kept in chains, never spoken, But the light, it is woken, And the dawn is callin’ you!  [Chorus] Rise up, ye naked peoples! Tear down the tyrant’s halls! Justice is a fire burnin’, Freedom rings, heed the call!  [Verse 2] They have ruled with their thunder, Struck us down, pulled us under, But the storm wakes our hunger, And the skies begin to roar!  [Chorus] Rise up, ye naked peoples! Tear down the tyrant’s halls! Justice is a fire burnin’, Freedom rings, heed the call!  [Bridge] Marchin’ now, hear us cryin’! Stars above, never dyin’! All their thrones, we’re defyin’, We are free forevermore!  [Final Chorus] Rise up, ye naked peoples! Tear down the tyrant’s halls! Justice is a fire burnin’, Freedom rings, heed the call!

description: “Question the Nation” is inspired by beat poet Lawrence Ferlinghetti’s “Pity the Nation” poem (after Khalil Gibran), filtered through my candid, thoughtful skepticism, and fiery, psychedelic truth-seeking lens—i.e. the bananasutra philosophy of what designing a meaningful & honest life in a sustainable & happy world is all about.   Musically, this EPx10 blends spoken-word protest, gipsy dub / experimental hip-hop / conscious blues lofi vibes... I like to think of it as a brave and poetic spiritual inquiry. I don’t claim to have answers, but I refuse to silence fair questions that matter; and, I sincerely care to invite you to pay attention, too!   — @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro] Question the nation… Hallucinate salvation… Where truth took a vacation… Bananasutra vibration…  [Verse 1] Who sold your soul at the discount mall? Who scrolls your dreams through the data sprawl? Who doctored your doubt with dopamine drip? Who coded your faith with a censorship script?  Who profits from panic, post after post? Who sells your fear for the likes they host? Who filters your pain till it looks aesthetic? Who turns your silence into something prophetic?  [Chorus] Question the nation, hear the narration, Dystopian salvation, mad fornication. Bananasutra, peel seducer, Fruit opener, pulse creator.  [Verse 2] Who digs ’em dicks of breaking bad news? Who hid the despair in patriotic hues? Who cheered the bully, called it divine? Who whispered “freedom” while drawing the line?  Who buried the poets in bureaucrat dust? Who trademarked love and privatized trust? Who voted progress, forgot the soul? Who took the toll just to play a role?  [Chorus] Question the nation, denounce corruption, Peace detonation, fair migration. Bananasutra, mantra mover, Dubbed-up Buddha, groove improver.  [Bridge] Who sleeps sound when the sirens cry? Who trolls like Felicia’s not nah-bye? Who scrolls past truth like an ad too long? Who hums along contempt empire’s song?  Who fears the mirror when the mask comes off? Who chokes on truth but still loves the cough? Who trades their soul for a trending thread? Who blesses the sly just to get ahead?  [Verse 3] Question the nation that bans reflection, That censors affection, that edits connection. Question the nation of pundits prophets, Algorithm bias in branded lockets.  Question the calm that feels like pain, The glittering screens that numb the brain. Question the cage that calls itself free, Question the nation. Question me.  [Outro] Bananasutra… breath of the data-dead, voice in the static thread… Sing them awake, make them shake, make them question instead.  Question the nation…  🍌✨

description: How do you feel about financing neofascism, Murica? Are you feeling dangerously insane yet? I'm asking because, to be completely honest, I dunno what(tf) dissent looks like now—but(t) I'm thinking not paying federal taxes seems like a reasonable, effective way to RESIST authoritarian cruelty, for example. I also desperately wonder why so few are reacting, much less organizing. Why are elected representatives doing what seems to account to basically nothing? Where(tf) are the brave thinkers, the benevolent leaders, the new millennium's progressive Joan of Arc? HOW CAN I HELP?   I dunno, but(t) I dare ask... even with just another BLOWsutra Revolution Ring song of yesterdays and tomorrows gone banana—it’s raw, it’s flawed, bloody dirty goddamn heck, it’s Monday in Murica 🙈🙉🙊🍟   — [Intro] No, it’s not bullshit as usual... The new normal is not neutral. Consent’s just gone, Rights abandoned. Democracy’s dead, Dissent’s gone dread...  [Verse 1 – state surveillance & corporate control] We used to scream into the streets, Now silence starts inside our feeds. They call it bugs… but posts go poof! YouTube’s chat rewrites the truth.  It’s a game of men of shame, History’s a threat to them. Big Tech broke its poker face, Now every scroll’s a hiding place.  [Chorus] This is what dissent looks like now: Invisible, internal, thin, A muted thought beneath your skin. It’s algorithms, not a gun, But hun, that’s how new wars are won. This is what dissent looks like now?  [Verse 2 – systemic institutional sabotage] They gutted justice from its core, Civil servants walked out the door. Philosophy? Deleted. Gone… Because ideas might catch on!  The deans stay quiet, donors cheer. The law’s sold in the name of fear. A government of grift and dare, Where treason hides in legal wear.  [Chorus] This is what dissent looks like now: A clause erased, a mail delayed, A syllabus they never made, A lawyer’s oath that’s lost its weight, A student debt that seals a fate… This is what dissent looks like now?  [Verse 3 – engineered chaos & bots Control] They seed the feeds with farmed out bots, Praise God, and peddle prison plots. The “debates” are traps that loop and stall, Just rage machines to waste us all.  Your logic’s flagged, your truth’s dismissed, While trolls define who can exist. They shoot and fire, then say “calm down”, And blame the victim, as most yawn...  [Bridge – this is not a drill] It’s not a glitch, It’s not a test, It’s policy, A bloody mess!  They want confusion, Promote delusion. They bait with faith, Then fear, then wrath!  Every move is built to break, Not fix, Not free, Not heal, Just take! Their plan is prepped, the script’s in place, And it’s ruthless, death wears no face…  [Final Chorus – the end game, i.e. so what now?] This is what dissent looks like now: A lullaby beneath a drone, A name redacted from a phone, A felon tweeting from hell’s throne.  May we dare scream, cry out loud… This is what dissent looks like now? 🕊️🩸

I like to imagine her singing it... like a rainbow in my cloud, forever (including the naughty word in the last verse, because she loves to laugh and def not afraid of good old banana jokes) 🍌🌈🙏    This is an edit of a GLOWsutra song originally inspired by Maya Angelou, and this EPx14 flows Mama DUB (1) ❯ Gipsy LOFI (2-6) ❯ Funky FOLK (7) ❯ Psychedelic BLUES (8-12) ❯ Cello Lullaby INDIE (13-14)  -- @bananasutra #originalsonglyrics    [Chorus / Intro] I wanna sing, I wanna pray out loud, To every rainbow in the cloud, Beyond the labels, lines, and tiers, Above the bias, noise, and fears.  [Verse 1] I wanna thank you, dear, for being kind, For proving hearts ain’t deaf or blind, No matter who you chose to be, No matter what sets your spirit free.  [Verse 2] No matter what makes you move and smile, No matter who you love or why, No matter where you catch your breath, No matter how you dance with faith.  [Chorus] I wanna sing, I wanna pray out loud, To every rainbow in the cloud, Beyond the labels, lines, and tiers, Above the bias, noise, and fears.  [Verse 3] No matter what tongue you learned to speak, No matter the size of your goddamn dick. I want you to know you’re seen, you’re rare, For daring not to fit the square.  [Outro] Let’s help each other learn to flow, Choose how we show, while others blow, Dare to grow and share out loud, Be the rainbow in the clouds.

In all candor, the truth is I dunno what(tf) to do! I feel completely lost, and increasingly scared too. And so, we MUST! #noempathynoremedy  Meanwhile, I keep dreaming, praying that we can all somehow hang in there, free and fed, and someone somewhere soon will have the heart and guts to step(tf) up, as a much needed leader of the ant!fa revolution--to help us all bloom past the doom. Murica needs a Joan D'Arc and it needs it NOW!  👀  -- @bananasutra #originallyrics (variations)  [Intro] Apes gone wrong, no more law, Power games with teeth and claw. Twats or whacks? We shine like truth in pitch-black night.  [Verse 1] Tell me who knows when or why, Or how the truth just up and died. Lyin’ ain’t wrong if it pays their bills… They sell you Bibles and poppin’ pills.  Pimp daddies rich off holy scams, Preach while counting dirty grams. I can't see no valid cause, For clowns to rule with fake-ass laws.  [Verse 2] Sick dumb luck, dumb folks vote. Dead souls sick, dead men float. Riots rise from puppet’s act, Anus talk and power pact…  Enough’s enough, we crack the lies, No more dreams sold in disguise. We read the rules, we feel the fire, No more kings on tech empires.  [Chorus] This ain’t a drill, it’s real, it’s on! The king wears lies, the crown is gone… We bloom past doom, we fight with light. We shine like truth in pitch-black night.  [Bridge] No constitution left to burn, It’s just a myth at every turn, But hearts still speak, and fists still drum, We ain’t afraid of what’s to come…  [Outro] Let’s breathe, don’t fret,  just read,  reflect. The truth ain’t dead, it just got wrecked. Start again, revolt with grace. Burn the frauds, reclaim this place…  🫵🤠

KNOWsutra (Naked Truth) - "Shameless", asking aren’t you ashamed we ain’t ashamed, and what are we doing, really? 2. GROWsutra (Dare to Care) - "Universal Currency", asking what's a child worth on the sheet, and how the hell did we get this cold? #truestory 🍌🍔  — Song 1 - KNOWsutra: Shameless  [Verse 1] Didn’t they used to hide the pain? Curtains drawn, lies explained. Now it’s cages on parade, Front row seats and lemonade.  [Verse 2] Spanish moss and razor wire, Swamp gas and a ring of fire. Streaming live from hell’s front porch, Sippin’ pride through plastic straws.  [Chorus] Aren’t you ashamed we ain’t ashamed? Used to whisper, now we frame it. History once burned in smoke, Now it’s merch and Facebook jokes. So what are we doing, really? Is this who we are, Or just who we let be?  [Verse 3] Families fenced and tagged by name, Like barcodes marked with blame. You scroll right past the gator’s grin, “Just policy,” with southern spin.  [Bridge] They buried truth, once, deep in code, Now it rides a float down Main Street road.  [Chorus] Aren’t you ashamed we ain’t ashamed? Used to hide itnow we claim it. This ain’t justice, it’s a show. Will you clap… or will you go?  [Outro] So tell me plain, if this ain’t war, Why are there camps on freedom’s floor?  — Song 2 - BLOWsutra: Optics of Cruelty  [Verse 1] Do you light the stage with pain? Do you script the bloodstains? Policies dressed up as art, Is that pride… or just a part?  [Verse 2] Is your barrel pointed well? Do you feel divine as people yell? Is your silence sleek and smooth, Like the lies you make look true?  [Chorus] Is it policy… or performance art? Dead kids make a striking chart. You polished boots to match the scene, Who needs gas when you’ve got a screen? Cruelty’s the point, admit it, You choreographed every minute.  [Verse 3] Does the pain make you feel tall? Do you flirt with fascist calls? You don’t stumble… this was built. Goebbels would applaud your guilt.  [Bridge] Zionist or Nazi cap, Doesn’t matter when it’s a trap. Only difference in the fight? Where the barrel’s aimed tonight?  [Chorus] Is it optics, or is it truth? Do you need the proof in youth? Is this theater, is this real, Or just how you love to feel?  [Outro] You don’t lead, you puppeteer. And I see the strings real clear.  — Song 3 - GROWsutra: Universal Currency  [Verse 1] What’s a child worth on the sheet? Not enough to skip elite. Line item, bolded, clean, $109k, no in-between.  [Verse 2] They die in heat, they drown in flood… While suits debate the cost of blood. They say “don’t politicize the pain”, But budgets got a dollar sign for shame.  [Chorus] Children are the currency, And decency’s the rate. But y’all keep trading futures For fear, and war, and hate. What do they cost, in flesh and soul? And how the hell did we get this cold?  [Verse 3] A child in Ohio, a girl in the rain, Died while you argued about campaign gain. You priced their breath and called it fair… As if love could balance a billionaire.  [Bridge] Empathy ain’t weak, it’s wealth. It’s everything you kill by stealth.  [Chorus] Children are the currency, And we’re bankrupt on the heart. When budgets trump their little lives, We’ve torn the world apart. What are they worth? You tell me straight. Before it’s all too damn late.  [Outro] This ain’t about right or left. It’s about what the soul has left.

BLOWsutra (Apes Gone Wrong) - "Optics of Cruelty", asking if cruelty is the point, and where the barrel’s aimed tonight? 3. GROWsutra (Dare to Care) - "Universal Currency", asking what's a child worth on the sheet, and how the hell did we get this cold? #truestory 🍌🍔  — Song 1 - KNOWsutra: Shameless  [Verse 1] Didn’t they used to hide the pain? Curtains drawn, lies explained. Now it’s cages on parade, Front row seats and lemonade.  [Verse 2] Spanish moss and razor wire, Swamp gas and a ring of fire. Streaming live from hell’s front porch, Sippin’ pride through plastic straws.  [Chorus] Aren’t you ashamed we ain’t ashamed? Used to whisper, now we frame it. History once burned in smoke, Now it’s merch and Facebook jokes. So what are we doing, really? Is this who we are, Or just who we let be?  [Verse 3] Families fenced and tagged by name, Like barcodes marked with blame. You scroll right past the gator’s grin, “Just policy,” with southern spin.  [Bridge] They buried truth, once, deep in code, Now it rides a float down Main Street road.  [Chorus] Aren’t you ashamed we ain’t ashamed? Used to hide itnow we claim it. This ain’t justice, it’s a show. Will you clap… or will you go?  [Outro] So tell me plain, if this ain’t war, Why are there camps on freedom’s floor?  — Song 2 - BLOWsutra: Optics of Cruelty  [Verse 1] Do you light the stage with pain? Do you script the bloodstains? Policies dressed up as art, Is that pride… or just a part?  [Verse 2] Is your barrel pointed well? Do you feel divine as people yell? Is your silence sleek and smooth, Like the lies you make look true?  [Chorus] Is it policy… or performance art? Dead kids make a striking chart. You polished boots to match the scene, Who needs gas when you’ve got a screen? Cruelty’s the point, admit it, You choreographed every minute.  [Verse 3] Does the pain make you feel tall? Do you flirt with fascist calls? You don’t stumble… this was built. Goebbels would applaud your guilt.  [Bridge] Zionist or Nazi cap, Doesn’t matter when it’s a trap. Only difference in the fight? Where the barrel’s aimed tonight?  [Chorus] Is it optics, or is it truth? Do you need the proof in youth? Is this theater, is this real, Or just how you love to feel?  [Outro] You don’t lead, you puppeteer. And I see the strings real clear.  — Song 3 - GROWsutra: Universal Currency  [Verse 1] What’s a child worth on the sheet? Not enough to skip elite. Line item, bolded, clean, $109k, no in-between.  [Verse 2] They die in heat, they drown in flood… While suits debate the cost of blood. They say “don’t politicize the pain”, But budgets got a dollar sign for shame.  [Chorus] Children are the currency, And decency’s the rate. But y’all keep trading futures For fear, and war, and hate. What do they cost, in flesh and soul? And how the hell did we get this cold?  [Verse 3] A child in Ohio, a girl in the rain, Died while you argued about campaign gain. You priced their breath and called it fair… As if love could balance a billionaire.  [Bridge] Empathy ain’t weak, it’s wealth. It’s everything you kill by stealth.  [Chorus] Children are the currency, And we’re bankrupt on the heart. When budgets trump their little lives, We’ve torn the world apart. What are they worth? You tell me straight. Before it’s all too damn late.  [Outro] This ain’t about right or left. It’s about what the soul has left.

description: "It's an Ethical Paradox, an Oxymoron Maze" Vol. 2 EPx15 is a gipsy jazz edit of a dense KNOWsutra (Bertrand Knows) song that still needs some distilling, and so here it flows, from Burlesque Jazzzzzzzzz (1-10) to Gipsy LoFi (11-14) to Indie DUB (15)...  Lyrics inspired by Bertrand Russel's "Marriage and Morals" essay, where he asked: "Are prostitution and traditional marriage interconnected by hypocritical societal structures and discriminatory economic dependency?"   In this controversial essay, he made the fairly objective argument that marriage often prioritizes financial stability and social status over love, mirroring prostitution’s very transactional nature, and critiques the rigidity of marital norms, such as lifelong exclusivity and fidelity, which often stifle desires and lead to unmet physical, emotional, and spiritual needs. What if pr0stituti0n was required as a societal “release valve” for repressed desires, existing mostly as the condemned counterpart to marriage? What if the very notion of "ethical paradox" was an absurd oxymoron that never seems to end indeed? I ponder...  Why not think of marriage as a relationship based on equality, respect, and personal freedom, i.e. friendship? Could practicing truth, and trust, with humility and integrity, help reduce foul plays--including society’s reliance on femmes de joie, for example, heh? Well duh, d'oh, heck yeah! In fact, Bertrand concluded the following: “Marriage is for women the commonest mode of livelihood, and the total amount of undesired sex endured by women is probably greater in marriage than in prostitution.” (!) (Marriage and Morals)  And if you're doubting the veracity and value of Bertrand's kind and wise questions and observations, here's a fun fact for ya: marital r⭐︎pe was A-OK legal in almost ALL countries of the world, until the mid-90s?! (GASP)  • • •  @bananasutra #lyrics  [Verse 1] Step right up to the paradox parade, Where the morals they sell come double-edged blade. They wag their fingers, legislate laws, Then break ’em in private to polite applause.  It’s a sugar-spun circus, bananas on stage, Where yes means no and restraint’s just a phrase. Marriage or market, they blur the scene, Stamp it “righteous”, don’t ask what it means.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Verse 2] In the chapel it’s sacred, divinely endowed, In the alley it’s vulgar, condemned out loud. One buys a mattress, one buys a ring, Different costumes, same bargaining.  They preach purity, polish the lie, While need’s the product they monetize. Suit and tie or a scarlet brand, Same old hustle… supply, demand.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Bridge] Here’s a riddle, let logic stew: Who makes the crime, then blames it on you? They build the cage, lock the lid, Then curse the creature they forbid.  [Verse 3] Russell saw it, cut clean through the fog, Truth gets strangled by moral smog. Love’s not a contract, priced or policed, It’s a living thing begging for release.  Burn the scripts that barter the heart, Let freedom finish what law couldn’t start. No paradox, no moral sleight, Just justice breathing in open light.  [Chorus] It’s an ethical paradox, an oxymoron maze, They shame what they need, still demand it gets praise. They swear it’s love, then they pay for the kiss, Condemn the same trade they refuse to resist.  [Outro] Fold up the map, walk out the maze, No room for riddles in love’s next phase. The ethical circus packs up its tent, Let truth be simple, that’s how it’s meant. • • •

description: New year, new song, and only two things, darling: get the facts right, keep love in sight, et voilà <3  "Two Things, Darling" is a KNOWsutra EPx11 flows LOFI ❯ INDIE ❯ DUB ❯ BLUES... The song inspired by my all-time fav dead-daddy, the one and only Bertrand Russel, who taught me the conquest happiness is a simple game of curiosity and kindness—for example, when he was asked to outline the advice he would give to future generations, circa 1959:   “I should like to say two things, one intellectual and one moral.  The intellectual thing I should want to say to them is this: When you are studying any matter or considering any philosophy, ask yourself only what are the facts and what is the truth that the facts bear out. description: This one started with Tom Waits, saying "There's no Prayer Like Desire".   And then, I thought...  "Truth is NOT found in WHO powers the light, not who we know or like, who won the fight, it’s not about who is good looking, sweet talking, crowd pleasing, or even award winning… truth is WHO about we believe in. Truth is NOT about WHAT we happen to believe in… truth is not what the preachers, saints, or sinners may say, whisper or scream. It’s not what we do that matters, truth is not about what book we choose to read into, it’s what songs we like to sing, or what tales we like share, or what false promises make us linger. Truth is not HOW or WHEN or WHERE we like to dance. It’s not about HOW one delivers an act of faith between two breaths, it’s now HOW others translate where it came from, when they can even fathom, it’s not about where the will to trust old words wisdom leads us, not how we preach along Leviticus or even Confucius. The truth that matters, the only truth I care about is WHY. It is the truth that never lies, because it lies deep inside one’s heart desires. It is why we choose to join the dance, why we break into a trance, why we find balance, why we care to dare bare the lore of lies untold. Truth is the soul that fuels the bold, the brave, it is the fire that burns in one’s true heart’s desire, the only prayer that shines like it’s divine. Truth is the beat of intimate intentions, the pulse of our deepest motivations, the seed of true  salvation. The truth is the only truth that matters is raw, it’s the reason WHY we love to share, WHY we dare to be in the bare, WHY we hope to win, why we pray we live. Because there’s no prayer like desire."  And then, I wrote several short (unreleased) KNOWsutra But(t) Why songs, all titled "There's No Prayer Like Desire"... this is one 'em.  @bananasutra #originalsong #lyrics  [verse 1] Not who powers the light, Not who wins the fight, It’s the song in the air, And the love that we dare.  [verse 2] Truth lies in the why, In the tears when we cry, Not what we preach or believe, But what we feel and receive.  [chorus] There’s no prayer like desire, It’s what lights the fire, It’s not the book we read, But the hunger that we feed.

description: People often ask me how I make songs, and the answer forever is it depends! That is the beauty of practicing the experimental art of creativity, it teaches us the paths to happiness are essentially like imagination, i.e.infinite. All you really need is a brave and open mind, and (more importantly) a curious and gratefool heart...   "Donkeys Years" is a SHOWsutra Fanana Club EP (i.e. where monkeys & donkeys play), because it was inspired by a silly party chit chat that brought me joy in the moment—plus, British humor is deliciously quirky cheeky (like I like), and huh, well, it's true I'm a hardcore slut for new words and expressions lol. But(t)... it is also very much infused with FLOWsutra and GLOWsutra vibes (i.e. where trust & gratitude shine), because at its core, it is (yet another:) thank you letter, to music, friends, fun, and freedom.    EPx20 flows (Side A) Dub INDIE ❯ Gipsy LOFI + (Side B) Fusion JAZZ ❯ Psychedelic BURLESQUE + (BONUS) a Ragga Mama Dub DUB finale, olé 💃🏻  -- @bananasutra  #originalsong #lyrics   🎵 DONKEYS YEARS  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Verse 1] Desert dust and beachside bass, Silly smiles on every face. Trippy souls and jesters peers, Dancing through the donkeys’ years.  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Verse 2] Forest nights and valley drums, Booty-shaking wisdom comes. Finding freedom, in trance gears, My monkey dears, my donkeys’ years.  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Glow-Out Outro] Thank you, ravers, light and loud, May we find healing in the crowd. SHOWsutra bows with peace fool grace… Now let’s hug once more,  and meet me by the bass
