description: People often ask me how I make songs, and the answer forever is it depends! That is the beauty of practicing the experimental art of creativity, it teaches us the paths to happiness are essentially like imagination, i.e.infinite. All you really need is a brave and open mind, and (more importantly) a curious and gratefool heart...   "Donkeys Years" is a SHOWsutra Fanana Club EP (i.e. where monkeys & donkeys play), because it was inspired by a silly party chit chat that brought me joy in the moment—plus, British humor is deliciously quirky cheeky (like I like), and huh, well, it's true I'm a hardcore slut for new words and expressions lol. But(t)... it is also very much infused with FLOWsutra and GLOWsutra vibes (i.e. where trust & gratitude shine), because at its core, it is (yet another:) thank you letter, to music, friends, fun, and freedom.    EPx20 flows (Side A) Dub INDIE ❯ Gipsy LOFI + (Side B) Fusion JAZZ ❯ Psychedelic BURLESQUE + (BONUS) a Ragga Mama Dub DUB finale, olé 💃🏻  -- @bananasutra  #originalsong #lyrics   🎵 DONKEYS YEARS  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Verse 1] Desert dust and beachside bass, Silly smiles on every face. Trippy souls and jesters peers, Dancing through the donkeys’ years.  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Verse 2] Forest nights and valley drums, Booty-shaking wisdom comes. Finding freedom, in trance gears, My monkey dears, my donkeys’ years.  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Glow-Out Outro] Thank you, ravers, light and loud, May we find healing in the crowd. SHOWsutra bows with peace fool grace… Now let’s hug once more,  and meet me by the bass

description: People often ask me how I make songs, and the answer forever is it depends! That is the beauty of practicing the experimental art of creativity, it teaches us the paths to happiness are essentially like imagination, i.e.infinite. All you really need is a brave and open mind, and (more importantly) a curious and gratefool heart...   "Donkeys Years" is a SHOWsutra Fanana Club EP (i.e. where monkeys & donkeys play), because it was inspired by a silly party chit chat that brought me joy in the moment—plus, British humor is deliciously quirky cheeky (like I like), and huh, well, it's true I'm a hardcore slut for new words and expressions lol. But(t)... it is also very much infused with FLOWsutra and GLOWsutra vibes (i.e. where trust & gratitude shine), because at its core, it is (yet another:) thank you letter, to music, friends, fun, and freedom.    EPx20 flows (Side A) Dub INDIE ❯ Gipsy LOFI + (Side B) Fusion JAZZ ❯ Psychedelic BURLESQUE + (BONUS) a Ragga Mama Dub DUB finale, olé 💃🏻  -- @bananasutra  #originalsong #lyrics   🎵 DONKEYS YEARS  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Verse 1] Desert dust and beachside bass, Silly smiles on every face. Trippy souls and jesters peers, Dancing through the donkeys’ years.  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Verse 2] Forest nights and valley drums, Booty-shaking wisdom comes. Finding freedom, in trance gears, My monkey dears, my donkeys’ years.  [Chorus] Donkeys’ years, oh dears, oh dears, Blacklight beats and ravers cheers. Shake those fears and shake those rears, Let’s dance on for donkeys’ years.  [Glow-Out Outro] Thank you, ravers, light and loud, May we find healing in the crowd. SHOWsutra bows with peace fool grace… Now let’s hug once more,  and meet me by the bass

description: Many months ago already, I created a series of revolutionary songs, to help me (and perhaps you, too) remember how howling for hope feels like, even if we clearly live on a planet where apes gone so goddamn wrong... This is one of 'em—a humble but(t) bold agnostic prayer, that we may all "Bloom brighter than gloom, bloom past the doom" 🍟 #freedomfries #chanson lol — @bananasutra #originalsong #lyrics  [Intro] We ain’t ghouls, we're gold and soul Born to rise, not play their role Magic minds with grit and grace We bring the storm with a softer face  [Chorus] Bloom brighter than gloom, bloom past the doom Love louder than war, bring heat to the room We bloom through the rut, bloom deep from the root We howl with the heart, in velvet and boots  [Verse 1] Respect the humble, raw and kind Compassion’s strength, not just a mind We ain't naive, we’re born to feel Our wounds are truth, our hope is real  Damn amazing animals, still Dreaming through this bitter chill Imagine joy in every step A world not owned by rich inept  [Verse 2] Let’s use tech to find what’s true Not control the chosen few Let’s bet on care, not blame and spite Let’s turn confusion into light  Learn to laugh, to cry, to scream To rip apart the toxic dream Let’s revolt with rhythm loud And write new laws in bloody sound  [Chorus] Bloom brighter than gloom, bloom past the doom Love louder than war, bring heat to the room We bloom through the rut, bloom deep from the root We howl with the heart, in velvet and boots  [Bridge] Bloom ain’t just for flowers and spring It’s how we rise, it’s how we sing In filth, in fire, in ash, in smoke We bloom when silence finally broke  [Outro] This ain't fiction, this is pain But pain births change, and love remains The revolution’s not just war It’s soul reborn, it’s so much more  🏴‍☠️🔥

track_title: [04] Peel Me Kindly • FLOWsutra Gone Banana Joke Gipsy JAZZ
ep_title: Peel Me Kindly 🍌 SHOWsutra Gone Banana à la Gipsy JAZZ EPx7
playlist_names_clean: JAZZsutra, SHOWsutra where bananas play
tags: Humor, banana joke, showsutra, gipsy jazz, conscious music, cheeky poetry, intimacy philosophy
description: I've been working on a bunch of BLOWsutra Gipsy Revolution songs—because the more I understand how mad bullshit bananas the world has gone, the more I can't help but(t) help me cope, by letting conscious, caring poetry pour out of me... And so, to help get my cortisol stress levels down, why not imagine you peeling me kindly, SHOWsutra meets FLOWsutra style, heh?! That sure is one delightfool way to nurture a brave smile, embrace the absurd, vulnerable truths we all share, and perhaps, help the universe align 😇🍌 #blessedbebananas  -- @bananasutra #originalsong #lyrics  [Verse 1] I don’t polish my edges, I don’t smooth out my flame,  what you see is the voltage, not a costume, not a game.  I don’t whisper for pity or rehearse what I feel,  I just call it like lightning, and I call the lightning real.  [Verse 2] I don’t sugar my meaning just to make it go down,  if the truth makes you dizzy, babe, enjoy the way you spin around.  I won’t package my softness like a product for the blind,  but if you’re curious and honest, you can try to peel me kind.  [Pre-Chorus] Yeah, I know I’m a handful, but not in the way they mean,  I’m the part of human nature that stays messy, bright, and clean.  [Chorus] So peel me kindly, no performance, no delay,  just a soul that likes to laugh while it’s lighting up the way.  Peel me kindly, take your time but stay awake,  ’cause the truth is only sweet when you savor what’s at stake.  [Verse 3] I don’t flirt with deception, I don’t bargain with my light,  I’m a woman built for clarity, not the theater of polite.  If my humor feels like wisdom with a twist of rebel shine,  It’s because the absurd truth makes the universe align.  [Bridge] I’m not hiding a secret, I’m not guarding a throne,  what I share is what I live, and what I live feels like home.  So if you need a safe illusion, darling, scroll another feed,  but if you want a real connection… take a breath and take the lead.  [Final Chorus] Peel me kindly, see the humor in the core,  see the part that keeps on dancing while the world wants something more.  Peel me kindly, feel the warmth inside the wise,  ’cause the sweetest revelations are the ones that don’t disguise.  [Glow-Out Outro] If the night feels a little brighter when the truth and music blend,  just remember every human glow is meant to be a friend.  And the world gets so much lighter when we drop the heavy lies,  so come shine with me a moment… let your heart stay uncompromised.

description: I dunno about you, yo, but(t) I know one thing fosho: I'd rather dare to care (and share) than ever pretend to play fair with devious haters! And also, I can't help but(t) worry for the kids I never had, their future... Because what(tf) are they supposed to conclude from the tragic fact the new so-called "winners" of the new world order are essentially slimy abusers with hypocritical morals, i.e. no values nor honor, just vain wealth hoarding suckers? How(tf) do you explain to a kid that, in this new dystopian reality gone mad bananas show we all seem trapped in, stinky rotten nefarious d*cks with deadly righteous double-standards are de facto the new rulers of (anti) human rights now, heh, how? #ohwhy #ahem     ✪ ✪ ✪ Original @bananasutra song #lyrics (partly inspired by #boburnham "How The World Works" song)  They’re asking ‘bout double standards, kids,  They're asking ‘bout what is fair,  While people in power break all of the rules,  And no one seems to care.  Corporations hold the power high,  No conscience, no check in place,  While leaders make promises they never keep,  Just lies that we have to face.  (Chorus)  And the kids ask: "Why don’t they pay for their wrongs?  If we can’t lie, then why can they?  Why do they break what’s been promised?  Why should we listen to what they say?”  They’re asking ‘bout the right from wrong, now,  They’re asking what matters most,  Is it truth, or greed, or power games,  And who’s held accountable?  Well, kids, it’s hard to explain this world,  Where honesty isn’t praised,  When promises break like fallen glass,  And fairness gets erased.  (Chorus)  So they’re asking: “Why don’t they pay for their wrongs?  If we can’t lie, then why can they?  Why do they break what’s been promised?  Why should we listen to what they say?”  ‘Cause children see what’s real and true,  They wonder why lies get a pass,  And they’re told to be good, to follow rules,  When others shatter trust like glass.  They’re asking about double standards, kids,  They’re asking for what is fair,  And maybe one day they’ll change this world  To one that’ll actually care.  (Outro)  Yes, maybe one day they’ll change this world  To one that’ll actually care.  ✪ ✪ ✪

description: “No Fear, My Dear” is a new bluesy humanist piano jazz kinda psychedelic soul torch song EPx19—a love letter inspired by and dedicated to the one and only Nina Simone, all strong women, and to the simple, not-so-radical idea that freedom only begins when fear ends 🕊️  EPx19 is a no BS BLOWsutra (Revolt Now) meditation, an agnostic prayer hour for truth, justice, & solidarity (for a world gone mad bananas)... yet another empathetic and courageous pep talk of light for dark times, to help our guts know, our hope grow, and our hearts glow  ❤️‍🔥  Side A (1-10) honors Nina's love for timeless acoustic bluesy piano jazz magic 🪄 Side B (11-19) indulges my love for psychedelic dub + indie folk + banjo blues + gipsy lofi experimental genres fusion  🏴‍☠️  ❢ ❢ ❢  @bananasutra song #lyrics   [INTRO] “I’ll tell you what freedom means to me… No fear, my dear, freedom means no fear.” And if my voice should tremble, Let it ring loud and clear.  [VERSE 1 — “I Had a Dream”] I had a dream we woke as one, No hearts undone, no souls outrun. A world where truths walked side by side, And no one had to run or hide.  [VERSE 2 — Strong-Women] My mother said, “Stand tall, my girl, Don’t bend your fire to fit their world.” She taught me souls can crack and break, But dignity’s our own to make.  [HOOK] No fear, my dear, the light inside us glows. No fear, my dear, true spirit always knows. No fear, my dear, freedom grows from our spark. No fear, my dear, bow out their goddamn dark.  [VERSE 3 — Sound-as-Salvation] Some pray in halls of dust and stone, Some kneel where tired saints have gone. But I find truth in rhythm’s rise, Where basslines pull the dark to light.  [VERSE 4 — Mirror of the Times] We watch the days grow mean and cold, Let’s join our hands, and break that mold. Let artists shine where lies appear, Hold a mirror against the fear.  [BRIDGE] If sorrow’s got you by the throat, I’ve walked that road, I know that note. Storm winds can strip us to the bone, And still we rise, don’t feel alone.  They’ll call the truth a threat, a scar, They’ll twist the past to dim a star. But breathe, my love, hold your own mark. Let freedom burn their toxic snark.  [HOOK] No fear, my dear, the light inside us glows. No fear, my dear, true spirit always knows. No fear, my dear, freedom grows from our spark. No fear, my dear, bow out their goddamn dark.  [OUTRO] If your voice should tremble, Let it tremble to the light. No fear, my dear, Let’s sing it through the night…  ❢ ❢ ❢

[VERSE 2 — Strong-Women] My mother said, “Stand tall, my girl, Don’t bend your fire to fit their world.” She taught me souls can crack and break, But dignity’s our own to make.  [HOOK] No fear, my dear, the light inside us glows. No fear, my dear, true spirit always knows. No fear, my dear, freedom grows from our spark. No fear, my dear, bow out their goddamn dark.  [VERSE 3 — Sound-as-Salvation] Some pray in halls of dust and stone, Some kneel where tired saints have gone. But I find truth in rhythm’s rise, Where basslines pull the dark to light.  [VERSE 4 — Mirror of the Times] We watch the days grow mean and cold, Let’s join our hands, and break that mold. Let artists shine where lies appear, Hold a mirror against the fear.  [BRIDGE] If sorrow’s got you by the throat, I’ve walked that road, I know that note. Storm winds can strip us to the bone, And still we rise, don’t feel alone.  They’ll call the truth a threat, a scar, They’ll twist the past to dim a star. But breathe, my love, hold your own mark. Let freedom burn their toxic snark.  [HOOK] No fear, my dear, the light inside us glows. No fear, my dear, true spirit always knows. No fear, my dear, freedom grows from our spark. No fear, my dear, bow out their goddamn dark.  [OUTRO] If your voice should tremble, Let it tremble to the light. No fear, my dear, Let’s sing it through the night…  ❢ ❢ ❢

description: This is Vol. 02 of one of my oldest peace prayer blues song (which I released as a single many months ago), about war history that repeats again and again and again... as if our foolish lill' goldfish brains were forever bamboozled into believing long-term "winning" means "beating" others, as if Blaise Pascal was an idiot and the ends always justified the means, as if ego power was more important to nurture than breathing in peace, as if taking brought more joy than sharing or giving, as if caring was too much to dare  #dontbeafoolishgoldfish  This EPx15 flows Cello INDIE (1-2) ❯ Psychedelic DUB (3-5) ❯ Gipsy LOFI (6-10) ❯ Dubby Banjo FOLK (11-13) ❯ True Soul BLUES (14-15) ... and I know I'm biased, but I thinks it's a beautiful one #enjoy  ❃ ❃ ❃ @bananasutra "Foolish Goldfish" @songlyrics  [Intro] Breathe in slow…  Hum the truths we know…  Shadows rise…  Blessed be whys…  [Verse 1] Take a moment, take a breath,  Let it settle in your chest.  What is fair, what is right?  Why do nightmares shape the night? description: “Synthema Sutra” is a nerdy banana philosophy explainer song, with no hooky hook, no catchy catch, no morale of the story even... It just asks what if Sutras were ancient Greek Synthemas, and strolls through each Sutra, one by one (KNOW, BLOW, SHOW, GROW, FLOW, GLOW, and BOW). One song, seven guiding principles, and a bunch of gods who totally would have benefited from #musictherapy :) Enjoy the melodic wander. Or don’t. Whatever works for ya. The gods won’t agree about it anyway, haha #truestory  EPx8 flows Indie (1), LoFi (2-3), Dub (4), Burlesque (5-7), and psychedelic Indie Punk Rock (8).  And if you're a Greek mythology nerd, or just curious about the ancient wisdom of musical storytelling gone bananas, or both, here's the split 🍌🏛️ 1. KNOWsutra : Prometheus ➵ Gave fire (knowledge) to humans; punished for empowering truth. A true win-win rebel. 2. BLOWsutra : Hydra + Medusa ➵ Hydra: corrupt systems that grow stronger when attacked wrong. Medusa: demonized femininity + misunderstood power. 3. SHOWsutra : Dionysus ➵ God of ecstatic joy, chaos, music, and theatre. Shows the sacred side of silliness and subversion. 4. FLOWsutra : Hermes ➵ Trickster god of transitions, language, and messages. A master of in-betweenness. 5. GROWsutra : Persephone ➵ Her cycle (abduction and return) teaches growth through descent and rebirth. Feminine resilience myth. 6. GLOWsutra : Apollo + Hestia ➵ Apollo = light, art, and healing. Hestia = the hearth, peace, inner warmth. 7. BOWsutra : Orpheus ➵ Music so beautiful it moved the gods. Journeyed to the underworld for love—faith, failure, and awe.  ♆♆♆ @bananasutra #lyrics   [Verse 1 – KNOW : Prometheus] Every truth you KNOW   Flickers soft and low   Like a stolen flame   From a god of shame   He gave us fire, paid the toll   To free the know from control    [Verse 2 – BLOW / Hydra + Medusa] Every cruel BLOW   Feeds the beast below   Cut one head, three rise   In the name of lies   And still we cage her rage and grace   To fear what dares to blow this place    [Verse 3 – SHOW : Dionysus ] Every mask you SHOW   Hides the pain you stow   But the sacred jest   Is a truth confessed   He laughs through wounds the wise won’t see   To show what dares to set us free    [Verse 4 – GROW : Persephone] Every time you GROW   You descend below   Like the seeds she sows   Where the silence knows   That roots need dark to rise again   And grow through loss, not just through gain    [Verse 5 – FLOW : Hermes ] Every word you FLOW   Is a place you go   Past the borderlines   Of the gods' designs   Hermes walks where logic ends   To let new meanings flow through bends    [Verse 6 – GLOW : Apollo + Hestia ] Every time you GLOW   Through the ache and slow   You become the spark   In the temple dark   He sings the wounds she warms to heal   They glow in silence, soft and real    [Verse 7 – BOW : Orpheus ] Every time you BOW   To the here and now   Like Orpheus did   For the love he hid   You trust the gods to give it back   But some truths die when we bow to lack    [Outro] Synthema… Sutra…   We know… we blow…   We show… we grow…   We flow… we glow…   And sometimes… we bow…    ♆♆♆

description: "Shady Fools" (Vol. 2 EPx9 is the twin sister song of "Shades of Fools", and what happens when I swap my KNOWsutra and BLOWsutra hats... because heh, better be safe than sorry, and also, because I often dream of a world where the shades of soul—not the color of skin—mattered (damn it)! Because (everybody knows), like Tom Waits once said, "there's no prayer like desire", And Cindy Lauper was definitely onto something with that "True Colors" song :)  Just remember this, when judging character: what matters is the why! #truestory   •  •  •  @bananasutra #lyrics  [Intro] I don’t know, I don’t know, But I know we’re all fools on show, Some play fair, some go low, Shady fools, oh they glow…  [Verse 1] In a carnival of painted smiles, Some walk straight, some crawl the miles, Seeking fortune, seeking fame, In the shadows, they all look the same.  [Chorus] Shady fools, in the masquerade, Hidin’ true selves, in the choices made, Not the who or the where, the when or how, But the why that cuts through the crowd.  [Verse 2] I’ve lived and learned, seen the spectrum wide, From fools that hide to those with pride, It’s not the face, the place, or name, But the reason that they play the game.  [Bridge] Oh, the games they play, the lies they say, All for a piece of the fool’s buffet, But in the end, under the moon’s soft glow, The why is the only truth you’ll ever know.  [Chorus] Shady fools, in the circus light, Every soul has a shade tonight, Look beyond the laughter, beyond the cries, And see the truth in their eyes.  [Outro] I don’t know, but here’s the truth I found, We’re all fools just dancin’ ‘round, Intentions matter, that’s the key, To see the shades of fools, oh can’t you see?   •  •  •   Note: if you're reading this, I'm gonna assume you like this song (like me:), and tell you that the first Volume of this EP, which I shared on SoundCloud several months ago as a single, is still my fav, and so you should totally look it up now :)

description: The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill. And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.  2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.  3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.  4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.  5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.  6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.  2. Affection: Love given and love received.  3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.  4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.  5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.  6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).  7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

description: Just another WTF song, I reckon 🍌 EPx10 flows Accordion 🪗 ❯ Cello Bass Guitar 🎻 ❯ Piano 🎹  Please pardon my French, and enjoy the absurd waltz circus des secrets de polichinelles--it's like a gipsy burlesque chanson show, a story about  dystopian abuse (of all kinds) is increasingly being normalized, here and there and again, as we (the people, women in particular) are being dehumanized... yet (the worst part) people be like shhh 🤫  🎪  🎪  @bananasutra #lyrics  [Intro]  Chut...  Fais comme si t’savais pas,  Fais comme si t’voyais pas,  Le roi est nu, mais quelle classe, n’est-ce pas ?  [Couplet 1]  Sous la dentelle des fashos,  On cache les corps, on cache les mots,  On peint la guerre couleur d’amour,  Et les bourreaux jouent les troubadours.  La foi prêche la décence,  Les fous vendent la délivrance,  Et les rois font la révérence  À leurs propres violences.  [Refrain]  C’est un secret de Polichinelle,  Le monde tourne à la ficelle.  On bénit l’ordre, on brûle l’ciel,  Au nom du bien, des seins, oh hell…  C’est un secret de Polichinelle,  Tout l’monde ment, tout l’monde est belle.  On rit, on pleure, on s’fait la belle,  Sous la loi des criminels.  [Couplet 2]  On dit “paix” pour vendre des bombes,  On dit “mère” pour taire les tombes,  On dit “libre” pour mieux soumettre,  Et “Dieu” pour justifier le maître.  Les hommes de loi, les femmes de honte,  Les vieilles idoles qu’on remonte,  Les dieux, les lois, les vieilles montres,  Tous décalés d’un monde qui s’démonte.   [Refrain]  C’est un secret de Polichinelle,  Le monde tourne à la ficelle.  On bénit l’ordre, on brûle l’ciel,  Au nom du bien, des seins, oh hell…  C’est un secret de Polichinelle…  On s’embrasse, on fait la belle,  Comme des culs qui se querellent,  Danse ma sœur, pense infidèle.  [Pont]  Fais-moi croire encore un peu,  Que le silence est vertueux,  Que l’obéissance est glorieuse,  Et que la foi n’est pas dangereuse…  Mais chut... le cirque recommence,  Marionnettes en transe,  Et sous la piste, les consciences  Qui s’embrasent en connivence.   [Refrain final]  C’est un secret de Polichinelle,  Qu’on s’aime fort, mais à genoux,  Et qu’le courage des demoiselles  Fait trembler tous les vieux papous.   C’est un secret de Polichinelle…  Sous la jupe du mensonge universel,  J’cache ma rage et mon appel,  Pour un monde moins artificiel.  [Outro]  Chut...  Tout le monde sait, Mais personne ne dit rien.  C’est bien plus commode… Et puis, plus inhumain...  🃏🍌

description: In France (where I grew up), there's a wise, old saying that goes "a glass of wine a day keeps the doctors away"...  Chez #bananasutra it's the same, but(t) with songs, hehe ✌️😽🍷🎶 #meow -- Piano EPx5 @bananasutra #lyrics  [Intro] We know drama begets drama, We know trauma begets trauma. Your cynicism sure beats mine… But(t) where’s the cruelty victory line? A rabbit hole of self-foolfilled prophecy, Vengefool honor, endless atrocity.  [Outro] We know drama begets drama, We know trauma begets trauma… Silence begets silence, too,  'Til someone breaks the loop… maybe you? -- #savethekittens (damn it)?!

description: Two sister-songs, with lyrics directly inspired by Dr. Ramani’s video “Narcissism: The Secondhand Smoke of Mental Health” (on YouTube)...  Why “secondhand smoke”? * Even if you don’t have NPD, being around narcissists makes you sick. * The harm spreads outward: family, partners, coworkers absorb the toxicity.   Five recognizable patterns: 1. Malignant/toxic narcissist – sadistic, manipulative, close to psychopathy. 2. Grandiose narcissist – bragging, flashy, entitled. 3. Covert/vulnerable narcissist – “woe is me,” hyper-sensitive, passive-aggressive. 4. Communal narcissist – the #hashtag-do-gooder; public philanthropy, private cruelty. 5. Benign narcissist – vapid, superficial, not as cruel, but emotionally shallow.  Seven diagnostic hallmarks (the “big seven”): 1. Lack of empathy (the bedrock). 2. Entitlement. 3. Grandiosity. 4. Superficiality. 5. Chronic need for admiration/validation. 6. Rage when threatened. 7. Arrogance (dismissiveness, devaluation).  Other patterns: - Gaslighting, projection, exploitation, jealousy, schadenfreude, manipulation. - Comorbidity with depression, substance abuse, compulsive sex/love behaviors. Impact on others: - Creates learned helplessness: partners feel nothing they do makes a difference. - Can devastate self-esteem, health, and careers.  Treatment: - Narcissists rarely seek therapy voluntarily. - Progress is very slow, at best moving them from toxic → tolerable. - No medication cures narcissism. - Empathy must be cultivated early; prevention is everything.  Hopeful note: - Empathy is teachable in children. Parents should model and mirror empathy above all else.  --- SIDE A EPx3: “Secondhand Smoke”   [Intro] Step right up, darlings, don’t choke, This song is called secondhand smoke. It’s about cocksure egos. Ha. Ready? Down we go.  [Verse 1] No mirror inside, so they borrow your face, Validation’s the drug they chase. Shiny cars, hollow eyes, Charm that blinds, and charm that lies.  [Chorus ] Mirror, mirror, what do you know? Arrogant hearts all need a glow show. Praise me, praise me… but can you grow? Like, can you flow and bow? (Or just blow, blow?)  [Verse 2] Entitled thrones on borrowed ground, Their laughter’s loud, their silence profound. Grand illusions, paper crowns, Lift you up, then tear you down.  [Chorus ] Mirror, mirror, what do you know? Arrogant hearts all need a glow show. Praise me, praise me… but can you grow? Like, can you flow and bow? (Or just blow, blow?)  [Bridge] No empathy, no remedy, Woke ain’t like smoke, ain’t your enemy. Round and round, the blowers spin, And sorrow seeps through my skin.  [Outro] Step away, darling, break the spell, Breathe your own air, and breathe it well. Leave their circus, let them choke,  On their own secondhand smoke.  --- SIDE B EPx3: "Arrogant hearts"  [Verse 1] Step right up to the mirror maze, Where charm is cheap and love decays, They smile so wide while they cut you thin, Secondhand smoke seeps under your skin.   [Chorus] No empathy, no remedy, Entitlement is their melody, Grandiose ghosts on high ego stage, Arrogant hearts and their puppets cage.   [Verse 2] Superficial saints with a selfie crown, Validation junkies shake you down, Malice erupts when masks won’t stay, Gaslight fever keeps truth at bay.   [Bridge] “Ladies and gents, beware the show! They’ll promise excellence, deliver shadow. Communal halos, malignant schemes, Covert whispers, grandiose dreams!”  [Final Chorus] Learned helplessness in smoky air, You breathe their poison unaware, The crowd applauds, the tyrant grins, But emptiness echoes where soul cannot sing.

description: Ce qui est marrant c'est que salaud au féminin, en français, c'est pas salaude! Ha, #justsayin Chanson inspirée par un vrai livre recent intitulé "Le Temp Des Salauds" 🍟🤓🤌  @bananasutra lyrics (variantions):  [Intro] Bienvenue, mesdames et messieurs,  Au grand bal des vertus douteuses.  Ici, les salauds dansent heureux,  Les cœurs vendus, les mains soyeuses.  Leur morale est bien repassée,  Mais toujours un peu tachée.  [Refrain] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds, Des faux héros, des pantins d’ego,  Qui dansent, qui dansent sous les drapeaux,  Au bal, au bal des salauds!  C’est le temps des salauds, oh-oh,  Des beaux parleurs, des faux normaux,  Qui rient très haut… pour mentir plus beau.  [Couplet 1 – Le délire raisonnable] Le nouveau réalisme, c’est l’art des salauds,  Un délirium sobre, cynisme en costard chaud.  Ils vendent la peur sous cellophane,  Et t’appellent “extrême” si tu dis “humain”.  Ils posent des questions de sages,  Mais répondent comme des mirages sauvages.  Ils jouent à la raison...  mais raisonnent faux,  C’est la saison, la moisson des salauds.  [Refrain] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds,  Des faux héros, des cerveaux trop clos,  Qui dansent, qui dansent sous les drapeaux,  Au bal, au bal des salauds!  [Couplet 2 – Les alliances du vide] Trois types de salauds, faut l’dire clair:  Les politiques, les patrons, les faiseurs d’prières.  Ceux qui savent mais trahissent,  Eux les lâches, qui profitent.  Le p’tit Jupiter, Machiavel au moral,  Fait valser les foules dans son bal libéral.  Il pactise, il nuance, tord le vrai,  Pour qu’le faux paraisse sensé.  [Pont] Forts avec les faibles, faibles avec les forts,  Ils vendent la paix pendant qu’ils signent la mort.  “Bon courage”, qu’ils disent, le sourire faux,  Mais c’est un orage… on danse, salauds?  [Couplet 3 – Les fous et les faux] Les fous aboient, les salauds cadrent,  Et les cons signent tous les contrats.  Les uns hurlent, les autres calculent,  Et les lucides… se taisent, s’annulent.  Les idoles changent, les valeurs se vendent,  La foule like, la vérité s’attend.  Les héros sont devenus salauds,  Nous, figurants d’un online show.  [Refrain – Final] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds,  Des faux héros, des gros egos,  Qui valsent au rythme des fiascos,  Au bal, au bal des salauds! (oh-oh)  Au bal… des salauds.  [Outro] J’en ai aimé, des salauds, c’est vrai,  Leurs mots brillants, leurs airs parfaits.  Mais minuit sonne, le bal s’oublie,  Ces salauds-là ne dansent plus… avec ma vie.

description: Ce qui est marrant c'est que salaud au féminin, en français, c'est pas salaude! Ha, #justsayin Chanson inspirée par un vrai livre recent intitulé "Le Temp Des Salauds" 🍟🤓🤌  @bananasutra lyrics (variantions):  [Intro] Bienvenue, mesdames et messieurs,  Au grand bal des vertus douteuses.  Ici, les salauds dansent heureux,  Les cœurs vendus, les mains soyeuses.  Leur morale est bien repassée,  Mais toujours un peu tachée.  [Refrain] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds, Des faux héros, des pantins d’ego,  Qui dansent, qui dansent sous les drapeaux,  Au bal, au bal des salauds!  C’est le temps des salauds, oh-oh,  Des beaux parleurs, des faux normaux,  Qui rient très haut… pour mentir plus beau.  [Couplet 1 – Le délire raisonnable] Le nouveau réalisme, c’est l’art des salauds,  Un délirium sobre, cynisme en costard chaud.  Ils vendent la peur sous cellophane,  Et t’appellent “extrême” si tu dis “humain”.  Ils posent des questions de sages,  Mais répondent comme des mirages sauvages.  Ils jouent à la raison...  mais raisonnent faux,  C’est la saison, la moisson des salauds.  [Refrain] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds,  Des faux héros, des cerveaux trop clos,  Qui dansent, qui dansent sous les drapeaux,  Au bal, au bal des salauds!  [Couplet 2 – Les alliances du vide] Trois types de salauds, faut l’dire clair:  Les politiques, les patrons, les faiseurs d’prières.  Ceux qui savent mais trahissent,  Eux les lâches, qui profitent.  Le p’tit Jupiter, Machiavel au moral,  Fait valser les foules dans son bal libéral.  Il pactise, il nuance, tord le vrai,  Pour qu’le faux paraisse sensé.  [Pont] Forts avec les faibles, faibles avec les forts,  Ils vendent la paix pendant qu’ils signent la mort.  “Bon courage”, qu’ils disent, le sourire faux,  Mais c’est un orage… on danse, salauds?  [Couplet 3 – Les fous et les faux] Les fous aboient, les salauds cadrent,  Et les cons signent tous les contrats.  Les uns hurlent, les autres calculent,  Et les lucides… se taisent, s’annulent.  Les idoles changent, les valeurs se vendent,  La foule like, la vérité s’attend.  Les héros sont devenus salauds,  Nous, figurants d’un online show.  [Refrain – Final] C’est le temps, le temps des salauds,  Des faux héros, des gros egos,  Qui valsent au rythme des fiascos,  Au bal, au bal des salauds! (oh-oh)  Au bal… des salauds.  [Outro] J’en ai aimé, des salauds, c’est vrai,  Leurs mots brillants, leurs airs parfaits.  Mais minuit sonne, le bal s’oublie,  Ces salauds-là ne dansent plus… avec ma vie.

description: Because Gladys is my middle name, and "Sonder" is a magic feeling of knowing wonder--when each stranger you see is the main character of their own life, and you are merely an extra in their story... The word was coined by author John Koenig and first appeared in "The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows", a project that creates names for emotions that don't have one  🕳️🐇   Gipsy Burlesque Blues Dream @bananasutra EPx14 #lyrics (variations):  [Intro – Down the Rabbit Dream]  The curtain breathes smoke, the dream’s out of tune, Gladys sings sideways beneath the fool moon. Mister White Rabbit spins clocks out of thin sand, time melts in mirrors all over the land. The Chessshire Cat strips in a glitch ’n bitch show, Whispering, “Truth’s just a pathetic trick, meow.” And Gladys keeps falling, big heart in her hand, into the bassline bloom of Sonderland.   [Chorus 1 – The Dance of Sonder]  Gladys in Sonderland, dance out of line, chase that White Rabbit with a glass of wine. Truth traded by cocky kings and sons, Love is fool, woke… screw their whacky plans. Oh laugh, my loves, the joke’s still grand, we all fall slow in Sonderland.  [Bridge – The Burlesque of Empathy]  Contempt kills the courage meant to soothe, Fear builds a cage on a stage, proof. The Cat draws claws in nonsense sand, the Queen flips hearts like contraband. And Sonder sighs, and Gladys sings with the band: Love that sees, not love that blinds, unchains the demons from our minds.  [Final Chorus – The Carnival Crescendo] Gladys in Sonderland, lift up your mask, toast to the fools who dare to ask. White Rabbit’s gone, the clocks are banned, we measure love by gone grains of sand. So laugh, my loves, the truth’s divine, the heart’s a door, swing open wide. Gladys in Sonderland, you understand: we fall to rise, we blend to mend.  [Outro – The Curtain Closes, or Maybe Opens] The Queen wipes the blood from her wonder lips. The Cat hums an old stolen hymn, its grin dissolving from outside to in. Gladys stands amazed, champagne in her hand, and bows to the holes of Sonderland. She laughs… It’s absurd, but it’s hers, this plan, to lose herself just to understand… “Every fall’s a beginning; Blessed be holes, Son.”   🥂 🎶

Mister White Rabbit spins clocks out of thin sand, time melts in mirrors all over the land. The Chessshire Cat strips in a glitch ’n bitch show, Whispering, “Truth’s just a pathetic trick, meow.” And Gladys keeps falling, big heart in her hand, into the bassline bloom of Sonderland.   [Chorus 1 – The Dance of Sonder]  Gladys in Sonderland, dance out of line, chase that White Rabbit with a glass of wine. Truth traded by cocky kings and sons, Love is fool, woke… screw their whacky plans. Oh laugh, my loves, the joke’s still grand, we all fall slow in Sonderland.  [Bridge – The Burlesque of Empathy]  Contempt kills the courage meant to soothe, Fear builds a cage on a stage, proof. The Cat draws claws in nonsense sand, the Queen flips hearts like contraband. And Sonder sighs, and Gladys sings with the band: Love that sees, not love that blinds, unchains the demons from our minds.  [Final Chorus – The Carnival Crescendo] Gladys in Sonderland, lift up your mask, toast to the fools who dare to ask. White Rabbit’s gone, the clocks are banned, we measure love by gone grains of sand. So laugh, my loves, the truth’s divine, the heart’s a door, swing open wide. Gladys in Sonderland, you understand: we fall to rise, we blend to mend.  [Outro – The Curtain Closes, or Maybe Opens] The Queen wipes the blood from her wonder lips. The Cat hums an old stolen hymn, its grin dissolving from outside to in. Gladys stands amazed, champagne in her hand, and bows to the holes of Sonderland. She laughs… It’s absurd, but it’s hers, this plan, to lose herself just to understand… “Every fall’s a beginning; Blessed be holes, Son.”   🥂 🎶

description: Light me up, librarian lover… and "Read Me Harder" EPX19 📚💨 Side A x9 = Gypsy HopFi Fusion BURLESQUE Edition Side B x10 = Psychedelic Americana BLUES Edition  I was listening to my "S.S. is for Sacred Sp3rm" EP when I saw yet another one of those daily terrifying #breakingnews social media posts, listing #books recently #banned from the (remaining) U.S. Public Schools and Libraries #circa2025  1. The Handmaid’s Tale by Margaret Atwood 2. Brave New World, by Aldous Huxley 3. Fahrenheit 451 by Ray Bradbury 4. 1984 by George Orwell 5. To Kill a Mockingbird by Harper Lee 6. The perks of being a wallflower, by Stephen Chbovsky 7. The Bluest Eye by Toni Morrison  8. Sold by Patricia McCormick 9. Maus by Art Spiegelman 10. An African and Latinx History of the United States by Paul Ortiz  So then, I had to write a "B.B. is for BANNED BOOKS" song, to honor my favorite authors on this list, because WOW... HOW freaking SCARY of an #americanhorror #truestory IS THAT?!   ☆☆☆ @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro] They banned the truth for being rude… But baby, rude is how we bloom. So light me up, librarian lover… and read me harder. B.B. is for Banned Books, and Badass Brains.  [Verse 1 – Harper Lee & Art Spiegelman] Harper told me, “Mock me, kill me,” still I sing, Truth’s a mockingbird with wings. Art drew the pain, a mouse in flame, He said, “Remember, never tame.” You can ban my ink, but not my roar, I’ll scratch your walls, and write some more.  [Chorus] They banned the books but not the beat, Banned the thought but not the heat, Banned the love but not the street. So read me, baby, read me sweet! If thinking’s sin, I’ll take the blame, Desire and truth are one and same.  [Verse 2 – Aldous Huxley & Margaret Atwood] Aldous whispered, “Take your soma, stay asleep,” But sugar, freedom don’t come cheap. Atwood smirked, “Blessed be the fruit,” Then laced her boots and staged a coup. Pop your soma, hush your fear, But holy lust still lights us clear.  [Bridge – George Orwell & Ray Bradbury] Big Brother’s watching, Ray lit the spark, Said, “Burn the dark, not those who mark.” Orwell winked through smoke and steam, “Truth’s a thoughtcrime, love’s the dream.” You can’t delete what won’t forget, We’re the match they can’t reset.  [Final Chorus] They banned the books but not the beat, Banned the thought but not the heat, Banned the love but not the street. So read me, baby, read me sweet! Truth’s taboo, but damn, it’s neat, Come turn the page with me.  [Outro] For Harper Lee, Art Spiegelman, Aldous Huxley, Margaret Atwood, George Orwell, and Ray Bradbury, for every mind they tried to muzzle. We see you. We feel you. And we’ll keep reading you harder.

The perks of being a wallflower, by Stephen Chbovsky 7. The Bluest Eye by Toni Morrison  8. Sold by Patricia McCormick 9. Maus by Art Spiegelman 10. An African and Latinx History of the United States by Paul Ortiz  So then, I had to write a "B.B. is for BANNED BOOKS" song, to honor my favorite authors on this list, because WOW... HOW freaking SCARY of an #americanhorror #truestory IS THAT?!   ☆☆☆ @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro] They banned the truth for being rude… But baby, rude is how we bloom. So light me up, librarian lover… and read me harder. B.B. is for Banned Books, and Badass Brains.  [Verse 1 – Harper Lee & Art Spiegelman] Harper told me, “Mock me, kill me,” still I sing, Truth’s a mockingbird with wings. Art drew the pain, a mouse in flame, He said, “Remember, never tame.” You can ban my ink, but not my roar, I’ll scratch your walls, and write some more.  [Chorus] They banned the books but not the beat, Banned the thought but not the heat, Banned the love but not the street. So read me, baby, read me sweet! If thinking’s sin, I’ll take the blame, Desire and truth are one and same.  [Verse 2 – Aldous Huxley & Margaret Atwood] Aldous whispered, “Take your soma, stay asleep,” But sugar, freedom don’t come cheap. Atwood smirked, “Blessed be the fruit,” Then laced her boots and staged a coup. Pop your soma, hush your fear, But holy lust still lights us clear.  [Bridge – George Orwell & Ray Bradbury] Big Brother’s watching, Ray lit the spark, Said, “Burn the dark, not those who mark.” Orwell winked through smoke and steam, “Truth’s a thoughtcrime, love’s the dream.” You can’t delete what won’t forget, We’re the match they can’t reset.  [Final Chorus] They banned the books but not the beat, Banned the thought but not the heat, Banned the love but not the street. So read me, baby, read me sweet! Truth’s taboo, but damn, it’s neat, Come turn the page with me.  [Outro] For Harper Lee, Art Spiegelman, Aldous Huxley, Margaret Atwood, George Orwell, and Ray Bradbury, for every mind they tried to muzzle. We see you. We feel you. And we’ll keep reading you harder.

description: This EPx8 takes a walk around the blocks of Blues ❯ Folk ❯ Jazz ❯ LoFi ❯ Dub, to celebrate Hammy's move (and life) SHOWsutra style, because it's funny because it's true: Hammy (and his daddy, whose name is not Clyde haha) got a new house on Clyde Avenue. And so now, it's "Hammy On Clyde"!  ✪ ✪ ✪ @bananasutra lyrics:   [Intro] They say trouble walks on two legs… But mine’s got four, and loves to beg His name’s Hammy. Hammy on Clyde.  [Verse 1] He’s a brown-eyed bandit, a bed-hoggin’ prince Took one look, and I ain’t been sane since Floppin’ ears and a Gumby in his teeth Tryin’ to break that toy’s neck, sweet canine grief  Howlin’ at sirens now just for fun Waggin’ like no gangster owns a man He don’t talk, but you feel what he means With a wiggle and a woof and a pee on your jeans  [Chorus] That’s Hammy, Hammy on Clyde Flyin’ through the air with that swagger and slide Soft like a whisper, wild like a tide Needy, sweetie, king of the ride Yeah, he’s Hammy… Hammy on Clyde!   [Verse 2] He’ll follow his people with a rhythm so sweet Sniffin’ dreams off the sidewalk, and pissin’ on deceit Little dog, big soul, and a loyalty loud Waggin’ his tail on the beat, feelin’ proud  He’s got zoomies in his bones and jazz in his feet When he’s runnin’ the block, man, the rhythm’s complete Clyde’s his kingdom, the hydrants his throne And every blade of grass? Smells like home  [Chorus] That’s Hammy… Hammy on Clyde Guardian of snacks and neighborhood pride Got a bark like a rebel and a cuddle inside He’ll lick your face and steal your guide Yeah, he’s Hammy… Hammy on Clyde!   [Bridge] He ain’t no gangster, he’s better than that He’s a therapist in fur, with no baseball hat Wears a tail, and when it wags, silly, you’re healed No tricks, just treats. That’s the realest deal  [Final Chorus] That’s Hammy… Hammy on Clyde Love with no leash, mischief that don’t hide He’ll sniff out your sorrow, and walk by your side A four-legged legend you can’t override Oh Hammy… oh my Hammy on Clyde!   [Outro] So if you’re ever lost in San Rafael’s tide, Look out for a blond with a goofy stride Listen up for his paws And Gumby gone outlaw Doggy love pride! Hammy… on Clyde.  🐕 💦

description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

description: I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.   But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.   And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,  I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.  When did caring turn into crime?  Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,  But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.  If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?  Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.  Every love I add don’t steal your chains.  Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;  It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.  Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,  I feel that tremor every day.  But if walls keep empathy out of sight,  Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,  But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.  Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?  Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,  Two trembling souls with open hands.  My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;  It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.  It needs no borders, no tags.  Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,  Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?  Would you rather numb, or rather feel?  If trust could hum a new refrain,  Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.  Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.  Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,  ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?  We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.  Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,  It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

Walk the block, pay the rent, get stopped with no clues? If fairness was real, would you lose your place? Or would equality feel like you’re in second place?  [Bridge]  What’s the weight of a word when it’s not meant for you? What’s the cost of the dream when it don’t come true? If justice is blind, why she peeking through her mask? Here’s a question, baby, don’t be scared to ask.  [Hook] Tell me, tell me, is it in the mirror? Or hiding in the jokes when the room gets clearer? If love’s universal, why you drawing them lines? Bananasutra asking questions, messing with your mind.  [Outro] So what is racism, honey, is it yours, is it mine? Or just a ghost in the closet we pretend’s benign? Keep on asking, keep peeling the skin, ’Cause the fruit gets sweeter when the truth kicks in  ⁉️‼️🍌

description: This is a French (my mother tongue) EPx17 song for those who’d rather be awake than reassured—the ones who’d rather KNOW & GROW than BLOW & SHOW blindly, even if “Some Truths Are Harder to Swallow” 🍌💦  i.e. my BJ (banana joke:) sister-song of “L’Embobinage”…   The lyrics are rooted in one of Carl Sagan’s most haunting and relevant psychological insights:   “One of the saddest lessons of history is this:  If we’ve been bamboozled long enough, we tend to reject any evidence of the bamboozle. We’re no longer interested in finding the truth. The bamboozle has captured us. It’s simply too painful to acknowledge (even to ourselves) that we’ve been taken. Once you give a charlatan power over you, you almost never get it back.”  “Une des leçons les plus tristes de l'histoire est celle-ci: si nous avons été embobinés assez longtemps, nous avons tendance à rejeter toute preuve de l'embobinage. Nous ne sommes plus intéressés à découvrir la vérité. L'embobinage nous a capturés. Il est tout simplement trop douloureux de reconnaître, même pour nous-mêmes, que nous avons été dupés. Une fois que vous donnez du pouvoir à un charlatan sur vous, vous ne le récupérez presque jamais.”  It’s a story rooted in the GROWsutra spirit: a philosophy of fierce compassion, where curiosity is stronger than comfort, where questioning is a form of kindness, and where truth, though sometimes bitter, is ultimately the beginning of healing.  — Lyrics:   [Verse 1] Une des leçons les plus tristes de l’histoire, Est celle-ci, Carl Sagan nous a dit, Embobinés depuis longtemps, c’est illusoire, Chercher la vérité, c’est si troublant,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Verse 2] Difficile de reconnaître, Que nous avons été dupés, Le pouvoir au charlatan, Jamais récupéré,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Outro] La vérité, toujours elusive, Nous sommes capturés, l’embobinage nous tient, Le charlatan règne, et nous restons perdus.

description: This is a French (my mother tongue) EPx17 song for those who’d rather be awake than reassured—the ones who’d rather KNOW & GROW than BLOW & SHOW blindly, even if “Some Truths Are Harder to Swallow” 🍌💦  i.e. my BJ (banana joke:) sister-song of “L’Embobinage”…   The lyrics are rooted in one of Carl Sagan’s most haunting and relevant psychological insights:   “One of the saddest lessons of history is this:  If we’ve been bamboozled long enough, we tend to reject any evidence of the bamboozle. We’re no longer interested in finding the truth. The bamboozle has captured us. It’s simply too painful to acknowledge (even to ourselves) that we’ve been taken. Once you give a charlatan power over you, you almost never get it back.”  “Une des leçons les plus tristes de l'histoire est celle-ci: si nous avons été embobinés assez longtemps, nous avons tendance à rejeter toute preuve de l'embobinage. Nous ne sommes plus intéressés à découvrir la vérité. L'embobinage nous a capturés. Il est tout simplement trop douloureux de reconnaître, même pour nous-mêmes, que nous avons été dupés. Une fois que vous donnez du pouvoir à un charlatan sur vous, vous ne le récupérez presque jamais.”  It’s a story rooted in the GROWsutra spirit: a philosophy of fierce compassion, where curiosity is stronger than comfort, where questioning is a form of kindness, and where truth, though sometimes bitter, is ultimately the beginning of healing.  — Lyrics:   [Verse 1] Une des leçons les plus tristes de l’histoire, Est celle-ci, Carl Sagan nous a dit, Embobinés depuis longtemps, c’est illusoire, Chercher la vérité, c’est si troublant,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Verse 2] Difficile de reconnaître, Que nous avons été dupés, Le pouvoir au charlatan, Jamais récupéré,  [Chorus] L’embobinage nous a pris, Trop douloureux, la vérité, Nous avons été trahis, Le charlatan a pris pied,  [Outro] La vérité, toujours elusive, Nous sommes capturés, l’embobinage nous tient, Le charlatan règne, et nous restons perdus.

description: “Easy (Death Is Nothing At All)” is a rare #bowsutra song inspired by a quote about death, from Henry ScottHolland (27 January 1847 - 17 March 1918), a Regius Professor of Divinity at the University of Oxford:  "Death is nothing at all. It does not count. I have only slipped away into the next room. Nothing has happened. Everything remains exactly as it was. I am I, and you are you, and the old life that we lived so fondly together is untouched, unchanged. Whatever we were to each other, that we are still. Call me by the old familiar name. Speak of me in the easy way which you always used. Put no difference into your tone. Wear no forced air of solemnity or sorrow. Laugh as we always laughed at the little jokes that we enjoyed together. Play, smile, think of me, pray for me. Let my name be ever the household word that it always was. Let it be spoken without an effort, without the ghost of a shadow upon it. Life means all that it ever meant. It is the same as it ever was. There is absolute and unbroken continuity. What is this death but a negligible accident? Why should I be out of mind because I am cut of sight? I am but waiting for you, for an interval, somewhere very near, just round the corner. All is well."   ❣  ❣  ❣  @bananasutra lyrics:  [Verse 1] Never think I’m gone mon chéri, Hear me sing, feel the sweet sweet swoon, Everything’s just as it always be, I’ll be back with you real soon.  [Chorus] Breathe easy, baby, easy, Life means all it ever meant. Breathe slowly, deep, easy peasy, No need for grief, it’s love misspent.  [Verse 2] Hear me whisper your name, darling Sing it just the way we would. Death don’t need no solemn crying, Let it breathe just like it should.  [Chorus] Breathe easy, baby, easy, Life means all it ever meant. Breathe slowly, deep, easy peasy, No need for grief, it’s love misspent.  [Bridge] Please laugh like nobody is watching  Smile when you think of me. Nothing can ever kill our loving,  We’re as near as near can be.  [Verse 3] I am right here, feel me singing, Forever flying in time, Life’s a wild trip, never-ending, Dancing with the rhythm and rhyme.  [Chorus] I’m easy, oh, I’m easy, There’s no shadow, there’s no gloom. Breathe with me, let me make it easy, I’m right here with you, watch us bloom  [Outro] Oh, it’s easy… easy peasy… All is well, my dear, mon chéri…   ❣  ❣  ❣

description: “Easy (Death Is Nothing At All)” is a rare #bowsutra song inspired by a quote about death, from Henry ScottHolland (27 January 1847 - 17 March 1918), a Regius Professor of Divinity at the University of Oxford:  "Death is nothing at all. It does not count. I have only slipped away into the next room. Nothing has happened. Everything remains exactly as it was. I am I, and you are you, and the old life that we lived so fondly together is untouched, unchanged. Whatever we were to each other, that we are still. Call me by the old familiar name. Speak of me in the easy way which you always used. Put no difference into your tone. Wear no forced air of solemnity or sorrow. Laugh as we always laughed at the little jokes that we enjoyed together. Play, smile, think of me, pray for me. Let my name be ever the household word that it always was. Let it be spoken without an effort, without the ghost of a shadow upon it. Life means all that it ever meant. It is the same as it ever was. There is absolute and unbroken continuity. What is this death but a negligible accident? Why should I be out of mind because I am cut of sight? I am but waiting for you, for an interval, somewhere very near, just round the corner. All is well."   ❣  ❣  ❣  @bananasutra lyrics:  [Verse 1] Never think I’m gone mon chéri, Hear me sing, feel the sweet sweet swoon, Everything’s just as it always be, I’ll be back with you real soon.  [Chorus] Breathe easy, baby, easy, Life means all it ever meant. Breathe slowly, deep, easy peasy, No need for grief, it’s love misspent.  [Verse 2] Hear me whisper your name, darling Sing it just the way we would. Death don’t need no solemn crying, Let it breathe just like it should.  [Chorus] Breathe easy, baby, easy, Life means all it ever meant. Breathe slowly, deep, easy peasy, No need for grief, it’s love misspent.  [Bridge] Please laugh like nobody is watching  Smile when you think of me. Nothing can ever kill our loving,  We’re as near as near can be.  [Verse 3] I am right here, feel me singing, Forever flying in time, Life’s a wild trip, never-ending, Dancing with the rhythm and rhyme.  [Chorus] I’m easy, oh, I’m easy, There’s no shadow, there’s no gloom. Breathe with me, let me make it easy, I’m right here with you, watch us bloom  [Outro] Oh, it’s easy… easy peasy… All is well, my dear, mon chéri…   ❣  ❣  ❣

description: A wise and worldly amigo I know joked the imminent revival of the #dodo may save us (all:) from double negative doom by mad anti-antirhino stampede… and so I thought, oh boy yass, waltz me burlesque baby, THANK GOD "Hope Is So Do-Do-Dope" (ha) 🪗💨 #SHOWSUTRA soul circus time (x9)!   ⸻ @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro] They thought we were extinct, But baby, we just blinked. We flapped our wings in dreams unseen… Dodo’s back. And we’re keen.  [Verse 1] The rhinos march in rows of grey, Stompin’ facts and truth away. “Be like us,” they grunt and mope, But we got wings, and do-do-dope.  They call us soft, they call us slow, But flappin’ joy is how we grow. Our hope don’t bark, it flies and floats, Above their fear, we sing new notes.  [Chorus] Hope is so do-do-dope! Flip, flop, flap it, nope! Can’t squash love with fascist trope, ‘Cause hope is so… do-do-dope!   [Verse 2] They said we’d never come again, Too kind to fight, too sweet to win. But kindness cuts like mighty oak, And makes the hate machine go broke.  Empathy ain’t weak, my friend, It’s why we dare, it’s why we mend (oh whyyy whyyy) We speak up, why we joke, elope, For futures shaped by do-do-hope (that’s whyyy)  [Bridge] The ghosts of dodos whisper true: “Don’t let the rhinos trample you.” In the face of old fascist lies…  We must laugh, rise, and organize!  [Final Chorus] Hope is so do-do-dope! Truth don’t need a microscope. It’s mighty, silly, fool in scope, And hope is just… so do-do-dope!   Do-do-dope! Do-do-dope! History can’t dim our hope. Even when they stomp and grope… Hope is so do-do-dope!  ⸻  #hopeiseverything (they say;) and #silly #gratitude too!  And ain't that great, heh? 'Cause that's all I got for you boo... wooo :)

description: A wise and worldly amigo I know joked the imminent revival of the #dodo may save us (all:) from double negative doom by mad anti-antirhino stampede… and so I thought, oh boy yass, waltz me burlesque baby, THANK GOD "Hope Is So Do-Do-Dope" (ha) 🪗💨 #SHOWSUTRA soul circus time (x9)!   ⸻ @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro] They thought we were extinct, But baby, we just blinked. We flapped our wings in dreams unseen… Dodo’s back. And we’re keen.  [Verse 1] The rhinos march in rows of grey, Stompin’ facts and truth away. “Be like us,” they grunt and mope, But we got wings, and do-do-dope.  They call us soft, they call us slow, But flappin’ joy is how we grow. Our hope don’t bark, it flies and floats, Above their fear, we sing new notes.  [Chorus] Hope is so do-do-dope! Flip, flop, flap it, nope! Can’t squash love with fascist trope, ‘Cause hope is so… do-do-dope!   [Verse 2] They said we’d never come again, Too kind to fight, too sweet to win. But kindness cuts like mighty oak, And makes the hate machine go broke.  Empathy ain’t weak, my friend, It’s why we dare, it’s why we mend (oh whyyy whyyy) We speak up, why we joke, elope, For futures shaped by do-do-hope (that’s whyyy)  [Bridge] The ghosts of dodos whisper true: “Don’t let the rhinos trample you.” In the face of old fascist lies…  We must laugh, rise, and organize!  [Final Chorus] Hope is so do-do-dope! Truth don’t need a microscope. It’s mighty, silly, fool in scope, And hope is just… so do-do-dope!   Do-do-dope! Do-do-dope! History can’t dim our hope. Even when they stomp and grope… Hope is so do-do-dope!  ⸻  #hopeiseverything (they say;) and #silly #gratitude too!  And ain't that great, heh? 'Cause that's all I got for you boo... wooo :)

description: What happens “when everyone who is right becomes a rhinoceros?”—Eugène Ionesco   RHINOCEROSS EPx7 flows from LOFI ❯ INDIE ❯ DUB ❯ BLUES ❯ Psychedelic Punk ROCK finale 🤙  "A song on the far right lane, lookin’ out at a world that has gone insane"... inspired by the official death of #freedomofspeech in Murica, mass surrealist anti-antidelusion, blind binary conformity, and the stubborn hope to stay human when a horny herd stampedes 🦏💨  ♦ ♦ ♦  @bananasutra lyrics:  [Verse 1] Freedom of speech turned dust, Like good old trust gone bust, ‘Cause a felon got the horn,  Now evil’s grooming fools of scorn.  He smirks “blow me, babe, it’s bliss.” But(t) I ask “What kind of kiss starts with trampling consent and bursts on your shameless fist?”  [Chorus] Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Can I scream when I’m lost? When the herd walks off a cliff, Who’s counting the cost?  Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Is contempt embossed  in hearts hard like stone, like the love got tossed?  [Verse 2] What’s a “true self” if it bends? Why shift to fit in with fiends? Does an order mean it’s real? Are we doomed if we still feel?  Ducks grow tusks overnight, Brag they “finally sold the light.” But they reek of TV static, Stink of stunted logic.  [Chorus] Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Do you fear the truth? Or just like to squash us, And the future of youth?  Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Is a stampede proof? Or a meme with cold might, Out there in the dark night?  [Bridge] Am I stubborn... or sane? Is resistance... just pain? Can you laugh… with a horn? Can we hope?… Be reborn?…  Blessed be… Not forlorn?  [Verse 3] I see tantrums run,  Yassholes on the road, Their greed says “YOLO,”  And their ego mocks “no.”  I ask “but(t) ain’t love real?”  They say “ha, truth is a mask.” I ask “what’s the alternative?”  They snark “don’t ask.”  So now I’m sittin' with a song on the far right lane, Lookin’ out at a world that has gone insane. Like, is it just me, holy howling “us”, Like, what have we done, what happened to us, Did all the hope burn, hit by a hell bus?  [Chorus] Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Do we run or rot? If ‘em questions’ all we’ve got, Why’s silence so hot?  Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Are we what you’re not? Like ‘em fools turned ghouls, Where are the good souls, Who refuse greed’s plot?  [Outro] If everyone’s a beast… Who shall share… love’s feast? What’s left... of peace When trust’s… deceased?  ...Rhinoce...ros...  Rhinoce...ros...  ♦ ♦ ♦  PS: Did you know a rhinoceros is deadlier than a tiger 💁🏻‍♀️⁉️ (I bet Ionesco did know, meow) True story, statistically: a human’s chances to survive an encounter with tiger are significantly higher than with a rhinoceros... so now you know!

description: What happens “when everyone who is right becomes a rhinoceros?”—Eugène Ionesco   RHINOCEROSS EPx7 flows from LOFI ❯ INDIE ❯ DUB ❯ BLUES ❯ Psychedelic Punk ROCK finale 🤙  "A song on the far right lane, lookin’ out at a world that has gone insane"... inspired by the official death of #freedomofspeech in Murica, mass surrealist anti-antidelusion, blind binary conformity, and the stubborn hope to stay human when a horny herd stampedes 🦏💨  ♦ ♦ ♦  @bananasutra lyrics:  [Verse 1] Freedom of speech turned dust, Like good old trust gone bust, ‘Cause a felon got the horn,  Now evil’s grooming fools of scorn.  He smirks “blow me, babe, it’s bliss.” But(t) I ask “What kind of kiss starts with trampling consent and bursts on your shameless fist?”  [Chorus] Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Can I scream when I’m lost? When the herd walks off a cliff, Who’s counting the cost?  Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Is contempt embossed  in hearts hard like stone, like the love got tossed?  [Verse 2] What’s a “true self” if it bends? Why shift to fit in with fiends? Does an order mean it’s real? Are we doomed if we still feel?  Ducks grow tusks overnight, Brag they “finally sold the light.” But they reek of TV static, Stink of stunted logic.  [Chorus] Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Do you fear the truth? Or just like to squash us, And the future of youth?  Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Is a stampede proof? Or a meme with cold might, Out there in the dark night?  [Bridge] Am I stubborn... or sane? Is resistance... just pain? Can you laugh… with a horn? Can we hope?… Be reborn?…  Blessed be… Not forlorn?  [Verse 3] I see tantrums run,  Yassholes on the road, Their greed says “YOLO,”  And their ego mocks “no.”  I ask “but(t) ain’t love real?”  They say “ha, truth is a mask.” I ask “what’s the alternative?”  They snark “don’t ask.”  So now I’m sittin' with a song on the far right lane, Lookin’ out at a world that has gone insane. Like, is it just me, holy howling “us”, Like, what have we done, what happened to us, Did all the hope burn, hit by a hell bus?  [Chorus] Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Do we run or rot? If ‘em questions’ all we’ve got, Why’s silence so hot?  Rhiii-no-ce-rosss! Are we what you’re not? Like ‘em fools turned ghouls, Where are the good souls, Who refuse greed’s plot?  [Outro] If everyone’s a beast… Who shall share… love’s feast? What’s left... of peace When trust’s… deceased?  ...Rhinoce...ros...  Rhinoce...ros...  ♦ ♦ ♦  PS: Did you know a rhinoceros is deadlier than a tiger 💁🏻‍♀️⁉️ (I bet Ionesco did know, meow) True story, statistically: a human’s chances to survive an encounter with tiger are significantly higher than with a rhinoceros... so now you know!

description: If this song got you shrugging, smirking, or squirming, man, please pause... and tell me why?   🩸🩸🩸  @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro]   They say it’s “too much.”   Too bloody.   Too messy.   Too loud.   Too real.   So I ask…  [Verse 1]   Why’s it taboo to talk of blood,   When half the world’s got cycles that flood?   Why’s it shameful to name a cramp,   But not to wave a warlord’s stamp?  Why is “discharge” more feared than lies?   Why do men squirm while a woman dries—   her tears, her womb, her sleepless nights,   while they debate her basic rights?  [Chorus]   Taboo for who?   Who made the rules?   Who taught us shame   in sterile schools?   It ain’t biology that’s the crime—   It’s silence weaponized through time.    Taboo for who?   'Cause I’m not scared—   I’ll sing what’s real   since they don’t dare.  [Verse 2]   Why is menopause met with a shrug,   while old white men get pills to plug   their shriveled pride with pharma might,   but women sweat through silent nights?  Why is "hormonal" used as a slur,   when the whole damn system *depends* on her?   Why don’t they teach us bone will thin?   Why ain’t that in the doc’s quick spin?  Why is a womb a ticking clock   unless it births, then it’s forgot?   Why is my pain dismissed as flair—   while men’s complaints get urgent care?  [Bridge]   It’s not taboo 'cause it’s grotesque,   it’s taboo 'cause it shows who’s next.   It shows resilience, mess, and might—   and that’s what gives the boys a fright.  [Interlude]   Let’s be honest.   It’s not about discomfort.   It’s about control.   And they’re losing it.  [Final Chorus]   Taboo for who?   I call your bluff.   Your squeamish pride?   Ain’t good enough.   This ain’t shame—it’s sacred truth.   It’s guts and fire and ancient proof.  Taboo for who?   I name the cost—   Of every silence   and line we’ve crossed.   So take your fear and go regroup—   the grown-up talk is in this loop.  [Outro]   If it makes you flinch,   it probably matters.

tags: philosophy, joseph campbell, truth, metaphor, religion, critical thinking, faith, burlesque, jackicorn
description: Another KNOWsutra EP, with 12 variations of 3 old songs, about truth and religion—inspired by this quote from the (brilliant, deep, subtle, and lovely) one and only Joseph Campbell: "Every religion is true one way or another. It is true when understood metaphorically. But when it gets stuck in its own metaphors, interpreting them as facts, then you are in trouble"... because, oh boy, ain't that true, heh Murica?! ;)  @banasutra lyrics x3:  — (V1) Metaphor’s Edge  [Verse 1] On the edge of belief, we teeter and sway, Caught between fact and the words we obey. But a story untold is no story at all, Yet frozen in truth, it leads to our fall.  [Chorus] Oh, take the edge, the metaphor’s kiss, Find the meaning that others may miss. Don’t get stuck in the riddle’s disguise, For only the open can truly be wise.  [Verse 2] Wolves in the sheep’s clothes, prophets of gold, Tell you the gospel, but the message grows cold. The tale is the journey, not the walls that confine, To walk with the wind is to walk with the divine.  [Chorus] Oh, take the edge, the metaphor’s kiss, Find the meaning that others may miss. Don’t get stuck in the riddle’s disguise, For only the open can truly be wise.  — (V2) Sacred Shadows  [Verse 1] Whispers in the dark, they speak of heaven’s gate, A tale so ancient, but twisted by fate. We worship the shadows, forget what they’re for, In the light of the moon, we must search for more.  [Chorus] When the sacred becomes stone, the spirit slips away, You’ll lose the dance of night for the brightness of day. But it’s in the shadow that truth comes to play, Hold the sacred as fluid, don’t let it decay.  [Verse 2] The stars above speak in riddles, in shapes we misread, We build temples of answers, but they’re just what we need. To feel safe in the chaos, to feel known in the void, But if you make it concrete, all the magic’s destroyed.  [Chorus] When the sacred becomes stone, the spirit slips away, You’ll lose the dance of night for the brightness of day. But it’s in the shadow that truth comes to play, Hold the sacred as fluid, don’t let it decay.  — (V3) The Song of the Universe  [Verse 1] Every story’s got a secret, hiding in plain view, It’s a mirror for your soul, shaping what you knew. But you’ll drown in deep illusion, if you take it word for word, When metaphors become the law, meaning gets blurred.  [Chorus] Oh, the trouble with truth, when it’s set in stone, Is that it loses its mystery, leaves you all alone. Dance with the shadows, don’t hold on too tight, For the song of the universe shines in metaphor’s light.  [Verse 2] Priests and prophets, saints and fools, all walk the same line, But the more they cling to “truth,” the further from divine. The symbols are the guideposts, not the end of the road, But some mistake the map for the meaning it showed.  [Chorus] Oh, the trouble with truth, when it’s stuck in the past, Is that it forgets it’s a tale, not a spell meant to last. Dance with the shadows, don’t hold on too tight, For the song of the universe shines in metaphor’s light.
