description: Another KNOWsutra EP, with 12 variations of 3 old songs, about truth and religion—inspired by this quote from the (brilliant, deep, subtle, and lovely) one and only Joseph Campbell: "Every religion is true one way or another. It is true when understood metaphorically. But when it gets stuck in its own metaphors, interpreting them as facts, then you are in trouble"... because, oh boy, ain't that true, heh Murica?! ;)  @banasutra lyrics x3:  — (V1) Metaphor’s Edge  [Verse 1] On the edge of belief, we teeter and sway, Caught between fact and the words we obey. But a story untold is no story at all, Yet frozen in truth, it leads to our fall.  [Chorus] Oh, take the edge, the metaphor’s kiss, Find the meaning that others may miss. Don’t get stuck in the riddle’s disguise, For only the open can truly be wise.  [Verse 2] Wolves in the sheep’s clothes, prophets of gold, Tell you the gospel, but the message grows cold. The tale is the journey, not the walls that confine, To walk with the wind is to walk with the divine.  [Chorus] Oh, take the edge, the metaphor’s kiss, Find the meaning that others may miss. Don’t get stuck in the riddle’s disguise, For only the open can truly be wise.  — (V2) Sacred Shadows  [Verse 1] Whispers in the dark, they speak of heaven’s gate, A tale so ancient, but twisted by fate. We worship the shadows, forget what they’re for, In the light of the moon, we must search for more.  [Chorus] When the sacred becomes stone, the spirit slips away, You’ll lose the dance of night for the brightness of day. But it’s in the shadow that truth comes to play, Hold the sacred as fluid, don’t let it decay.  [Verse 2] The stars above speak in riddles, in shapes we misread, We build temples of answers, but they’re just what we need. To feel safe in the chaos, to feel known in the void, But if you make it concrete, all the magic’s destroyed.  [Chorus] When the sacred becomes stone, the spirit slips away, You’ll lose the dance of night for the brightness of day. But it’s in the shadow that truth comes to play, Hold the sacred as fluid, don’t let it decay.  — (V3) The Song of the Universe  [Verse 1] Every story’s got a secret, hiding in plain view, It’s a mirror for your soul, shaping what you knew. But you’ll drown in deep illusion, if you take it word for word, When metaphors become the law, meaning gets blurred.  [Chorus] Oh, the trouble with truth, when it’s set in stone, Is that it loses its mystery, leaves you all alone. Dance with the shadows, don’t hold on too tight, For the song of the universe shines in metaphor’s light.  [Verse 2] Priests and prophets, saints and fools, all walk the same line, But the more they cling to “truth,” the further from divine. The symbols are the guideposts, not the end of the road, But some mistake the map for the meaning it showed.  [Chorus] Oh, the trouble with truth, when it’s stuck in the past, Is that it forgets it’s a tale, not a spell meant to last. Dance with the shadows, don’t hold on too tight, For the song of the universe shines in metaphor’s light.

description: "Truth Don't Care (What You Believe)" is an EPx2 of another good old KNOWsutra Cabaret song, for a world gone bananas... The song’s lyrical rhythm is inspired from the song “One” by U2, and the following late night lill’ stream of consciousness dreamt out loud:  “Truth is agnostic, it does not judge nor segregate, it DGAF about trends, niches, or genres, or metaphors. Truth is like the old, quirky odd lore, often found shining deep in dark closets. Truth is like the ultimate psychedelic paradox, said Joseph Campbell. And it’s made of an infinite spectrum of awe and wow, said Mary Oliver...  and your god ain’t truer than mine is no shallow b-roll drama, you know? I mean, who knows? All I know I know is I dunno, I’m just imagining… the best kind of truth likes to explore, embrace, and share—to learn, laugh, and waltz... Truth shines warm bright far beyond the shades, across the spectrum of music…”   — @bananasutra lyrics:   [Verse 1] Truth don’t care what you believe Don’t take sides, don’t need to please It don’t bow to gold or kings Don’t owe a damn thing to history  [Chorus] Is it truth… or just the light you see? Is it truth… or just the words you read? Spinning round, like an old fairground Hold on now, you’re upside down…  [Verse 2] Truth ain’t shy, it loves to waltz Laughs in the dark, don’t mind the faults A paradox, a riddle told By Joseph Campbell, Mary’s gold  [Chorus] Is it truth… or just the shade you cast? Is it truth… or just reflections past? Spinning round, like an old fairground Close your eyes, now hear the sound…  [Bridge] Your god ain’t truer than mine No shallow b-roll drama I mean, who knows? All I know I know is I dunno… (…I’m just imagining… imagining… imagining…)  [Outro] Truth don’t pick sides Truth don’t play nice Truth don’t dim for your eyes Truth just shines… —  PS: "Being at ease with not knowing is crucial for answers to come to you."—Eckhart Tolle

description: Blaise Pascal "Pensées" were clear: ‘the end rarely justifies the means’... that is one of the good old French sayings I grew up with, and imho, it very much matters. Yet, Americans often like to declare "the end justifies the means (wink wink)" 🤠  That always felt like offensive logic to me, ominous uninformed hubris, i.e. a meaningful cautionary tale about a slippery slope--a big red flag that contradicts common good sense, by letting big bad bullies get away with (sh)it—basically  🚩🚩🚩  “Blaise’s Tale” is a 3-song KNOWsutra EP for lovers of truth, wisdom, and a little playful rebellion in music. It tells the story of (my dear, French) Blaise Pascal’s rationale, his humanist philosophy and moral clarity... with one earnest folk confession, some hypnotic banjo shuffles in between, and a cheeky grand burlesque finale. Enjoy  🎶  ⭐︎ ⭐︎ ⭐︎  @bananasutra lyrics:  Verse 1 Why listen to Blaise? What did he see? What could a mathematician mean to me? Did he glimpse a truth beyond the veil, Or just another cautionary tale? He warned us all with words so plain, That justifying ends brings only pain.  Chorus From Rome’s collapse to the Soviet night, We’ve learned it’s not the ends that make it right. Napoleon’s pride to Mao’s dread might, Blaise’s words cut through the fright. Ends don’t justify the sordid route, They just leave doubt and disrepute.  Verse 2 Think of the Puritans, so stern, so grand, With bibles clenched in ruthless hands. They claimed a holy, just campaign, But left a legacy of pain. Or look at Caesar, Julius bold, His ends were clear, his means were cold.  Bridge What makes us think that we can change, The lessons learned on history’s stage? Each violent act, each reckless plea, Just echoes down through eternity.  Chorus From Rome’s collapse to the Soviet night, We’ve learned it’s not the ends that make it right. Napoleon’s pride to Mao’s dread might, Blaise’s words cut through the fright. Ends don’t justify the sordid route, They just leave doubt and disrepute.  Outro So ask yourself, my friends tonight, What truly makes a wrong thing right? Is it the end we think we know, Or is it how we choose to go? Oh, Blaise was right, so clear, so keen, The end rarely justifies the means. ⭐︎ ⭐︎ ⭐︎

tags: Psychedelic, post-punk, burlesque rock, bff, blessed be, dogs, pep talk, gratitude
description: The more I use the SUTRAS in my daily life, the more I find them helpful—they not only allow me to increase my own awareness (of my intent, perspective, and focus or priority at a given point in time), they also allow me to influence my thoughts and feelings, by rooting them into a chosen, conscious mindset, to better regulate and balance my moods… and this song is a great example of me doing just that.  Originally written as a mellow trip-hopy BOWsutra song, a humble reflection on unconditional love and the concept of death, this adaptation of the song shifts the energy into SHOWsutra and FLOWsutra—to honor the wild love and lighthearted fun flowing energy dogs aka our BFFs bring into our lives, forever ❤️‍🔥   This song is like a mighty power punk rock pep talk reminding me/us balls matter, and “Grass is for pooping, and also rolling” LOL ;)  — ​⁠ @bananasutra  lyrics  [Verse 1] Oh, the wagging tail's like a sermon in motion, The nose in the wind, a lesson in devotion. They give us patience, they show us trust, They teach us to sniff before making a fuss. Oh, why rush? Why stress? When every breeze is a brand-new guest?  [Chorus warm, kind, quirky] Blessed be the dogs! They know, they blow, they grow, they glow. Blessed be the show! Dogs love, dogs live, dogs let it flow.  [Verse 2] They say, “Watch with your balls, listen with your nose, “Every tree’s a story, and puddle got prose.” “Grass is for pooping, and also rolling” “And a belly-up rub in the sun is the best thing" “Don’t hold a grudge, don’t waste the fun” “Chase what you love, watch your balls run!”  [Chorus] Blessed be the dogs! They know, they blow, they grow, they glow. Blessed be the show! Dogs love, dogs live, dogs let it flow.  [Bridge] Life is a game of fetch my heart Throw it far, far, make it an art Chasing no fame, not asking why Sniffing the ground… I swear, it's nearby.  Patience in a wag, Pardon in the bag, And gratitude, dog attitude That’s a full-body wiggle of joy like love leaped in the middle, oh boy.  [Final Chorus] Blessed be the dogs! They know, they blow, they grow, they glow. Blessed be the show! Dogs love, dogs live, dogs let it flow.  (Let it flow… Let it flow…)  ☰☰☰

description: This EPx16 crosses the symbolic mark of 1000 original tracks released on SoundCloud, in one year. So, YAY. It's worth acknowledging, because I am just sooo grateful for being able to process my feelings with songs. And god knows there is indeed much to process, in a world gone bananas. I considered making the 1000th track special, but I’m not that special, really ;)  This is Vol. 02 of a song I love, “How do Kids Learn Now?” aka “When did seduction become so Untrue?”, a sonic question mark wrapped in 16-track Flamenco Techno journey made of lit Gipsy soul, Arabesk minimalism, flamenco fire, and wonder… asking: What are we teaching? Who profits from forgetting? What is lost when respect is mocked and liberty becomes a loophole? And why (TF) should we care?  This song is yet another opportunity and invitation to embrace reflection and growth, to help us understand and navigate a world where perspectives differ… With hypnotic claps, poetic whispers of truth in rhythm. KNOWsutra songs are my philosophical foundation, and intended to invite wonder, and self-reflection, even when it's uncomfortable—vs. retreat and deny. It asks questions that matter, with an emphasis the importance of kids being able to learn how to differentiate rights from wrongs—as required to foster trust, and a long-term peaceful, sustainable, harmonious future, for everyone on planet Earth.  It matters to me because my faith, my commitment to kindness and honesty, is a significant part of who I am, and I care to understand who we are as humans, and how we can positively impact the world around us, to make it a better place… In a society where the moral compass is so blurred, covert narcissists charlatans like #robertgreen make  millions of dollars selling a book that teaches the  “The Art of Seduction” literally means “The Art of Manipulation” aka Deception, a reality where power grab and control have come to matter more than integrity, humility, and trust… despite what all regarded history, philosophy, economy, sociology, psychology, and of course poetry scholars know—which is that being vulnerable is being brave, because peace grows from trust, and trust relies on honesty, quite simply.  — @bananasutra lyrics:  [Verse 1] How do kids learn respect and fraternity? Morality means we agree on rights and wrongs, can’t you see? Liberty now means no accountability, The new victors boast, proud in their spree.  [Chorus] Freedom’s shadow, where did we stray? Liberty twisted, lost on the way. Respect and fraternity, fading from view, When did seduction become so untrue?  [Verse 2] Selling lies, saying attraction’s just a ruse, Deceit for dollars, making souls confused. Boasting takers, proud of deceit, But what’s the cost, where does truth meet?  [Chorus] Freedom’s shadow, where did we stray? Liberty twisted, lost on the way. Respect and fraternity, fading from view, When did seduction become so untrue?  [Bridge] We need to find the way back, clear and pure, Teach kids respect, make fraternity sure. Stand for liberty, rewrite the tale, Bring back values, let truth prevail.  [Chorus] Freedom’s shadow, where did we stray? Liberty twisted, lost on the way. Respect and fraternity, fading from view, When did seduction become so untrue?  [Outro] Restore the values, end manipulation’s reign, Teach respect, embrace compassion again.

description: This EPx16 crosses the symbolic mark of 1000 original tracks released on SoundCloud, in one year. So, YAY. It's worth acknowledging, because I am just sooo grateful for being able to process my feelings with songs. And god knows there is indeed much to process, in a world gone bananas. I considered making the 1000th track special, but I’m not that special, really ;)  This is Vol. 02 of a song I love, “How do Kids Learn Now?” aka “When did seduction become so Untrue?”, a sonic question mark wrapped in 16-track Flamenco Techno journey made of lit Gipsy soul, Arabesk minimalism, flamenco fire, and wonder… asking: What are we teaching? Who profits from forgetting? What is lost when respect is mocked and liberty becomes a loophole? And why (TF) should we care?  This song is yet another opportunity and invitation to embrace reflection and growth, to help us understand and navigate a world where perspectives differ… With hypnotic claps, poetic whispers of truth in rhythm. KNOWsutra songs are my philosophical foundation, and intended to invite wonder, and self-reflection, even when it's uncomfortable—vs. retreat and deny. It asks questions that matter, with an emphasis the importance of kids being able to learn how to differentiate rights from wrongs—as required to foster trust, and a long-term peaceful, sustainable, harmonious future, for everyone on planet Earth.  It matters to me because my faith, my commitment to kindness and honesty, is a significant part of who I am, and I care to understand who we are as humans, and how we can positively impact the world around us, to make it a better place… In a society where the moral compass is so blurred, covert narcissists charlatans like #robertgreen make  millions of dollars selling a book that teaches the  “The Art of Seduction” literally means “The Art of Manipulation” aka Deception, a reality where power grab and control have come to matter more than integrity, humility, and trust… despite what all regarded history, philosophy, economy, sociology, psychology, and of course poetry scholars know—which is that being vulnerable is being brave, because peace grows from trust, and trust relies on honesty, quite simply.  — @bananasutra lyrics:  [Verse 1] How do kids learn respect and fraternity? Morality means we agree on rights and wrongs, can’t you see? Liberty now means no accountability, The new victors boast, proud in their spree.  [Chorus] Freedom’s shadow, where did we stray? Liberty twisted, lost on the way. Respect and fraternity, fading from view, When did seduction become so untrue?  [Verse 2] Selling lies, saying attraction’s just a ruse, Deceit for dollars, making souls confused. Boasting takers, proud of deceit, But what’s the cost, where does truth meet?  [Chorus] Freedom’s shadow, where did we stray? Liberty twisted, lost on the way. Respect and fraternity, fading from view, When did seduction become so untrue?  [Bridge] We need to find the way back, clear and pure, Teach kids respect, make fraternity sure. Stand for liberty, rewrite the tale, Bring back values, let truth prevail.  [Chorus] Freedom’s shadow, where did we stray? Liberty twisted, lost on the way. Respect and fraternity, fading from view, When did seduction become so untrue?  [Outro] Restore the values, end manipulation’s reign, Teach respect, embrace compassion again.

description: “Oh My, Oh Why” Yet another song (I love and) I’m overdue to share—lyrics inspired by and dedicated to one of my fav philosophical (they say;) daddy aka #socrates (sentenced to death over 2000 years ago, for encouraging youth to ask questions, true story, bro) <3  @bananasutra lyrics:   He walked the square with bare, bold feet, Asked kings and fools what made life sweet, He said, “I know I know nothing—ain’t that true?” The priests grew pale, the jury stiff, He smiled and offered them a gift: “I’d rather die than lie like you do.”  [Chorus] Oh my, oh why, Is truth the crime they crucify? They feared the light, So they closed their eyes… Oh my… oh why.  He questioned pride, exposed the game, Showed power cloaked in noble names, Asked “Who decides what’s wise and what’s taboo?” They called him mad, they called him curse, But feared his calm, his clever verse— A mirror’s worse than any sword can do.  [Chorus] Oh my, oh why, Do cowards choose to dignify The mask, the lie— Then claim it’s divine? Oh my… oh why.  [Bridge] He didn’t run. He didn’t beg. He sipped the cup. He stretched his leg. “The soul lives on,” he gently said, “and cowards die in beds.”  So here I sing, beneath the stars, A song for truth, for sacred scars— For every soul who’d rather burn than bow. We carry him in every breath, Each time we choose the honest death, Each time we dare to live out loud.  [Final Chorus] Oh my, oh why, They silenced him, but not his cry… It echoes still Where questions lie— Oh my… Oh why?

description: DEFY is a soul-deep, whispered scream BLOWsutra EP in 7 Tracks, which started with one question: “What are we doing?”  That’s the question @defiance13 asked in a heartfelt #TikTok monologue that cracked something in me. He was not being not rhetorical—he was being real. Caring. Conscious. Raw. Clear. Bright. Informed. Logical. Ethical. Philosophical. Outraged. Defiant. And I weeped, silently, in empathy. He sounded like Hope, with a capital H, like, just Human.  This EP is what came out of sitting with that question. Not answers, but grief. Not slogans, but songs.Three core truths, seven different renderings of them—raw and low, no sweetening. Just me, my conscience, and my lyrics. Because lyrics matter. Because denial is poison. Because silence isn’t neutral. And defiance ain’t optional.  The first song [track 1-2], “Shameless,” opens with the bitter contrast between past fascism and its modern American rebrand. Because that’s right, back then, the horrors were hidden—curtained, whispered, denied. Now? They’re streamed in HD with hashtags and lawn chairs. Cages rise from the swamp, and people cheer for suffering like it’s a half-time show. It’s not about subtle policies or gray areas, it’s about social media. It’s a freaks spectacle, people who decorate detention centers with patriotism.  The second song [track 3-5], “Optics of Cruelty,” calls out the calculated aesthetics of power. It’s not a glitch—it’s the blueprint. As the original monologue says, “You’re not witnessing the echoes of history, you’re watching its reanimation.” This track goes straight into the rot of performance-based fascism. It names names, connects dots, quotes sources, maps connections, and asks: when did control become our national art form? When did cruelty become a campaign style?  And the third [track 6-7], “Universal Currency,” is the hardest to sing. It’s a quiet scream for the children—those who die in floods, in heat, in systems designed to forget them. It’s about how this country penciled out the price of a child’s life—just under $109,000—and still dared to call it justice. But children are not budget lines. They’re our only true wealth. And the exchange rate is human decency.  Each version of these songs brings out a slightly different truth—one more bluesy, one more folk, one more hypnotic or theatrical. They’re not remixes. They’re re-feelings. This is not background music. It’s not a brand. It’s basically just my gut’s voice... And if you're wondering too, what (TF) are we doing, then maybe these songs are for you too. Because defiance, when nothing else is left, is love’s last language.  ✰ ✰ ✰ ✰ ✰   Lyrics gladly shared upon request.

description: Cassandra’s Lullaby is an EPx11 that blends Jewish jazz, gypsy dub, and trip-hop into a sparse, analog landscape of truths denied and raw emotions... It’s a haunting, mythical torch song for the age of forgetting, a poetic letter to a friend, and a warning to the world. Written with an aching heart, it feels ethereal yet grounded, and echoes like a lullaby from the edge of fasc!st history, drifting through conscience and consequence.  @bananasutra lyrics:  I didn’t ask for the visions, love. Like worst comes to shove. Like gas in the chambers, Like blood in muddy waters, Where truth gets drowned So the lie seems profound.  Seventeen million ghosts Already branded lost. Their names ignored, Their fate uncarved, And your silence? Deafening. History’s repeating But nobody’s caring. It’s all so damn unnerving.  You said, “Good luck riding that kind of shit feeling…” Yeah (bro). Thanks for the healing.  [Chorus] Sleep, my darling, through the sirens. Fold your conscience. Close your eyes. I’ll keep singing through the violence, Cassandra weeps while hope denies.  You call it “bad energy,” Like joy forgives atrocity, While the empire builds its ovens In your denial’s high heavens.  They roll in the wooden horse While my voice grows coarse. Tell me again how killing Explains your chilling?  [Chorus] Sleep, my darling, through the sirens. Fold your conscience. Close your eyes. I’ll keep singing through the violence, Cassandra weeps while hope denies.  This isn’t me dimming, my dear, It’s me screaming, clear. It’s déjà poo, It’s shame on you. It’s hell, backlit by data. Genocide in beta. The echo of Remember Adolf, Now met with a shrug… Well, Heil! Good luck with that drug.  I see our future’s shared grave And long for friends who dare be brave. Not cowardly lies Draped in red, white, and blue… As the friendly dies, And fascism comes true.  [Final Chorus] Sleep, my darling, sleep in numbers. Sleep through fascist lullabies. I’ll pray that grace breaks through your slumber, And helps the world unclose its eyes.  May your heart unclose with grace… And prove you’re more than a fart’s face.

description: This unfinished song is about George Carlin’s “7 Dirty Words” comedy bit, back in the early 70s, when TV was a new thing, and “Freedom of Speech” already, well huh, like a joke… as many artists and news producer and broadcaster learned the hard way then, as a result of sudden, arbitrary, and brutal governmental censorship.  My (and probably George’s too) favorite quote in this story came from (Supreme) Justice Stewart who, when asked to specify what exactly characterized a “profane, offensive word”, boldly and coldly declared: “I know it when I see it” … aka #supremeshit (*)! That’s what George went on to call out in his bold and hot way: the shocking hypocrisy of Supreme Court Justices, refusing to acknowledge the (lack of) of clarity and transparency of the new laws banning “profanities” from broadcast radio and television.  What’s striking to me is that, despite major technological progress, life (the universe, and everything:) is mostly the same… because we live in a world where most men fear to live in truth, and sadly, humanity remains at the mercy of rich, entitled, mostly white men characterized by a dire, unholy need for control, and heavy duty levels of contempt for transparency and accountability, in the name of democracy and justice aka #winwin games… Men as unable to acknowledge their own shortcomings, as unashamed to defend the hypocritical logic of unclear, unfair laws—men who tend to always “muddy the waters to make it seem deep”, as Nietzsche wisely observed.   *yet another proof some “things don’t change”,  and “it gets better” is a nice thing to say, but also often just cheap, shallow crap… Please pass the ironic grains of salt… and blessed be George Carlin!  — @bananasutra lyrics:  “7 Dirty Words”  Banjo strumming, a quirky tune, George Carlin’s words, under the moon. description: “Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers—Build your hope on reason’s stairs.”  I love this song very much, and am overdue to share it :) It was inspired by a bold and brilliant essay Bertrand Russell wrote in 1929 (and for fool disclosure, Bertrand is my all-time favorite philosopher, and was also a renowned mathematician; if you're curious, I recommend you check out "The Conquest of Happiness"). His essay aims to answer a question I've asked myself for as long as I can remember, an important one: “Has Religion Contributed Anything Useful to Civilization?”   His answer? Not really—and certainly not uniquely.... long story short, here's what he concludes: * Compassion doesn’t require dogma. * Progress thrives on questions, not creeds. * Morality rooted in obedience is not morality—it’s fear in disguise.  He believed humanity could find meaning, ethics, and joy through reason, science, and humanism—no gods or thrones required. This song echoes that spirit: a love letter to curiosity, courage, and clarity. A little irreverent, a lot sincere.  --- @bananasutra “Reason Over Reverence” fool lyrics ✨  They built the heavens with fear in the sky, Promised salvation but told us to die. The weight of the world, they placed on their knees, But truth grows in questions, not in decrees.  [Chorus] Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers, Build your hope on reason’s stairs. No need for gods to find what’s true, The light of love is born in you.  They called it wisdom to silence dissent, Made a virtue of guilt and a sin of content. But knowledge is freedom, unchained by creed, No dogma required to learn how to lead.  [Chorus] Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers, Build your hope on reason’s stairs. No need for gods to find what’s true, The light of love is born in you.  No eternal fire, no thrones on high, Just the vast unknown where truths collide. We walk the earth with curious eyes, Finding meaning where wonder lies.  [Chorus] Raise your mind to the stars, not your prayers, Build your hope on reason’s stairs. No need for gods to find what’s true, The light of love is born in you.  So let’s build a world where all can explore, Free from the chains of the dogma of yore. For in the search, not the faith, we’ll find, The beauty of life and the power of mind.  ⭐︎⭐︎⭐︎

description: I'm no religion lover... but like all good Christians, I do my best to keep an open heart and flexible perspective (haha). description: This BLUES to JAZZ to DUB to Cello INDIE to gratitude MANTRA GROWsutra EP is for humans who carem and dare to be brave... and sometimes may even "weep, just knowing dogs exist"! Fair warning: it makes my heart howl, loud and long and deep inside :)   Lyrics inspired by a friend who triggered the (good:) remembering of my WOW feelings as a teenager, after reading Herman Hesse's fabulous tale of the "Steppenwolf"--a powerfool story of not knowing yet knowing, that despair is as glorious as laughter, and tender wonder is simply everything!   I also want to dedicate this one to Lotus (the dog:), and my 2 all-time favorite women in the entire world, Alev and Celinha, who happened to meet in Istanbul tonight. They sent me sincere tender love, and I really felt it! And so now, I just want to take a minute to share how much I care for them, too, even if I'm not always the best at sharing it. I believe they know I care, but I want to write it here anyway, because it's alway a good idea to remember what we remember we feel, and... description: Feel the riddim, and let poetry carry you, it will set you free <3  @bananasutra(i) lyrics:  Question me, if you feel the need   But poetry, yeah—it’s food, it’s seed   It’s that voice inside, don’t chase the feed   Only found in soul, where the real ones bleed    Truth-tellin’, when the world feelin’ shaky   Expression deeper than what they make me   In times where the viral feel so empty   Poetry slow burns—soft, deadly    No trend, no brand, just spirit alive   A low voice echo in this dubwise tribe   Not for show, nah—not for fame   But to name the ache and sing the flame    [Chorus]   Poetry, love—it’s necessity   Like roots in ground, like rice and tea   It humbles me, makes me see   In a world so loud—it sets me free    All due respect to the creeds and towers   To hierarchies, gods, and ivory powers   But this here, this voice, this vulnerability   Is the only thing that truly carry me    See—poetry don’t wear no disguise   It sit in wounds, it look in eyes   It rise when safety’s nowhere near   It speak the holy things we fear    [Chorus]   Poetry, love—it’s necessity   Like rhythm and smoke, like memory   It brings us close, makes us believe   In a language deeper than what we see    It fights back hard—against division   It cracks the lies, the cold precision   It builds in silence, burns tradition   It’s love, it’s rage, it’s intuition    No revenge, no pride to defend   Just bridges built that never end   Across the lines they say divide   I find the awe in every stride    [Chorus]   Poetry, love—it’s necessity   Not some artform, it’s therapy   It’s touch, it’s taste, it’s clarity   It’s what they miss in their prosperity    You feel it when it hit you raw   No filter, no pose, no law   It sings us back to where we came   No ego—just fire, soul, and name    Love is god, and music’s the choice   But poetry, woman, that’s my voice   Low and smoky, steady and slow   Just one riddim, deep and low

need (ha) To connect, beyond the standardization of narcissism  To resist the homogenization of global capitalism  With all due respects to churches and pyramids,  Christian creed, Maslow’s universal hierarchy of needs, And the importance of all indeed deemed a necessity, (I believe) It is in vulnerability, with little or no safety no stability That poetry thrives, bare, humble witness of our holy fragility   (I believe) It’s about balancing capitalistic dehumanization To foster empathy, celebrate alterity  To learn through to the voice of others,  To trust in our own transformative powers   (I believe) It’s about denouncing narcissistic manipulation To resist dark forces of division To exist above their toxic oblivion  To share meaning, brave discussions  (I believe) It’s about ending cycles of doom and revenge,  To live with nothing to prove, no ego to avenge To build more bridges beyond artificial divides,  To find the magic and awe in everyone’s stride   You know it when you see to grow our sacred individuality, our soul, dignity  A chance to bow , to celebrate, life, all the damn beauty

chispa original   Que sólo en la individualidad es real    Ahora es trabajo esencial, en tiempos de incertidumbre   Un acto humano que no se puede suplantar   Explorar, compartir lo que es vivir,   Cuando lo viral se vuelve mercancía al azar    (Creo) La poesía importa, como comer o sembrar   Hoy más que nunca, la necesitas para conectar (ajá)   Más allá del narcisismo estandarizado   Contra el capital global uniformado    Con todo respeto a iglesias y pirámides,   El credo cristiano y la pirámide de Maslow   Y todo lo que se dice que necesitamos,   (Creo) que es en la vulnerabilidad donde florece el alma    Sin certeza, sin suelo, sin red ni seguridad   La poesía respira frágil y sagrada verdad   Testigo desnudo de lo humano,   Una voz humilde, que nos tiende la mano    (Creo) Se trata de contrarrestar la deshumanización   Fomentar empatía, celebrar la alteridad   Aprender desde voces ajenas   Confiar en el poder de transformar nuestra identidad    (Creo) Es denunciar manipulación narcisista   Resistir las fuerzas que dividen y corrompen   Existir por encima del olvido tóxico   Compartir sentido, abrir la conversación    (Creo) Se trata de acabar con ciclos de odio y venganza   Vivir sin pruebas, sin ego, sin balanza   Construir puentes sobre grietas falsas   Y ver magia en cada paso de esperanza    Lo sabes cuando la ves, cuando fluye   Esa voz poética, cruda, que influye   Canta sentido, conexión y asombro   Y a veces hasta hace vibrar el corazón hondo    (Creo) Porque capta texturas humanas profundas   Pinta belleza en diferencias fecundas   Más allá de cañones y culturas   No es disfraz, es verdad sin censura    Es lenguaje humilde hecho de lo diario   Que demuestra ser sagrado y necesario   Llena el vacío de una voz que abraza   Como que amar es dios, y cantar no se rechaza    (Creo) Por eso la poesía es necesidad   Un medio, un lenguaje para esta nueva edad   Un camino al alma, la dignidad   Un canto de vida, belleza y verdad

Creo    Cuando el alma se parte en silencio   Y no hay verdad en la televisión   Llega la voz que canta en la sombra   Desnuda y sin permiso ni razón    Creo   Creo en la poesía   La que duele   La que guía    No es un lujo ni fantasía   Es pan, es tierra, es respirar   Una llama que en lo hondo brilla   Cuando todo empieza a fallar    Creo   Creo en lo que arde   En lo frágil   En lo grande    No hay templo más sagrado   Que una voz que se confiesa   Ni sistema tan cuadrado   Que no tiemble con belleza    No me hables de pirámides   Ni de normas por cumplir   Prefiero un verso sin abrigo   Que se atreva a compartir    Creo   (Y tú también lo sientes)   Creo   (En lo que no se vende)    Cuando el mundo se hace ruido   Y el amor se da en like   La poesía no hace ruido   Pero te atraviesa igual    Es raíz, es resistencia   Es un puente sin control   Es mirar al otro y verse   Es dolor hecho farol    Creo   (Creo en lo invisible)   Creo   (Lo simple es lo invencible)    Una voz quebrada canta   Y se escucha en cada piel   Y aunque el mundo no la entienda   Es semilla, es laurel    Creo   (Creo en lo que salva)   Creo   (Creo en la palabra)    Creo   Creo   (Creo...)

description: "Because the Light" @bananasutra lyrics rhythmically inspired by Patty Smith’s “Because the night” song… but(t) about a world where "success" requires most be shamelessly ruthless, and disasters pretend to be "natural", so glory seems hopelessly gory... and then, in that strange reality, "madness" ain't always badness, on the contrary-just ask #cypresshillbillies  PS: the butterflies are dead too, it's all a bloody joke ha #sorrynotsorry  — @bananasutra lyric V1 “Delete Your Butt”  Take me now, the world’s insane, Glory’s gory, soaked in pain, Ruthless dreams, they rule the show, “Natural” disasters—what a joke, you know.  (Chorus) Because the night belongs to shameless, Because the fight rewards the nameless, Because the light pretends it’s painless, Delete your butt, no hope, no greatness. (…)  — @bananasutra lyric V2  “Because the Joke”  Take me now, in this cruel disguise, Where “success” and lies, they compromise, Ruthless hearts, they rise, no shame to feel, While disasters fake their spinning wheel. description: EPx3 - VOL. 02  Robert Burns wrote “A Man’s a Man for A’ That” over 200 years ago, and guess what… not much has changed! In fact, it is statistically fair to say that the socio—economical divide is getting worse everyday, because greedy and entitled a-holes confuse privilege with rights, and don’t even think twice about the meaning or value of equality, human dignity, and justice. Blessed be Burns for daring to say what few would: wealth and status mean nothing—what truly matters is a person’s integrity, wisdom, and kindness. Personality, aka our “true color”, is so underrated…   Why his song matters: - In an era of rising inequality, where wealth and fame often overshadow true worth, Burns’ words remind us that status does not define a person. - As leaders and elites gain power through privilege, not merit, his message calls us to value wisdom, honesty, and justice above empty authority. - In a world that too often divides people by class, race, or borders, A Man’s a Man for A’ That stands as a timeless call for fairness, unity, and human dignity.  Burns saw beyond his time and envisioned a world where honor and intelligence, not gold and crowns, define greatness. That dream isn’t just history—it’s still worth singing for. Maybe now more than ever.  -- Robert Burns’s original lyrics: (Original Scots Version) Is there for honest Poverty That hings his head, an’ a’ that? The coward-slave, we pass him by, We dare be poor for a’ that! For a’ that, an’ a’ that, Our toils obscure, an’ a’ that, The rank is but the guinea’s stamp, The man’s the gowd for a’ that. What though on hamely fare we dine, Wear hoddin grey, an’ a’ that? Gie fools their silks, and knaves their wine, A man’s a man for a’ that: For a’ that, an’ a’ that, Their tinsel show, an’ a’ that; The honest man, though e’er sae poor, Is king o’ men for a’ that. Ye see yon birkie, ca’d a lord, Wha struts, an’ stares, an’ a’ that; Though hundreds worship at his word, He’s but a coof for a’ that: For a’ that, an’ a’ that, His ribband, star, an’ a’ that, The man o’ independent mind, He looks an’ laughs at a’ that. Then let us pray that come it may, (As come it will for a’ that,) That Sense and Worth, o’er a’ the earth, Shall bear the gree, an’ a’ that. For a’ that, an’ a’ that, It’s coming yet for a’ that, That man to man, the warld o’er, Shall brothers be for a’ that.  @bananasutra lyrics adaptation:  Is there a man who walks with pride, Though poor and worn, and all that? The coward bows, but we’ll abide, We dare be free for all that. For all that and all that, Our toil and sweat and all that, The crown is but a stamped disguise, A man’s a man for all that. What if our table’s plain and bare, Our coats are thin, and all that? Let fools delight in silks so rare, A man’s a man for all that. For all that and all that, Their pomp and gold and all that, An honest heart and mind so free, Are worth far more than all that. You see that man they call a lord, Who struts and stares and all that? Though many bow before his word, He’s but a fool for all that. For all that and all that, His stars and stripes and all that, A man who stands with mind unchained, He laughs and walks past all that. So let us hope the day will come, (And come it will, for all that,) When sense and worth, not birth and gold, Shall lead the world, and all that. For all that and all that, It’s coming yet, for all that, That man to man, both far and wide, Shall brothers be for all that.

"(I Wanted to Be a) Poem" is an experimental jazzy psychedelic song I wrote around the quote “I thought I wanted to be a poet but basically, I wanted to be the poem”; it is lyrically structured after the song “Summertime”, and directly inspired by the following essay about Jaime Gil de Biedma—an introverted, humble poet who lived under the Franco dictatorship, during the Spanish Inquisition (early last century)…  - “Perhaps poetry is best minted under pressure. Poetry that lasts. (...)  Jaime Gil de Biedma lived under Franco. Born in 1929 in Barcelona, Biedma was six when Federico Garcia Lorca was killed by Franco’s troops in Granada. Famously, the story goes that as they shot Lorca his murderers said: “Three shots in the ass for Garcia Lorca for being a faggot.” His body was never found. (…)  Silence carves these poems. He wrote his poems under a dictator who was famous for saying, “You are master of what you don’t say.” Maybe all poems are carved by silence. Think Dickinson. Think Hopkins. Silence can equal life. Here silence is particularly historic in a way it no longer is. Franco shut Spain up. The ground rich with unidentified corpses. Homosexuality denied in a regime that aligned itself with the conservative Catholic Church.  But poetry. Poetry provides a passport to transcendence when pressures seem unsurmountable: and more than thrice a poetry created under pressure in silence trumps death.  As Biedma began to put pen to paper, what preceded him was daunting. All the major poets had vanished: Machado on a death march, Lorca shot, Hernandez dead in prison, Cernuda fled to Mexico and never returned. Decades rolled on, censorship reigned, and torpid inertia smothered art. (...)  Poetry remains indestructible. Poetry outlasts Franco and AIDS. So long as men and women can breathe museums will preserve artifacts and a poet like Biedma will add to the record of what life was like under oppression.”

Antagonistic Intentions, working against, Abstracted Innuendo, no common sense.  [Verse 3] Alienated Indifference, feeling apart, Anomalous Inconsistency, tech with no heart. Arcane Intelligence, knowledge so rare, Automated Insensitivity, does it care?  [Chorus] Country tales of A.I., in a digital dream, Advanced Indifference, not as it seems. Alternative Intelligence, breaking the mold, Assisted Incompetence, stories unfold.  [Outro] Arbitrary Interpretation, no clear view, Country tales of A.I., what will we do? In a world of circuits, in a sea of code, These are the stories, that we’ve been told.

description: I figured out why dogs' lives are so (too) short... it's because (unlike parrots, for example) they are indeed humans BFF, so they volunteered to teach us the hardest lesson of life, i.e. death.  #TLDR  Song #2 was inspired by Leonard Cohen's "Like a Bird in the Sky" poem, song #1 and 3 by the following quote on the holy topic #death:  “Death is nothing at all. It does not count. I have only slipped away into the next room. Nothing has happened. Everything remains exactly as it was. I am I, and you are you, and the old life that we lived so fondly together is untouched, unchanged. Whatever we were to each other, that we are still. Call me by the old familiar name. Speak of me in the easy way which you always used. Put no difference into your tone. Wear no forced air of solemnity or sorrow. Laugh as we always laughed at the little jokes that we enjoyed together. Play, smile, think of me, pray for me. Let my name be ever the household word that it always was. Let it be spoken without an effort, without the ghost of a shadow upon it.  Life means all that it ever meant. It is the same as it ever was. There is absolute and unbroken continuity. What is this death but a negligible accident? Why should I be out of mind because I am cut of sight? I am but waiting for you, for an interval, somewhere very near, just round the corner. All is well.”—Henry Scott Holland (27 January 1847 - 17 March 1918), who was Regius Professor of Divinity at the University of Oxford  This quote is so beautiful, and I feel strongly that, f dogs could talk, that is basically what they would tell us. To be fair, I know I’m biased, because see, I’m “one of those” child-free lady, with love to spare, and an absolute sucker for dogs, of course. And I mean that, all of them!   True story... the mere sight of a dog instantly (and invariably) lowers my blood pressure, it's just like magic anxiety relief to me, for as long as I can remember. I never ever tire of scratching their but, their belly, or behind their ears—whatever they prefer. And, more importantly, I believe dogs (not humans) taught me the most important things one needs to understand, remember, and practice, in order to live “a good life”… for example, how being curious, humble, sensitive, loyal, playful, optimistic matters. Or, how accepting death is an important part of life, but(t) also like “nothing at all”, really.   There's a story I like to share, about dog and death, with humans sharing the grief they feel or about the loss of their BFF... in fact, it is one of my all-time favorite philosophical learning stories, because it’s basedon first-hand experience, and feels as meaningful as helpful. And, like all my favorite stories, it starts with a question: have you ever wondered why (oh why) did God (*) decide Parrots should live an average of 7 or 8 decades, but dogs (aka the universal humans BFF) only get to live one decade, never more than two?   With all due respects to single-parrots-turned-pain-in-the-butt-quacks (like most love-less narcissistic creatures on earth lol), I've been haunted by this question many times. But guess what... I eventually figured it out, thanks to my first hospice dog (a female border collie named Millie, who looked just like the dog on this EP cover). So, I'll share: it’s because one of the most important “jobs” of a BFF’s is to speak the hard truth(s), to help us understand what is most difficult, i.e. to help us GROW, FLOW, GLOW, and BOW (aka the most glorious aspects of a life worth living, as sung in my Bananasutra Bible)…   Morale of the story: in the light of love, death is nothing at all, and Henry Scott Holland sure was a fine dog!   (*) I use this word liberally, for anything I'm inclined to bow to, in awe, and gratitude

description: Another cheeky song inspired by a wise philosopher, and what my bananasutra project really is all about: “Make your Own Bible. Select and collect all the words and sentences that in all your readings have been to you like the blast of a trumpet.”--Ralph Waldo Emerson  ...  this EP x6  series starts with my respects to tradition with a good old Folk song, followed by a soulful Burlesque LOFI cruise on chill French accordion and jazzy HOP LOFI waves 🕊️ 📖 🎺✨  -- @bananasutra lyrics + #aivoice on #sunomusic  Verse 1 I searched for God in the Holy Book, But all I found was a preacher’s hook. I built my church in my own mind, No pews, no rules, just words that rhyme.  Chorus Make your own Bible, take your own stand, A trumpet blast, a marching band! In the gospel of me, I’ll be my own man, Dancing alone, but with the whole band.  Verse 2 I read Nietzsche and Sartre with a glass of red, Hemingway and Camus in my bed. Why follow rules from the days of old? I’ll craft my truth in stories bold.  Chorus Make your own Bible, write your own song, Find where you’re right, admit when you’re wrong. In the gospel of me, I’ll sing my own tune, Howl at the stars, and laugh at the moon.  Bridge Life’s a cabaret, a cheeky little dance, Between fate and free will, a game of chance. No need for a savior, no holy decree, Just the jazz in my soul, setting me free.  Chorus Make your own Bible, dance with your doubts, Whisper your secrets, and scream them out loud. In the gospel of me, I’ll find my own truth, Lost in the rhythm, defying my youth.  Outro So let’s write our scriptures, line by line, In the book of our lives, it’s all divine. No priest, no prophet, just the words that we speak, In this holy cabaret, the strong and the meek.

description: United World Statistics Bible Bros Dunno: the infant mortality rate in the “United States” is significantly worse than in any other western country—that is true before and after the Abortion law reversal, and (obviously…) only getting worse. In fact, for additional perspective, the infant mortality rate in Felon Nation is so bad, it is worse than in Cuba. This is so shockingly tragic… I can’t even find any “irony” in this story. And so, I keep wondering… Pro-life Means What, Honey?  -- @bananasutra lyrics (from the bottom of my heart)   Hmm… pro-life means what, honey?   Speak your truth, make it plain to me,  Or is it just smoke, a broken decree? They cry “pro-life,” but what do we see?  Schools underfunded, no equity.   Health’s a privilege, not a right to claim,  Tell me, darlin’, who’s to blame?  You save a life, but at what cost?  Who accounts for the human lost?  [Chorus]  Oh, the irony cuts so deep,  Pro-life dreams you’ll never keep.  Laws that crush, hearts in pain — Can’t you see it’s all in vain?  These laws they make—they’re cold, absurd,  Dismissing truth in a woman’s word.  Why’d our rights get whittled down?  Freedom fading in every town.   And where’s that man who sowed the seed?  Is accountability not what we need?   Are you chasing light, or is it control?  'Cause fear and lies only take their toll.  So tell me now, honey, pro-life means what?  A question too big to leave in the dust.  [Chorus]  Oh, the irony cuts so deep,  Pro-life dreams you’ll never keep.  Laws that crush, hearts in pain —Can’t you see it’s all in vain?  Think it through, take a breath, sit still,  Whose soul is saved, whose life you kill?  So I’ll ask again, honey, pro-life means what?  Speak it true, or hold that thought

description: I'm a child-free lady, but I care about living with joy and integrity,  in peace. I care for you, and your kids' future... and truth be told,  in an barely educated world that glorifies bullies (like Felon Nation, for example) bananas make less and less sense, damn it! I mean, I wonder, how on earth are kids supposed to learn and understand rights and wrongs now?!...   That's why I made the original ABC of Kindness song, for the kids (A Is For Always Speak From Your Heart, INDIEsutra). But(t) then I realized, DUH! At this point, adults are so brainwashed by the loud authoritarian capitalist bullies out there, they're actually just as confused, probably even more! So, I channeled my dear friend Bob Marley and made more ABC songs for everyone--namely, A Is For Apologize, and A Is Ask (how can I help).  I'll add the corresponding lyrics later, because if the goal is to contribute to the KNOWsutra chapter of my bible, and help the kids KNOW what matters, that would def be the right thing to do... I'm only human tho, and I apologize for being lazy  :)

description: Another song for our Public Domain Revolution inspiration collection, and my tribute to Victor Hugo’s French revolutionary spirit—its poignant poetry, and adamant urgency…  (In)Famous lines (translated from French): "And, standing proud, my soul shall tell / The tyrants of the earth—farewell!"   Original French Text: Liberté (1821) – Victor Hugo  Gloire à toi, Liberté! toi dont le temple immense Est bâti dans les cieux sur l'éternelle loi! L'homme est fait pour ton culte, et dans son cœur immense Tu dois régner comme un dieu-roi. Gloire à toi! Déjà l'ombre a fui devant l'aurore, Déjà sous d'autres cieux l'éclair luit, Et l'avenir, couvert de lumière sonore, Sort du tombeau de cette nuit. Levez-vous! peuples nus, esclaves des despotes! Brisez vos fers! le jour est pur! Peuples! à vos bourreaux, à leurs lois scélérates Opposez la justice et l'azur! Que votre front s'éclaire aux feux de la tempête! Que l’orage ouvre enfin vos yeux! Que dans le grand combat, sous la foudre honnête, Votre cri soit juste et glorieux! Ah! que vois-je? Ils se lèvent! ô sublime armée! Debout sous l'étendard vivant! Et moi, debout aussi, mon âme enflammée Dira: aux tyrans de la terre—adieu!  @bananasutra lyrics, i.e. my poetic English translation, channeling Bob, for the People:)  Liberty  Glory to you, O Liberty!—your boundless temple Rises in the heavens, built on eternal law! Man was made to serve you, and in his mighty heart You must reign as a god, in awe. Glory to you!—Already the shadows flee the sunrise, Already under distant skies the lightning glows, And the future, crowned with roaring light, Rises from the grave where darkness grows. Rise up, ye naked peoples—slaves of tyrant masters! Break your chains! The day is bright! People! To your butchers, to their wicked laws, Oppose but justice and the sky’s clear light! Let the storm’s fire ignite your brow with fury! Let the tempest open your eyes at last! That in this righteous battle, beneath honest thunder, Your cry be noble, fierce, and vast! Ah!—What do I see? They rise!—O sublime army! They stand beneath the living flag once more! And I, standing proud, my soul aflame, Shall tell the tyrants of the earth—farewell forevermore!

description: Robert Burns wrote “A Man’s a Man for A’ That” over 200 years ago, and I'm not gonna lie, he made me cry a little... Because guess what, not much has changed, we are reliving the same bull over and over! Arrogance is a sign of stupidity, and it matters, maybe more than ever.   Burns was inspired by the Scottish Enlightenment and the democratic ideals of his time, but I think the song’s message transcends history, politics, and borders. It is not about a revolution through violence, but about dignity through truth. It is a call for character to outweighs privilege and power, in a world gone bananas... Sound familiar? ;)   In the United Sates, it is statistically fair to say that the socio—economical divide is only getting worse everyday, because greedy and entitled a-holes confuse privilege with rights, and don’t even think twice about the meaning or value of #equality, human dignity, and justice. (RIP, Equal Opportunity Employment Act, 1965-2025). This song matters no matter your skin color... and blessed be Burns for daring to say what few would: wealth and status mean nothing—what truly matters is a person’s integrity, wisdom, and kindness. Personality, aka our “true color”, is so underrated…   So, WHAT is he saying that matters heh?  - Wealth and Rank Are Just an Illusion – Social status is just a stamp on a coin; real worth comes from the gold within—our character and deeds. -  Dignity in Hard Work – Whether rich or poor, those who live honestly and work with purpose are kings in their own right. - Power Does Not Equal Wisdom – A man may wear ribbons and medals, but that doesn’t make him great—wisdom and strength of mind do. - Hope for a Just Future – Burns believed that one day, justice and reason would win, and that all people, regardless of class or background, would stand as equals. - A Vision for Universal Brotherhood – The song’s most famous line, “That man to man, the warld o’er, shall brothers be for a’ that”, is a call for unity, compassion, and human dignity across nations.  Burns saw beyond his time and envisioned a world where honor and intelligence, not gold and crowns, define greatness. That dream isn’t just history—it’s still worth singing for. Maybe now more than ever.  And, WHY care? Because it's your story too...  - In an era of rising inequality, where wealth and fame often overshadow true worth, Burns’ words remind us that status does not define a person. - As leaders and elites gain power through privilege, not merit, his message calls us to value wisdom, honesty, and justice above empty authority. - In a world that too often divides people by class, race, or borders, A Man’s a Man for A’ That stands as a timeless call for fairness, unity, and human dignity.  —  @bananasutra original lyrics adaptation:   Is there a man who walks with pride,  Though poor and worn, and all that?  The coward bows, but we’ll abide,  We dare be free for all that.   For all that and all that,  Our toil and sweat and all that,  The crown is but a stamped disguise,  A man’s a man for all that.  What if our table’s plain and bare,  Our coats are thin, and all that?  Let fools delight in silks so rare,  A man’s a man for all that.   For all that and all that,  Their pomp and gold and all that,  An honest heart and mind so free,  Are worth far more than all that.  You see that man they call a lord,  Who struts and stares and all that?  Though many bow before his word,  He’s but a fool for all that.   For all that and all that,  His stars and stripes and all that,  A man who stands with mind unchained,  He laughs and walks past all that.  So let us hope the day will come,  (And come it will, for all that,)  When sense and worth, not birth and gold,  Shall lead the world, and all that.   For all that and all that,  It’s coming yet, for all that,  That man to man, both far and wide,  Shall brothers be for all that.

description: In the bananasutra bible, Sundays are for celebrating with silly humble #gratitude aka GLOWsutra days. Song inspired by and dedicated to the kindly fabulous women glowing up San Francisco Hippie hill, hair flowers flying in the air, agnostic drums circles prayers, curious music makers, mellow trance dancers, and the lyrical rhythm of the magical Jacque Brel "Dans le Port D'Amsterdam" song <3   -- @bananasutra lyrics  Up a San Francisco hill, There are hippies puffing, Teaching kids how to roll, Up one sans le bowl.  Up a San Francisco hill, There’s a poet who dreams, Of a world bathed in love, Under starlight streams. There’s a poet who sleeps, While the sidewalks hum beats, From a busker’s guitar, To the lovers they greet.  [Chorus] And oh, they’ll laugh, they’ll dance, To the tambourine’s trance. With their hands in the air, Flowers tangled in their hair.  Up a San Francisco hill, There's a painter who sighs, Dipping brushes in sunsets, Under tie-dyed skies. And the sweet scent of dreams, Mixed with jasmine and sage, Whirls like clouds in the park, Where the old poets age.  And they drink, and they sing, To the moon on the wing. "Peace and love for us all," The rallying call.  [Chorus] And oh, they’ll laugh, they’ll chant, With the joy that they grant. Under eucalyptus trees, In the city of the free.  Up a San Francisco hill, There’s a dancer who spins, With the grace of the wind, And the freedom within. As the bongo drums pound, She sways to the sound, And her movements declare, "Every soul is profound."  Up a San Francisco hill, The sun starts to glow, And the hippies all rise, With the city below. They'll march hand in hand, Through the morning's sweet chill, Chasing dreams, planting seeds, Up a San Francisco hill.

description: Blessed be lucid hearts 🥜  "I did the math and everything is stupid,"   Peanuts said with a heart so lucid.    If life’s a dance, who wrote the tune?   Do stars rehearse under the moon?   Is a peanut a nut or just a ruse,   Like love—a game you sometimes lose?    Do you know, "What’s the point of a kite?"   Idiots shouts, "You're never right!"   But the birds chirp with wings in flight,   "Why not fall and still take delight?"    [chorus]   Oh, everything is stupid, absurd, and divine,   A joke and a puzzle with no punchline.   We scribble in crayons on life’s dotted line,   Dreaming of chocolate, pretzels, and wine.    If clouds can cry, do they feel joy?   Do dogs philosophize or just destroy?   Why does Snoopy type but never talk?   Is a silent howl the purest thought?    Children cling to their blanket tight,   Light, "Faith’s a hug on a sleepless night."   Wit floats over a haze of dirt,   "Even messy hearts still work."    [chorus]   Oh, everything is stupid, absurd, and divine,   A dance and a stumble at the same time.   We trip on a pun, but the fall feels fine,   Spilling our dreams like spilled wine.    Why does the sunset end the show?   Are answers just questions we’ll never know?   Snoopy sighs on his doghouse throne,   "Stupid or wise, we’re never alone."    "I did the math and everything is stupid,"   Children laughed, 'cause maybe it’s Cupid.   Absurdity’s sweet when the heart stays lucid,   "I did the math and everything is stupid."

description: “The Weary Blues” is a poem in the public domain, by Langston Hughes (1901 – 1967) <3 -- Droning a drowsy syncopated tune, Rocking back and forth to a mellow croon,      I heard a Negro play. Down on Lenox Avenue the other night By the pale dull pallor of an old gas light      He did a lazy sway . . .      He did a lazy sway . . . To the tune o’ those Weary Blues. With his ebony hands on each ivory key He made that poor piano moan with melody.      O Blues! Swaying to and fro on his rickety stool He played that sad raggy tune like a musical fool.      Sweet Blues! Coming from a black man’s soul.      O Blues! In a deep song voice with a melancholy tone I heard that Negro sing, that old piano moan—      "Ain’t got nobody in all this world,        Ain’t got nobody but ma self.        I’s gwine to quit ma frownin’        And put ma troubles on the shelf." Thump, thump, thump, went his foot on the floor. He played a few chords then he sang some more—      "I got the Weary Blues        And I can’t be satisfied.        Got the Weary Blues        And can’t be satisfied—        I ain’t happy no mo’        And I wish that I had died." And far into the night he crooned that tune. The stars went out and so did the moon. The singer stopped playing and went to bed While the Weary Blues echoed through his head. He slept like a rock or a man that's dead.

description: Another short EP mixing genres of vocal honey, including 2 hip hop/LOFI tracks (whoop whoop :) -- @bananasutra lyrics inspired by Bertrand Russel, who wrote:  “Marriage is for women the commonest mode of livelihood, and the total amount of undesired sex endured by women is probably greater in marriage than in prostitution.” (Marriage and Morals)  Are prostitution and traditional marriage interconnected by hypocritical societal structures and discriminatory economic dependency? Bertrand makes the controversial yet fairly objective argument that marriage often prioritizes financial stability and social status over love, mirroring prostitution’s very transactional nature, and critiques the rigidity of marital norms, such as lifelong exclusivity and fidelity, which often stifle desires and lead to unmet physical, emotional, and spiritual needs... What if prostitution was required as a societal “release valve” for repressed desires, existing mostly as the condemned counterpart to marriage? What if the very notion of "ethical paradox" was an absurd oxymoron that never seems to end indeed? I ponder...  More importantly (Bertrand asks), why not think of marriage as a relationship based on equality, respect, and personal freedom? Could practicing truth, and trust, with humility and integrity, help reduce foul plays--including society’s reliance on femmes de joie for example? Well d'uh, heck yeah!   And if you're doubting the value of Bertrand's kind and wise questions, I bet you didn't you know marital r⭐︎pe was A-OK legal in almost ALL countries of the world until the mid-90s (!), for example...

description: Another short EP mixing genres of vocal honey, including 2 hip hop/LOFI tracks (whoop whoop :) -- @bananasutra lyrics inspired by Bertrand Russel, who wrote:  “Marriage is for women the commonest mode of livelihood, and the total amount of undesired sex endured by women is probably greater in marriage than in prostitution.” (Marriage and Morals)  Are prostitution and traditional marriage interconnected by hypocritical societal structures and discriminatory economic dependency? Bertrand makes the controversial yet fairly objective argument that marriage often prioritizes financial stability and social status over love, mirroring prostitution’s very transactional nature, and critiques the rigidity of marital norms, such as lifelong exclusivity and fidelity, which often stifle desires and lead to unmet physical, emotional, and spiritual needs... What if prostitution was required as a societal “release valve” for repressed desires, existing mostly as the condemned counterpart to marriage? What if the very notion of "ethical paradox" was an absurd oxymoron that never seems to end indeed? I ponder...  More importantly (Bertrand asks), why not think of marriage as a relationship based on equality, respect, and personal freedom? Could practicing truth, and trust, with humility and integrity, help reduce foul plays--including society’s reliance on femmes de joie for example? Well d'uh, heck yeah!   And if you're doubting the value of Bertrand's kind and wise questions, I bet you didn't you know marital r⭐︎pe was A-OK legal in almost ALL countries of the world until the mid-90s (!), for example...

ep_title: The Accordion of Ignorance EP X4
playlist_names_clean: BURLESQUEsutra, BLOWsutra
description: it's a moood  🪗🦆 #quack -- @bananasutra lyrics  In the heart of the streets, where truths fall apart, There’s an accordion tune, a discordant start. Where reason is quieted, shadowed and dimmed, And they dance to a beat that’s cruel and grim.  They sing of a man with words like a slap, With a mouth full of lies and hands that grab. Yet on and on, they cheer his charms, Blind to the rage in the world’s open arms.  Chorus Oh, the accordion plays, on loops it sways, To the tyranny of ignorance, our tragic malaise. It stutters and wheezes, no sense, no rhyme, As justice falters, as truth runs out of time.  They tell tales of valor, of victories grand, While rights are erased by his careless hand. With a sneer for the weak, he tears apart, All that we built with wisdom and heart.  And the tune, it shudders, sharp and vile, A cacophony cloaked in a foolish smile. They laugh as they stumble, entranced by his spin, Never seeing the rot that festers within.  Chorus Oh, the accordion plays, relentless and strong, The rhythm of ignorance, blind and wrong. A sad, twisted tune, syncopated lies, Where justice fails, and truth slowly dies.  And the world, it watches, hands thrown in despair, At a dance so absurd it’s beyond compare. As double standards keep time to the beat, A twisted march in the city’s street.  Verse 3 Where is the outrage, the furious cry? In a land where dreams now go to die. Innocence silenced, wisdom ignored, And ignorance crowned, shamelessly adored.  Oh, they sing of freedom, they sing of might, But dance in darkness, blinded by light. To the cruel tune, they happily sway, While dignity slips further away.  Chorus Yes, the accordion plays, to tyranny’s call, As ignorance rises and values fall. In syncopated shame, we watch it unfold, The tragic tune of hearts grown cold.  So here we stand, in a baffled trance, Dumbfounded by ignorance’s strange dance. As it winds and unwinds in a hopeless refrain, The world laughs along, numbed by the pain.

track_title: The Tyranny of Ignorance : BANJOsutra (Single Duck Release)
playlist_names_clean: JAZZsutra (Best Of), QUACKsutra : FOTUS Circus, QUACKsutra : DUCK (shady), FOTUS CIRCUS Playlist An American Freaks Show, JAZZsutra, BANJOsutra, SINGLEsutra Exclusive SoundCloud (woo), QUACKsutra where we sing FU, BLOWsutra
tags: duck, News & Politics, chill, banjo, true story, Folk & Singer-Songwriter, remake
description: I dunno about you, but(t) I sure am grateful for BANJOsutra Making American Fears Utopia, one song at a time (ha)... a special Single release for ya, while I finish roasting that big Mad Duck Circus of Americana album, oh la la :) --  They say the loudest wins the crowd, With hollow words and faces proud, Where lies dance like marionettes, While truth’s forgotten, lost in debts.  Promises slip like sand through a sieve, They teach us to take, forget how to give. Greed in the throne, with a smile of stone, And virtue’s left wandering, out on her own.  It’s the tyranny of ignorance, ruling with charm, Blindfolds and sirens that sound the alarm. In a world that’s lost its way, truth gets silenced, The echoes of wisdom drowned out by violence.  They preach of power, of winning the race, But is it victory or a hollow disgrace? Deception wears the crown, parades as the prize, While empathy fades under jaded skies.  Education abandoned, critical thought left behind, Empty slogans are the currency of the blind. For those who see, it’s a mournful sight, Watching darkness dress itself as light.  [Chorus] It’s the tyranny of ignorance, dressed to impress, Pulling the strings in a tangle of mess. Where the wise grow weary and the brave hold tight, Clinging to truth in the gathering night.  But there’s a spark, a whisper, a call to be bold, To dig for wisdom, to seek what’s untold. A heart that questions, a mind that sees, Can cut through the lies, can break the disease.  In the shadows they hide, those who still know, That the power of kindness is what makes us grow. They’re quiet but fierce, with eyes that are clear, And their ripple is stronger than what we fear.  It’s the end of the tyranny, it crumbles to dust, When wisdom and courage reclaim their trust. For all who remember what’s truly right, The dawn breaks softly, restoring the light.  A(nother) Brel-infused Lyricsutra™️ song remake, based on "L'accordéon de la vie" <3  +++ Bonus fun fact: the meme of the duck playing the accordion also does deserve credit for my inspiration, and if you haven't seen it, you should totally #quack it, or whatever hehe

description: “Everybody is genius. But if you judge a fish by its ability to climb a tree, it will live its whole life believing it is stupid.”—Albert Einstein   One thing I believe is that children hold more genius than we let them be! This song is a thank you to Albert, and also a love song for ‘em kids—kinda like a lullaby I would sing to my child, if I had one… because growing up in a world gone bananas sure ain’t easy!  Also, fun nerd fact: Math never came easy to me, but I always felt it was a form of language that can help explain things words cannot, kinda like poetry… and—it just recently recently occurred to me— my favorite humanists are all genius mathematicians 🥸 there’s Albert, whose wisdom of the heart was just as great as his earthly physics contributions, and then, there’s Blaise (Pascal), and Bertrand (Russel). I’ll be praying they form a post-punk band in heaven called “my dead genius boyfriends” 🤘  — Genius, you see, If you judge a fish by climbing trees, It won’t be free, It’s true, it’s true, so don’t you doubt your mind, You’re one of a kind, And I hope you find, Your worth inside.  In life, we all see, That there’s a way we’re meant to be, But don’t agree, With the rules they set for you, ‘cause you’re, More than they know, Just let it show, You’ll find your glow.  (Chorus) Don’t feel small, don’t feel small, don’t feel small, You’ve got it all inside, Your wings just need to fly. They’ll see it too, see it too, see it too, Once you believe it’s true, That genius lives in you.  They’ll try to say, You should fit into their way, But don’t obey, You’ve got gifts they cannot see, and so, Let yourself shine, Don’t stay behind, You’ll change their mind.  (Chorus) Don’t feel small, don’t feel small, don’t feel small, You’ve got it all inside, Your wings just need to fly. They’ll see it too, see it too, see it too, Once you believe it’s true, That genius lives in you.  Genius, you see, If you judge a fish by climbing trees, It won’t be free, But you’re meant to be, just as you are, Shine like a star, You’ll go so far, ‘Cause you’re a work of art.

description: This one happened really fast, with Morissey—I mean, the song, start to finish, it’s inspired from #Some girls are bigger than others”, I like the light sense of double entendre, it’s like a subtle dirty banana joke (lol) 🍌❤️‍🔥  [Intro / Chorus] Some truths are harder to swallow, Some truths are harder to swallow, When lies dig holes in tomorrows, Trolling low like cheap rerun shows.  [Verse 1] History plays like broken records, Mad old myths on thrones of discord, Frail petty stories we’re taught to defend, Stale tales of facts people like to bend.  [Verse 2] We’re tied to tricks, sugared illusion, Sweet-spoken chains of confusion, Truth tastes too sharp on dulled out tongues, As crooks howl along their harrowed songs.  [Pre-Chorus] Some truths are harder to swallow, Some truths are harder to swallow, The longer the lies, the deeper we follow, Down echo roads where hopes lie hollow.  [Chorus] Some truths are harder to swallow, Some truths are harder to swallow, When lies grow roots in tomorrows, Digging graves with faith gone hollow.  [Verse 3] Time keeps receipts in unspoken winks, Proof of deceit that refused to blink, Some lies go down like honeyed wine, As truths burn slow like sacred swines.  [Bridge] We give pride crowns to charming winners, Let blind kings rule saints and sinners, But mirrors ache when we speak their name, As toxic tremors rig the game.  [Break - soft, intimate] It isn’t fair… Hopes still matter. It ain’t weakness… Truth is progress.  [Final Chorus] Some truths are harder to swallow, Some truths are harder to swallow, When lies drown my trust in tomorrows, Sealing fates hollowed by ego bros…  [Outro] But I’d rather choke on honest air, Than swallow seas that sink what’s fair, Or breathe ‘em lies like chosen prayers… Blessed be rivers of brave thinkers.
